author: cjchanh
body:
## What
Recalibrate the Fleet Watch swap-pressure and launch-pressure gates so swap-percentage refuses GPU/worker launches only when **real memory is also pressured** — fixing false-blocks on big-RAM hosts while preserving and hardening fail-closed behavior.

## Why
On a 128GB host, `fleet guard` refused a legitimate 38GB MLX load because swap was 81% used (> the 80% policy) — even though 93GB of GPU budget and ~76GB of RAM were free. swap-% on a small, proactively-used dynamic swapfile (3.3GB of a 4GB pool) is a thrashing *proxy*; it should not veto launches when memory is genuinely healthy.

## Change
- Both gates (`check_swap_pressure`, `launch_pressure_blockers`) now require memory corroboration before swap-based refusal: **available RAM < 8GB floor OR pressure ≥ 80% ceiling** (the ceiling is shared by both gates). The direct memory-pressure check (`MEMORY_PRESSURE_HIGH`) is unchanged; the swap-% warning stays advisory.
- **Fail-closed preserved and hardened** (surfaced by craft-gate review): missing OR invalid (negative) telemetry ⇒ treated as pressured; the `vm_stat`-failure path now returns an unavailable `MemoryState` instead of fabricating all-RAM-free; `_get_total_memory_mb` never raises (the guard always returns a decision, never propagates an exception).
- Schema-additive (`mem_available_mb` / `mem_pressure_pct` / `mem_pressured` added to the verdict; reason/audit strings carry the corroboration data) — no key renames, so `~/.claude/hooks/fleet_guard_hook.py` is unaffected.

## Verification
- **339 tests pass** — new ALLOW (big-RAM), DENY (low-RAM / high-pressure), and fail-closed (missing / invalid / malformed telemetry, tiny-pool) cases.
- Live `fleet guard --gpu 38000 --port 8100` → `allowed: true` on a 128GB host; genuine pressure still blocks (proven by tests).
- Reviewed via two isolated craft-gate passes; all S1 findings (fail-open telemetry seams, uncaught exception, 75-vs-80 threshold divergence) fixed.

## Follow-up (non-blocking)
- Extract a shared `_is_memory_pressured(memory, floor, ceiling)` helper to de-duplicate the corroboration predicate across the two modules (the ceiling is already unified, so the duplication is currently harmless).

## Note
Base is `feat/session-ledger` because this branch is built on it (shares a `test_cli.py` edit). Retarget to `main` once session-ledger lands, or rebase on request.

author: copilot
body:
Adds CSS animations to enhance visual feedback during game load and exercise progression. Provides visual rhythm on page load, immediate feedback during exercises, and urgency cues when time pressure increases.

## Changes

**CSS Animations** (`src/index.css`)
- Added 7 keyframe animations: `slideInUp`, `fadeInScale`, `fadeIn`, `bounce-in`, `timer-pulse`, and supporting utilities
- All animations use GPU-accelerated transforms (opacity/scale) for consistent 60fps performance

**Component Animation Classes** (`src/App.tsx`)
- **Page Load**: Header and sections slide up with staggered delays (0–500ms) to guide attention
- **Exercise Cards**: Cascade in with progressive delays
- **Live Workout**: Section fades in with scale effect; exercise content (title, prompt, inputs) fade in sequentially with 0.1–0.2s delays
- **Timer Feedback**: Timer pulses when ≤10 seconds remain; progress bar shifts from cyan to red under time pressure
- **Feedback Messages**: Bounce animation on submission to celebrate/encourage

## Example
```jsx
// Before: static sections
<section className="rounded-3xl border border-white/10 bg-white/5 p-5">

// After: entrance animation with stagger
<section className="animate-slide-in-up rounded-3xl border border-white/10 bg-white/5 p-5" 
  style={{ animationDelay: '0.2s' }}>
```

Animations are purely CSS-based with no runtime overhead or new dependencies.

body:
Follow-up fix to the CustomerOrders screen shipped in JAS-53.

`CustomerOrders.test.tsx`'s fetch router matched on exact path equality (`pathOf(url) === "/customer-orders"`), so it broke whenever `VITE_API_BASE_URL` adds a prefix. A local `.env.local` of `/api` makes `api()` call `/api/customer-orders` → no route matched → 18 data tests timed out. CI and fresh clones don't have `.env.local` (gitignored), so BASE was `""` and the suite passed there — masking the issue (and why it slipped through the per-PR gate).

## Fix
Switch the route predicates to **suffix matching** (`endsWith` / anchored regex) — consistent with the other screen tests — and extract the order id via `split("/").pop()`. Test-only change.

## Verified
- With `.env.local` (`VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api`) present: CustomerOrders **19/19** (was 18 failed), full suite **89/89**.
- Lint + build clean. Diff gate is a no-op (test-only, no instrumented lines).

Fixes JAS-53

author: kennythecoder22
body:
### Motivation
- Teen Kitsu runs were suppressing fallback when the primary Kitsu query returned raw API rows but produced zero final Teen-safe survivors, causing underfill; Adult Kitsu behavior must remain unchanged.
- The goal is to make the router treat a Teen primary with raw-but-no-final-survivors as an underfill and allow a Teen-only continuation Kitsu query before falling back to broad terminal queries.

### Description
- Added Teen diagnostics and counters: `kitsuTeenPrimaryRawCount`, `kitsuTeenPrimaryFinalSurvivorCount`, `kitsuTeenFallbackSuppressedBecauseRawOnly`, `kitsuTeenFallbackContinuedBecauseNoFinalSurvivors`, `kitsuTeenFallbackContinuationQueries`, `kitsuTeenFinalKitsuSurvivorTitles`, and preserved `kitsuTeenUnderfillReason` for reporting.
- Changed fallback decision logic so a Teen primary that has raw API rows but zero final/adapter survivors is considered an underfill (sets `kitsuTeenFallbackShouldHaveContinued`) and can trigger one Teen-only continuation fetch instead of suppressing fallback because `raw > 0`.
- Allowed the Teen-only continuation to bypass the single-query fetch cap in a controlled way (the continuation is tracked via `isTeenContinuationFallbackAttempt` and recorded in `kitsuTeenFallbackContinuationQueries`) while leaving Adult Kitsu caps/behaviors intact.
- Collected final Teen-backed Kitsu survivor titles after assembly into `kitsuTeenFinalKitsuSurvivorTitles` and surfaced the new diagnostics in the router debug payload.
- Removed duplicate diagnostic keys previously present in the router return object to avoid repetition.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` to verify there were no whitespace/merge artifacts; this passed.
- Ran type checks with `npm run typecheck` / `npx tsc --noEmit`; these still report existing, repo-wide TypeScript errors unrelated to this change (type errors in other modules and missing external types), so the failures are not introduced by this PR.
- Ran `npx eslint screens/recommenders/recommenderRouter.ts`; lint output shows pre-existing warnings/errors in the large router file but no new linting failures attributable to the change.
- Verified the modified logic compiles locally within the change region (addressed an interim missing identifier during edits) and added diagnostic fields are present in the router debug payload; automated repo-wide checks remain green only for pre-change validations and continue to show legacy issues unrelated to the Teen Kitsu fallback fix.

author: weizhoublue
body:
…h action

 
/kind bug
 

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

## Trigger Scenario
Every official release image build triggered by ci-release.yaml (tag push or GitHub release published) flows through ci-build-images.yaml → docker-build-and-pushaction. Neither the release workflow nor the dev workflow passes commit-sha to the action, and the action never passed BUILD_REF as a Docker build arg at all.

## Fault Behavior
All officially published EPP and sidecar images are built with:

 CommitSHA = "unknown"
 BuildRef  = ""

These values are embedded at compile time via -ldflags and cannot be changed at runtime. Every release image carries wrong version metadata permanently.

## Expected Behavior
The Go codebase explicitly consumes both values in three production paths:
 - Startup log: cmd/epp/runner/runner.go, cmd/pd-sidecar/main.go
 - Prometheus info metric: metrics.RecordInferenceExtensionInfo()
 - OpenTelemetry tracing: semconv.ServiceVersionKey, attribute "commit-sha"

The Dockerfiles (Dockerfile.epp, Dockerfile.sidecar) already declare ARG COMMIT_SHA and ARG BUILD_REF and inject them via -ldflags. The local make image-build-epppath correctly passes both. CI should produce identical metadata.

author: generald
body:
![type](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-feat-blue) ![breaking](https://img.shields.io/badge/breaking-no-green) ![scope](https://img.shields.io/badge/scope-render-blue) ![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-added-green) ![status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-live%20verification%20pending-yellow)

Closes #3.

Replaces the placeholder `render()` with a live minimap of the **active tab**, feeding the live `PaneManifest` into the already-complete, unit-tested `src/minimap.rs`.

## What changed

Two small, pure modules bridge zellij's application state to the frozen renderer — the renderer itself is untouched:

- **`src/projection.rs`** (input adapter) — `TabInfo`/`PaneInfo` → `minimap::PaneRect`. `active_tab()` finds the tab zellij marks active; `project()` drops `is_plugin || is_floating || is_suppressed` panes (tab-bar / status-bar / overlays) and maps `pane_x/y/columns/rows/title/is_focused` onto the rect.
- **`src/paint.rs`** (output adapter, dependency-free) — `framed()` reframes the renderer's `\n`-separated rows into per-row cursor-positioned (`\u{1b}[{n};1H`) + end-of-line-cleared (`\u{1b}[0K`) output, so a shrinking 3-row block leaves no bleed (design §4.6, the load-bearing gotcha). `inactive_hints()` / `positioned_hints()` give non-active tabs a minimal `⌘N` placeholder.
- **`src/lib.rs`** — `render()` is now thin glue: pick the active tab, project its panes, clamp the width budget at the render site (`active_width.clamp(16, 28)`; the parser stays unclamped per #2), paint 3 rows. Repaint already fires on `TabUpdate` / `PaneUpdate`.

## Out of scope (separate issues)

- Theme/color source (`ModeInfo.style`) — colors are still index-derived.
- Full multi-tab packing with width budgeting and `+N` overflow (`src/line.rs`) — #4. Non-active tabs render minimally here, by design.

## Verification

**Automated (green):**

- 34 native tests pass (`cargo test --lib --target aarch64-apple-darwin`) — projection geometry (2-col / 2-row split offsets preserved, chrome filtered) and paint framing (per-row positioning, EOL clear, no trailing newline, row cap).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (host) and `cargo clippy --release --target wasm32-wasip1 -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1` succeeds.

**Live gate (pending — required before merge):** the Done-when items that need a real session — minimap updates *immediately* on split/close, a 2-col split shows two side-by-side bands, chrome stays filtered, no bleed on shrink — are verified by loading the `.wasm` into a pane (`zellij action start-or-reload-plugin`), granting `ReadApplicationState` on-screen, and reading the projected rects back via the `eprintln!` → `zellij.log` oracle established in #1. This needs an attended session + permission grant + one visual glance.

## Stacked PR

Based on `feat/2-config-stabilize-bar` (#11), not `main`, since #3 builds on #2's config + load wiring. Merge #11 first, then this retargets to `main`.

`feat/existing-vs-developed-compare` 브랜치의 26개 커밋을 main 으로 병합합니다. 핵심은 **기존설계 패턴 학습(P3j)** 전체 구현 + 정밀셀 sparse 확장 + 뷰어 워크플로 재설계입니다.

## 주요 변경

### 기존설계 패턴 학습 (pgvector, P3j)
- **L1** — pgvector 학습 저장소(`db/schema/route_stub_pattern.sql`: `feat vector(24)`·`dir_unit vector(3)`·HNSW + 집계뷰) + Python 학습 파이프라인(`routing3d_py/{route_db,pattern_learn,pattern_db}.py`). 405표본/38키, pytest 9/9.
- **L2a** — 학습면 PoC 투영(`Model/PatternStore.cs` + `SceneViewModel.LiftPocToSurface`). project6 c100: 185→187, 23.6s→6.4s.
- **전처리** — 접근불가(파묻힌) PoC→최근접 자유셀 스냅. 187→194.
- **L2b** — 기존설계 회랑 소프트바이어스(옵트인): C ABI `r3d_set_corridor_cells` + corridor 키 `long long` 확장. 194→198.

### 엔진 — 정밀셀 sparse 확장 (3.11)
- `ImplicitOccupancy`(복셀화 폐기·64비트 키·온디맨드 클리어런스) + 격자>5M셀 자동 전환. ctest `implicit` 추가, Dense==Implicit 전수 일치(골든 바이트 불변).

### 뷰어 워크플로
- 라우팅 진행 다이얼로그(그룹/유틸·시작/종단 PoC·엔진 단계 진행율 + 3D 라이브 갱신), 자동설계 삭제, 충돌확장 항상 ON, 덕트 관통 해결(PoC 표면 투영 + 가중 A*).

## 검증
- C++ ctest 10/10 · Python pytest 203 + 패턴 9/9
- 실데이터: project6 c100 (208작업) baseline 185 → 최종 **198/208**, 3자(Python=C++=C#) 일치

## 불변식
- 엔진 골든 불변(회랑은 `w_corridor>0` 일 때만 동작) — 회귀 0.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## 추가 작업 (이 세션, 동일 브랜치에 적재)

### L2b 속도 튜닝 — `perf(viewer)`
회랑(L2b) 페널티의 비용장을 admissible 휴리스틱이 과소평가하던 게 병목. weighted A* `w_heur` 1.5→2.0 + weighted 임계 5M→300k셀:
- **회랑 ON: 47s → 6.2s (약 7.6× 단축)**, 성공 198→199
- 회랑 OFF baseline 도 부수적으로 194→199 (혼잡 배관 2건이 탐색상한 내 해결)
- 엔진 무변경(뷰어 파라미터 튜닝). 골든 정확도(ctest) 무관.

### L3 패턴학습 — `feat(pattern)`
- **L3a 랙 번들링**: 유틸그룹 수평 런 z-높이(파이프 랙)를 학습해 엔진 `rack_levels`(면제 z-셀)로 같은 그룹 배관을 공용 랙에 번들. 도메인 신호 입증(Gas 83%@z12200·Exhaust 97%@z13400 등). **project6 c100 199→200, 랙 z-집중도 17.3%→21.4%, totalLen↓**. 랙 페널티 cell×0.2(회랑 0.5보다 부드럽게). Python 학습(`learn_rack_levels`+`--rack-report`) · C# 런타임(`BuildRackLevels`) · UI 토글 · 진단 env `R3D_RACK`+집중도 지표.
- **L3b 검색증강 ANN**: pgvector HNSW K-NN 거리가중 투표 추론 프리미티브 `suggest_stub`/`StubSuggestion`(집계뷰 키별 단일 mode 대신 PoC 컨텍스트별 ANN). DB 통합 테스트로 실 DB 검증.

**검증**: pytest 243 통과(패턴 12 = 순수 9 + DB 3). 엔진(C++) 무변경 — 순수 뷰어/Python.

author: fraserdrops
body:
Fixes all 4 module boundary violations in the `notifications` module and enforces it.
| Violation | Strategy |
|---|---|
| `NotificationOwner` → `feature/admin` (UserPicker) ×2 | **Move UserPicker into `common/components/`** — generic user-selection component used by both admin tools and notifications; only depends on shared code. |
| `CreateOrEditQuestionAlertModal` → `feature/query_builder` (`getQuestion`, `getVisualizationSettings`, `updateUrl`) ×2 | **Invert via props/callbacks** — see below. |

The alert modal decoupling:
- Deleted the unused `CreateOrEditQuestionAlertModalWithQuestion` wrapper (the only reader of `getQuestion`; no production usages).
- `visualizationSettings` becomes an optional prop. The QB host passes its computed settings (preserving unsaved-changes behavior for goal detection); other hosts fall back to the question's saved settings, which `getAlertType` already supports.
- The post-save `updateUrl` dispatch moves to the QB host (`QueryModals`) via the existing `onAlertCreated`/`onAlertUpdated` callbacks, replacing the `skipUrlUpdate` flag. Non-QB hosts (admin, metrics, SDK) no longer dispatch a QB URL action they never needed.

body:
## Summary

Drops 3 now-stale `@ts-expect-error` directives from `plugin-worker-manager.test.ts`. Slice-10 added them as a workaround when the SDK's `dist/protocol.d.ts` didn't yet declare `actorContext` on `PerformActionParams`. The SDK source has shipped that field since (`actorContext?: PluginPerformActionActorContext | null` at `packages/plugins/sdk/src/protocol.ts:416`), and once dist is fresh the static type matches the test literal. Each directive is now an unused suppression — TypeScript reports them as `TS2578`.

## Verification

```bash
# rebuild SDK dist first (clears any local staleness)
pnpm --filter @paperclipai/plugin-sdk build

cd server
cat > tsconfig.tests-included.json <<'JSON'
{ "extends": "./tsconfig.json", "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true },
  "include": ["src", "src/__tests__"], "exclude": [] }
JSON
npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.tests-included.json
# → 0 errors in plugin-worker-manager.test.ts (was 3 TS2578)
rm tsconfig.tests-included.json

npx vitest run src/__tests__/plugin-worker-manager.test.ts
# → 19/19 passing
```

## Worth knowing for next time

The 3 `TS2578` errors **only surface once SDK dist is fresh**. Devs running `npx tsc --noEmit` directly against a stale `packages/plugins/sdk/dist/` report a different (larger) error set — production-looking errors that are actually stale-dist artifacts, not real drift.

The pnpm-script flow (`pnpm typecheck`) is safe: `server`'s typecheck invokes `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/plugin-sdk ensure-build-deps` which rebuilds the SDK + shared when stale. CI runs through this path. Bypass it (raw `tsc`, LSP without a freshness hook) and you can chase ghosts. Worth a separate PR to wire `ensure-build-deps` into the vitest preflight or a pre-commit hook so the LSP-style harness can't drift.

## Slice chain

| Slice | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 3-12 | merged | ✓ |
| 13 | #265 | ✓ |
| 14 | #266 | ✓ |
| **15** | **this PR** | **review** |

After this lands, the only remaining test-included tsc errors are the 6 structural TS6059 across `packages/plugins/sdk/` and `packages/shared/` — a separate cleanup needing composite project references or a `rootDir` relaxation.

body:
mod-107 of the Chief AI Officer track. AI security from the CAO perspective — not engineering depth, but program-level fluency. Pairs with `ai-infra-security-learning` which carries the engineering-depth treatment.

## Contents
- `README.md` — module index
- `lecture-notes.md` — 6 sections, ~100 min. §1 threat landscape (real vs hype), §2 attack taxonomies (MITRE ATLAS, OWASP LLM Top 10, NIST AI 100-2 E2023), §3 defense-in-depth (9 layers), §4 red-teaming as governance practice, §5 the CAO × CISO boundary (mirror of mod-104 §5 CAO × MRM), §6 AI incident classification
- `exercises/` — 5 exercises, 16 hours total. Uses Tessera Bank's agentic agent (continuation from mod-106) plus Sentinel Mutual, Northfield Mutual, Halverston Capital for variety.
- `quiz.md` — 20 questions
- `resources.md` — annotated, framework-first

## Framework anchors
MITRE ATLAS, OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025), NIST AI 100-2 E2023, NIST SP 800-39, EU AI Act Arts 15 + 73, NYDFS Part 500 §500.17.

## Review notes
- No auto-merge.
- §1.1 vs §1.2 (real vs hype threat categorisation) takes a position on what's documented vs theoretical. Read for whether it lands as informed prioritisation or as dismissive of emerging threats.
- §5 (CAO × CISO boundary) deliberately mirrors mod-104 §5 structure. Read for whether the parallel reads as principled or as formulaic.
- Exercise 03 (boundary dispute) introduces a *split-authorship* resolution. Read for whether the steel-manning of the CISO position is fair.
- Exercise 02 (red-team design) explicitly prohibits real customer harm in the rules of engagement. Read for whether the constraint balance is right.

## Summary

Phase 2 execution of WP-195 — the analysis-layer companion to WP-194's setup-matrix sweep runner. Engine pure helper + operator CLI; read-only over the manifest; no second execution path.

Closes the deferral WP-194 left open. Phase 1 SPEC landed in #176; this PR completes the implementation and flips the governance ledger.

## Commits

- **EC-222: implement sweep manifest anomaly oracle** (`9384305`) — the implementation. 4 files: `sweep.analyze.ts` (15 locked exports), `sweep.analyze.test.ts` (38 tests; EC required ≥12), `analyze-sweep-manifest.mjs` (CLI), `complete-game-tests.md` (reference doc).
- **SPEC: governance close for WP-195 / EC-222** (`08ad237`) — flips D-19501..D-19507 from Proposed to Landed (Active); WP-195 row `[ ]` → `[x]`; EC-222 row Draft → Done; STATUS.md narrative.

## What changes

`packages/game-engine/src/simulation/sweep.analyze.ts` exports EXACTLY 15 symbols per the EC-222 lock:

- **Functions (3):** `parseManifestLine`, `classifyCell`, `classifyManifestRecords`
- **Const (1):** `SWEEP_ANOMALY_CLASSES` — `['endgame-reached', 'not-endgame', 'escaped-villain-cap', 'fatal']`, drift-pinned to the `SweepAnomalyClass` union
- **Types/interfaces (11):** `SweepAnomalyClass`, `ParsedSuccessRecord`, `ParsedFatalRecord`, `ParsedManifestRecord`, `ClassifiedCell`, `NumericDistributionStats`, `FatalErrorBucket`, `MalformedLine`, `ManifestSummary`, `ManifestClassification`, `ParseRecordResult`

`scripts/analyze-sweep-manifest.mjs` — locked CLI shape `--manifest <path> [--format markdown|json]`; markdown default; duplicate-flag last-wins; flag-without-value full-sentence stderr + exit non-zero.

## Load-bearing locks (all honored)

- **D-19501** — exact-set parse contract on enumerable own-properties; plain-object precondition (`typeof === 'object' && !== null && !Array.isArray && Object.getPrototypeOf === Object.prototype`) runs FIRST so arrays / `null` / primitives / non-`Object.prototype` objects yield precondition-specific `malformedReason`.
- **D-19502** — closed 4-class anomaly taxonomy; `'not-endgame'` merges cap-hit + stuck-game (manifest lacks `turnsElapsed`); fatal `errorSignature` = first 80 UTF-16 code units VERBATIM (no normalization, no hashing).
- **D-19503** — `MAX_TURNS_PER_GAME = 200` local copy with `// why:` citing D-19503; drift-pinned to `simulation.runner.ts:54` via source-reading test (mirrors `par.aggregator.ts:450` precedent). `ESCAPE_LIMIT` imported from `endgame/endgame.types.ts`.
- **D-19504** — `--format markdown|json` with markdown default; both deterministic.
- **D-19505** — malformed lines non-fatal; warn-and-continue with ascending `lineNumber` synchronous stderr emission.
- **D-19506** — v1 two-axis lock (mirrors WP-194 MVP scope).
- **D-19507** — script named `analyze-sweep-manifest.mjs` (verb-noun-noun mirroring `record-game-fixture.mjs`).

Other locked invariants honored end-to-end: Unicode code-unit comparator (NOT `localeCompare`) for JSON deep-sort + `cellSeeds` sort + fatal-signature secondary sort; stdout byte-stream contract (UTF-8 / single trailing `\n` / no BOM); sum accumulation honors input-array iteration order (no Kahan, no reordering); `mean`/`median` average full-precision FIRST then round to 2 decimals; `p95` nearest-rank `Math.ceil(0.95 * count) - 1`; `fatalErrorSignatures` v1 retention = FULL (markdown preview top 3, JSON carries all); cell-count invariant `sum(anomalyCounts) === totalCells === sum(winnerCounts)` enforced by construction.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @legendary-arena/game-engine build` exits 0

# Docker Compose

## Serviços

| Serviço | Porta | O que é |
|---|---|---|
| `app` | 8000 | FastAPI (API principal) |
| `db` | — | PostgreSQL 16 |
| `minio` | 9000 / 9001 | Storage S3-compatível (substitui AWS em dev) |
| `minio-init` | — | Cria o bucket automaticamente (roda e termina) |
| `pgadmin` | 5050 | Interface web para o banco de dados |
| `jenkins` | 8080 | CI/CD |

---

## Como rodar

**Primeira vez (ou após mudanças no código):**
```bash
docker compose up --build
```

**Demais vezes:**
```bash
docker compose up
```

**Parar tudo:**
```bash
docker compose down
```

**Parar e remover volumes (reset completo):**
```bash
docker compose down -v
```

---

## Acessos

| Interface | URL | Login |
|---|---|---|
| API / Swagger | http://localhost:8000/docs | — |
| MinIO Console | http://localhost:9001 | `minioadmin` / `minioadmin123` |
| pgAdmin | http://localhost:5050 | `admin@blog.com` / `admin` |
| Jenkins | http://localhost:8080 | (configurado no primeiro acesso) |

---

## Variáveis de ambiente

Não é necessário `.env` para rodar — todos os valores têm defaults no compose. Para sobrescrever (ex.: produção), crie um `.env` baseado no `.env.example`:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Variáveis disponíveis:

| Variável | Default no compose | Descrição |
|---|---|---|
| `POSTGRES_DB` | `blogdb` | Nome do banco |
| `POSTGRES_USER` | `bloguser` | Usuário do banco |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `blogpass` | Senha do banco |
| `SECRET_KEY` | `change-me-in-production` | Chave JWT |
| `ALGORITHM` | `HS256` | Algoritmo JWT |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES` | `30` | TTL do token |
| `MINIO_ROOT_USER` | `minioadmin` | Usuário MinIO / AWS Access Key |
| `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `minioadmin123` | Senha MinIO / AWS Secret Key |
| `BUCKET_NAME` | `blog-bucket` | Nome do bucket S3 |
| `REGION_NAME` | `us-east-1` | Região AWS |
| `PGADMIN_EMAIL` | `admin@blog.com` | Email de acesso ao pgAdmin |
| `PGADMIN_PASSWORD` | `admin` | Senha de acesso ao pgAdmin |

author: quakewang
body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to SeaTunnel! Please make sure that your code changes
are covered with tests. And in case of new features or big changes
remember to adjust the documentation.

Feel free to ping committers for the review!

## Contribution Checklist
  - Make sure that the pull request corresponds to a [GITHUB issue](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/issues).
  - Name the pull request in the form "[Feature] [component] Title of the pull request", where *Feature* can be replaced by `Hotfix`, `Bug`, etc.
  - Minor fixes should be named following this pattern: `[hotfix] [docs] Fix typo in README.md doc`.
-->

### Purpose of this pull request

<!-- Describe the purpose of this pull request. For example: This pull request adds checkstyle plugin.-->

Fix Paimon sink branch handling in save mode and schema evolution.

Previously, Paimon save mode DDL was executed against the main table before the writer switched to the configured branch. This could make `schema_save_mode=RECREATE_SCHEMA` drop/recreate the main table, `data_save_mode=DROP_DATA` truncate the main table, or branch auto-create scenarios accidentally create a main table.

Schema evolution also used a non-branch Paimon `Identifier`, so alter table events were applied to the main table while the writer wrote to the branch.

This PR rejects unsupported non-main branch save mode paths before DDL execution and applies schema evolution with a branch-aware `Identifier`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

<!--
Note that it means *any* user-facing change including all aspects such as the documentation fix.
If yes, please clarify the previous behavior and the change this PR proposes - provide the console output, description and/or an example to show the behavior difference if possible.
If possible, please also clarify if this is a user-facing change compared to the released SeaTunnel versions or within the unreleased branches such as dev.
If no, write 'No'.
If you are adding/modifying connector documents, please follow our new specifications: https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/issues/4544.
-->

Yes.

For Paimon sink non-main branches, the main table and target branch must already exist. `schema_save_mode=RECREATE_SCHEMA` and `data_save_mode=DROP_DATA` are rejected for non-main branches to avoid modifying the main table.

The Paimon sink documentation is updated with this constraint.

### How was this patch tested?

<!--
If tests were added, say they were added here. Please make sure to add some test cases that check the changes thoroughly including negative and positive cases if possible.
If it was tested in a way different from regular unit tests, please clarify how you tested step by step, ideally copy and paste-able, so that other reviewers can test and check, and descendants can verify in the future.
If tests were not added, please describe why they were not added and/or why it was difficult to add.
If you are adding E2E test cases, maybe refer to https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/blob/dev/seatunnel-e2e/seatunnel-connector-v2-e2e/connector-cdc-mysql-e2e/src/test/resources/mysqlcdc_to_mysql.conf, here is a good example.
-->


Added `PaimonBranchSaveModeHandlerTest` to cover:
- missing main table does not auto-create a main table for branch writes
- missing branch fails without auto-creating the branch
- `data_save_mode=DROP_DATA` does not truncate/drop branch metadata
- `schema_save_mode=RECREATE_SCHEMA` does not drop/recreate the main table
- restore save mode path rejects destructive branch save mode
- schema evolution alters only the target branch schema

Verified with:

```bash
./mvnw spotless:check -pl seatunnel-connectors-v2/connector-paimon
./mvnw -pl seatunnel-connectors-v2/connector-paimon -Dtest=PaimonBranchSaveModeHandlerTest test
./mvnw spotless:apply -pl seatunnel-connectors-v2/connector-paimon
./mvnw -q -DskipTests verify
```

### Check list

* [ ] If any new Jar binary package adding in your PR, please add License Notice according
  [New License Guide](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/blob/dev/docs/en/developer/new-license.md)
* [x] If necessary, please update the documentation to describe the new feature. https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/tree/dev/docs
* [ ] If necessary, please update `incompatible-changes.md` to describe the incompatibility caused by this PR.
* [ ] If you are contributing the connector code, please check that the following files are updated:
  1. Update [plugin-mapping.properties](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/blob/dev/plugin-mapping.properties) and add new connector information in it
  2. Update the pom file of [seatunnel-dist](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/blob/dev/seatunnel-dist/pom.xml)
  3. Add ci label in [label-scope-conf](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/blob/dev/.github/workflows/labeler/label-scope-conf.yml)
  4. Add e2e testcase in [seatunnel-e2e](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/tree/dev/seatunnel-e2e/seatunnel-connector-v2-e2e/)
  5. Update connector [plugin_config](https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/blob/dev/config/plugin_config)

the existing docs. Part of the Summer-Hydro documentation push — this is the

link to instead of carrying their own troubleshooting sections.

A plain-language tour aimed at operators and new engineers:
- **Platform-agnostic framing** — Ben, DriX, and the EchoBoat family share the
  autonomy layer; `cmd_vel`/helm is the framework boundary, and ArduPilot/MAVROS
  is only *BizzyBoat's* low-level backend (Ben/DriX use their own).

author: weicao
body:
## Summary

Fix Galera cluster deadlock after KubeBlocks Stop/Start operation.

- **Bug**: `podManagementPolicy=Parallel` terminates all Galera nodes simultaneously. No node gets `safe_to_bootstrap=1` in `grastate.dat`, so on restart all nodes try to join but no primary component exists → CrashLoop deadlock.
- **Fix**: Add crash recovery path (c) to `should_bootstrap()` in `galera-start.sh`:
  - `_any_peer_alive()` — TCP probe port 3306 on peer FQDNs to distinguish full-cluster-restart from single-pod-restart (split-brain safety)
  - `_wsrep_recover_and_bootstrap()` — run `mariadbd --wsrep-recover` to validate InnoDB consistency, then mark `safe_to_bootstrap=1`
  - When pod-0 has `safe_to_bootstrap=0` AND no peer alive → recover → bootstrap
- **Split-brain safe**: if any peer has port 3306 open, pod-0 joins instead of bootstrapping
- Chart version bump: alpha.117 → alpha.118 (script-only change via ConfigMap, no CmpD spec mutation)

## Evidence

alpha.117 galera T6 Stop/Start failure: all 3 nodes `safe_to_bootstrap=0 seqno=-1`, `NON_PRIM`, `failed to reach primary view`, cluster Failed/CrashLoop. Evidence sha256 `d9c6f97ed926ba479e6fac681fbefa52b319d939d81c30d704938b9c923dc633`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Helm template render: galera ConfigMap includes new `_any_peer_alive` + `_wsrep_recover_and_bootstrap` functions
- [ ] Standalone / replication topologies render clean (no galera script leakage)
- [ ] Deploy alpha.118 to vcluster, run galera T6 Stop/Start — expect cluster recovery instead of CrashLoop
- [ ] Verify T1-T5 + CM1-CM4 still PASS (no regression)
- [ ] Verify single-pod crash scenario: kill pod-0 while pod-1/pod-2 running → pod-0 should join (not bootstrap)

author: alexbazeley
body:
## What

Add `git pull --rebase origin main` before `git push` in both the `consolidate` and `committees_refresh` push steps of the monthly FEC refresh.

## Why

The June 1 monthly run (the first since the cron was re-enabled in #18) failed. Root cause was **branch protection** requiring the `test` status check, which the non-admin `github-actions[bot]` can't satisfy on a direct push (`GH006 Protected branch update failed`). That's been resolved separately by dropping the required-status-check from `main`'s protection (force-push / deletion protection retained).

On re-run, the push then failed `non-fast-forward (fetch first)` because re-running an older run checks out the original (June 1) commit SHA while newer commits had since landed on `main`. The real monthly cron checks out the live tip so it wouldn't hit *that* exact case — but the same class of failure (a manual push racing the cron) is real and silent. This makes both push steps resilient.

The refresh only stages data files (`master.db`, `data.json`, owner YAMLs, provenance log), so a rebase over unrelated code/brief commits replays cleanly.

## Verification

- LFS commit/push path itself is confirmed working from the June 1 run logs (`Uploading LFS objects: 100% (1/1), 130 MB | 35 MB/s, done.`).
- CI (`test`) runs on this PR.

## What
Three contained, layout-only fixes from a dashboard UI style audit (totoday request). No copy changes, no logic changes — pure Tailwind/className.

## Fixes
**① Timeline reading width (the big one).** Message body had no max-width → prose tracked the full content column (**~1028px / ~140ch** at 1440), fighting the editorial reading surface (KB content is already capped, reads ~620px). author: genesiscz
body:
## Summary

Adds `tools tz` — a natural-language timezone converter. Parses a time+zone expression with `chrono-node` and converts across IANA zones using only `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (no extra timezone dependency).

Supported forms:

- `tz '3pm PST in Prague'` — explicit zone, explicit target
- `tz 'now in Tokyo'` — reference-anchored instant, single target
- `tz '2026-06-02 09:00 Europe/Prague to America/New_York'` — wall-clock + explicit source zone + target
- `tz '3pm PST'` — no target, falls back to default zone set (Local, UTC, New York, London, Prague, Tokyo)
- `--to a,b,c` to override targets; `--json` for structured output

## Design

- `lib/zones.ts` — alias map (PST/EST/CET/Prague/Tokyo/...) + raw IANA validation via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` round-trip. Pure.
- `lib/convert.ts` — `zoneOffsetMinutes`, `epochFromWallClockInZone` (two-pass DST-correct), `renderZone`, `convert`, `formatZoneLine`. The conversion/formatting core takes a fixed epoch in and never reads the system clock.
- `lib/parse.ts` — splits the expression, then three branches: (a) chrono-certain offset (uses chrono's epoch, also covers `now`/relative), (b) date-only fallback, (c) wall-clock interpreted in the source/local zone.
- `index.ts` — commander entrypoint; injects `Date.now()` and the resolved local zone, keeping the pure core clock-free.

## Verification

- `bunx biome check src/tz` → exit 0 (clean, no fixes needed)
- `bun test src/tz` → 21 pass / 0 fail, 49 assertions. Hermetic and deterministic (current time injected as `nowMs`, no network/clock/clipboard).
- `./tools tz --help` → exit 0; real conversions smoke-tested (3pm PST → 23:00Z → Prague 01:00 CEST verified).

## Notes

Low-priority salvage of pre-written code. Draft for review. No follow-up known to be required; the alias map is intentionally small and can be extended later.

author: rrhester
body:
Fixes the "No eligible open shifts in the first week" toast after Smart Fill.

### Two fixes
1. **Open-shift query was too narrow.** It required `status = "scheduled"`, but the codebase's own Smart Fill treats a shift as open whenever `driver_id IS NULL` and the status isn't terminal — freshly-generated open shifts can carry another status and were silently missed. Now matches that: `driver_id IS NULL` and `status NOT IN (completed, no_show, called_off, cancelled)`.
2. **Anchored to the first week that has openings.** Previously it only looked at the first-available *calendar* week; a mid-week or future first-available date (or a sparse first week) came up empty. It now finds the earliest eligible open shift and runs the engine for that shift's week. The empty message is also clearer ("the week may be fully staffed or not built yet…").

### Heads-up (likely root cause for you)
Your schedule showed **114% coverage** (over-staffed), which usually means **no open/unassigned shifts exist** — Smart Fill assigns the new hire to *existing* open shifts, so with none open there's nothing to place even after this fix. See my chat note: I can make Smart Fill **generate** shifts for the new hire when the board is full, if that's the behavior you want.

No migration. `dashboard/live.js`.

author: gaborage
body:
## Phase D — make the migrate CLI `go install`-able

Final phase of the release-mechanism work. Makes `go install github.com/gaborage/go-bricks/tools/migration/cmd/go-bricks-migrate@vX.Y.Z` work and report the right version. (Titled `build(migrate):` so it doesn't trigger a framework release — the CLI has its own `tools/migration/vX.Y.Z` tag stream.)

### Changes
- **Drop the `replace` directive** from `tools/migration/go.mod` and pin `require go-bricks v0.38.0` (a real published version). A `replace` directive makes a module impossible to `go install @version`; removing it is the unblock. Verified: `GOWORK=off go -C tools/migration build ./...` builds against the **published** framework, not `../../`.
- **Add a root `go.work`** (allowlisted in `.gitignore`) so local dev still resolves the framework from the working tree. `go.work` is **not** consulted by `go install pkg@version`, so committing it is safe.
- **`main.go` reports the real version on `go install`** via `runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo()` — ldflags only fire during `make build` in a git tree, so a module-cache build otherwise reported `"dev"`. TDD'd (`resolveVersion`, 6 table cases).
- **Scope the CLI's `git describe`** to `--match 'tools/migration/v*'` (strip the prefix) so the CLI version reflects its own tag, not the framework's. Document `go install` in the README.

### Verification
`GOWORK=off` build (published framework) ✅ · workspace dev build ✅ · `TestResolveVersion` 6/6 ✅ · gofmt/vet clean · `replace` count 0 · `require` = v0.38.0.

### Follow-up (immediately after merge)
A `tools/migration/v0.38.0` submodule tag will be cut (the CLI's first release tag) so `@v0.38.0` / `@latest` resolve. The tag-protection ruleset covers `tools/migration/v*` (admin-bypass), same as framework tags.

## What

Applies Emil Kowalski's design-engineering principles across the whole static site, plus a small clean-URL fix.

All 5 pages share ~80% identical inline CSS, so instead of editing each 5×, the polish lives in a shared **`polish.css`** + **`polish.js`**, linked after each page's inline `<style>` so it overrides the existing transitions by source order. ## Changes

**Design polish (`polish.css` / `polish.js`)**
- Custom easing tokens (`--ease-out` / `--ease-in-out` / `--ease-drawer`) — replaces weak browser defaults
- `scale(0.97)` `:active` press feedback on every button / CTA / card-link
- Card hover lifts, crew-photo + masonry zoom, project-link arrow nudge (via `transform`, not animating `gap`)
- Hover effects gated behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so taps don't get stuck states

Driven with headless Chromium (puppeteer-core → `/usr/bin/chromium`), not just by reading CSS:

### Motivation
- Provide a freestanding, deterministic vector-field kernel for the RMR engine implemented in fixed-point Q16.16 math with no heap/libm/libc calls on the hot path and bounded loops for safe integration into low-level pipelines. 
- Expose a small public API and stable smoke signature to enable regression checks and host/Android consumers while explicitly flagging the Attractor #22 VOID paradox instead of silently patching it. 
- Integrate the kernel into the canonical RMR core manifest and CI selftest targets so it is exercised by existing host test suites.

### Description
- Added public header `engine/rmr/include/rmr_vector_field.h` defining Q16 constants, opcodes (`0x60..0x6F`), flags (failsafe/rollback/watchdog/VOID22) and the `RmR_VectorFieldState` API. 
- Implemented the freestanding kernel in `engine/rmr/src/rmr_vector_field.c` with integer-only Q16 arithmetic, bitmask selection, CRC-like mixing, deterministic mapping (number → mod42 → arc → chord → h=√3/2·chord → toroid node), contraction loop, watchdog/rollback and bytecode interpreter. 
- Added host selftest `demo_cli/src/rmr_vector_field_selftest.c` which validates index mapping, bytecode flow, contraction math, watchdog/VOID safeguards and the stable smoke signature. 
- Registered the new source in `engine/rmr/sources_rmr_core.cmake` and wired the selftest into `CMakeLists.txt` so the test runs under the existing `run_selftest` target.

author: barnickelus
body:
## Fixes the shredded/spiky white Victorian frames

**Cause:** The textured GLB stored `POSITION` **interleaved** with `NORMAL` + `TEXCOORD_0` in a single vertex buffer (stride 8 floats). But the runtime stretch in `addVictorianMesh` reads `geo.attributes.position.array` as a tightly-packed `[x,y,z, x,y,z, …]` array and indexes `base[i*3]`. With interleaving, `base[i*3]` lands in the middle of the neighboring normal/UV data — so it stretched **garbage positions** into NaN spikes, producing the white shattered-glass frames in the screenshot.

(The previous fix corrected the overall *scale*; this one corrects the *buffer layout* — both had to be right.)

**Fix:** Rebuilt the asset with `VertexLayout.SEPARATE`, so each attribute gets its own tightly-packed bufferView. Now `position.array[i*3] === getX(i)`, exactly what the runtime expects (and how the original `victorian-frame.glb` was laid out).

## Verification
Replicated the **exact** `addVictorianMesh` stretch math on the new asset:
- **0 NaN** vertices across square / wide / tall paintings (was producing spikes).
- Sane sizes: 0.61×0.61 m art → 0.80×1.18 m frame; constant border, opening scales with art.
- `position.array[i*3]` matches `getX(i)` for every sampled vertex (de-interleaved).
- Clean render with intact tracery — no spikes, no explosion.

Same 2.28 MB, float positions in 8-unit space, textures optimized.

body:
## Problem

The session detail view renders tool calls as a flat timestamp-ordered list with no grouping by execution turn. A "turn" is a set of tool invocations within 500ms of each other — the natural unit of agent reasoning. Tool invocations must be attributable by turn before they can be auditable.

## Approach

**`lib/turn-cluster.ts`** — pure utility, no React:
- `clusterByTurn(tools: ToolCall[], windowMs = 500): TurnGroup[]`
- Iterates the sorted input in order (precondition documented; does not re-sort)
- New turn when gap between consecutive `startedAt` values *exceeds* `windowMs` (strict `>`)
- 1-based `turnIndex`; preserves input order within each group

**`components/session/TurnGroup.tsx`** — client component:
- Renders a "Step N — X tools" header chip as a real `<button aria-expanded>` (keyboard-accessible)
- Groups ≥ 3 tools: collapsed by default (`aria-expanded="false"`)
- Groups < 3 tools: expanded by default (`aria-expanded="true"`)
- Clicking toggles expanded state; children only mount when expanded
- Optional `renderTool` prop for custom row rendering

**Architecture note:** No existing session-detail page or `/api/sessions/:id/tools` endpoint exists in daax-web (backend changes are out of scope per issue). Both units are built ready-to-mount. Decision logged: no speculative backend work added.

author: philluiz2323
body:
Closes #227.

## Problem
`buildObservedPullRequestScenarios` (local-branch.ts) classifies each open PR by checking `isStaleOpenPr` (no update in >=14 days) BEFORE `isBlockedOpenPr` (changes requested / bad mergeable state). The two predicates are independent, so a PR that is both changes-requested AND >=14 days old is counted as `stale`.

That inverts the authoritative classifier `classifyOpenPullRequest` (pending-pr-scenarios.ts:193-200), which checks blocked BEFORE stale. The two buckets are used asymmetrically downstream: `observedStalePrCount` is subtracted from open-PR pressure in the `afterStalePrsClose` and `bestReasonableCase` scenarios (preview.ts:355/372/389), while `observedBlockedPrCount` is only a note (preview.ts:466). So a changes-requested PR (blocked on the author) gets optimistically modeled as `stale, likely to close and free up a slot`, which can flip `openPrMultiplier` 0->1 and inflate the projected score.

## Fix
Reorder the classification in `buildObservedPullRequestScenarios` so `isBlockedOpenPr` is checked before `isStaleOpenPr`, matching `classifyOpenPullRequest`. A PR that is both blocked and stale now counts as blocked (open-PR pressure stays) instead of stale (subtracted). PRs that are only stale or only blocked are unaffected.

## Tests
Strengthened the existing observed-scenario test with a PR that is both `CHANGES_REQUESTED` and stale (updatedAt 2020). It must now count as blocked (`blocked: 2`, `stale: 1`) and the `afterStalePrsClose` projection must keep `openPrCount: 5`, not subtract it. With the old stale-first order this PR landed in `stale` (`blocked: 1`, `stale: 2`, `openPrCount: 4`), so the test is a genuine fail-on-revert.

`vitest run` local-branch + pending-pr-scenarios + scoring 59/59; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: friedenberg
body:
Registers a `git`-scheme capture/diff backend under the FDR 0005
plugin registry, following the yt-dlp plugin's exec-a-tool +
freshness-probe template.

Capture resolves the branch tip via `git ls-remote`, clones the
single branch bare, and stores a self-contained `git bundle` (full
history) plus a one-line `ref.txt` tip-commit sidecar as ordinary
content-addressed blobs. Diff uses the cheap `ref.txt` as a freshness
key: a tip match re-emits receipt entries verbatim (no re-clone), a
miss re-clones+bundles for fresh blob-ids. Restore is deferred — the
bundle is a regular file the filesystem plugin materializes.

Accepts `git:<remote>[#branch]` and `git://host/path[#branch]`;
defaults to the remote's HEAD branch when no fragment is given;
refuses remotes/branches beginning with `-` to block flag injection.

Includes FDR 0006, a package CLAUDE.md, and a hermetic test suite
backed by a fake `git` shim.

author: aayush-engineer
body:
## Description

When a browser agent (configured with `@mastra/agent-browser`) stores a `system-reminder` message with `role: "signal"`, navigating to that agent page in Studio caused a React render crash:

**Root cause:** `@assistant-ui/react` only accepts `"user" | "assistant" | "system"` roles. When a stored thread contains a `role: "signal"` message (e.g. a browser context reminder with the current URL), it hit the unknown-role error path and crashed the entire page. The only workaround was manually deleting the thread from the database.

**Fix:** Filter out `role: "signal"` messages before they reach `toAssistantUIMessage`. These are internal browser-context markers and should never be rendered in the chat UI. The filter is applied to both loaded (`initialMessages`) and streamed messages since both flow through the same `messages` state.

**Before:** Any browser agent thread with a stored `system-reminder` message caused a blank "Something went wrong" crash on page load.  
**After:** The agent page loads correctly and existing threads remain fully usable.

## Related issue(s)

Fixes #17414

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Checklist

- [x] I have linked the related issue(s) in the description above
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (if applicable)
- [x] I have addressed all Coderabbit comments on this PR

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## ELI5

When the chat interface loads old conversations from browser agents, some messages are stored in a special internal format that the chat display library doesn't understand. This PR filters out those special internal messages before showing them, so the app doesn't crash when you try to view these conversations.

---

## Changes

### Changeset: `fix-studio-crash-signal-role.md`
Added changeset documenting a patch release for `@mastra/playground-ui` that fixes the Studio crash when loading browser agent threads with `system-reminder` messages.

### Code Fix: `packages/playground/src/services/mastra-runtime-provider.tsx`
Updated the message filtering logic in `MastraRuntimeProvider` to exclude messages with `role: "signal"` (in addition to the existing filter for messages with `metadata.status: 'error'`) before they are processed and passed to the Assistant UI renderer. This prevents validation errors in `@assistant-ui/react`, which only accepts `"user"`, `"assistant"`, or `"system"` roles.

---

## Impact

**Before:** Loading a browser agent thread containing stored `system-reminder` messages with `role: "signal"` caused Studio to crash with the error "Something went wrong" (or "System messages must have exactly one text message part"), requiring manual thread deletion from the database.

**After:** Browser agent threads load successfully. Internal `signal`-role messages (which represent browser context metadata rather than actual chat messages) are silently filtered out and do not appear in the chat UI, preventing the crash while preserving the thread.

---

## Related Issue
Fixes `#17414`

author: nwparker
body:
## Summary
- Normalize braille OSC-title spinner frames to one semantic working-title frame.
- Suppress duplicate normalized terminal title callbacks before they mutate high-fanout renderer state.
- Reset the duplicate-title guard on transport disconnect.

Supersedes closed, unmerged PR #4428 with the same scoped fix rebased onto current `main`.

## Profiling / Data
- Fresh live process sample on the packaged app showed renderer PID `54595` at ~37% CPU and ~888 MB RSS (`/Applications/Orca.app`, version 1.4.38).
- macOS `sample 54595 5` showed the hot renderer work under JS timer/microtask execution, not daemon or GPU work.
- Fresh daemon socket profile showed large retained terminal state: packaged `daemon-v11` has 47 live sessions and packaged `daemon-v10` has 10 live sessions. Those sessions create many OSC-title sources that can fan into renderer store updates.
- Prior focused repro for this path: Pi/Codex-style braille spinner OSC frames can arrive about every 80ms; without this guard each frame emits `onTitleChange`, which wakes `updateTabTitle`, Zustand subscribers, runtime graph sync keys, mobile session publication, and tab/status UI even when only the spinner glyph changed.
- New deterministic test proves four raw spinner frames in one PTY chunk now emit exactly one normalized title callback.

## Regression Risk
- User-visible tab status should remain correct because the first working title still emits immediately.
- Raw titles are still passed to the agent tracker on emitted title changes; only duplicate normalized title callbacks are suppressed.
- Non-spinner title changes still emit normally.
- Disconnect resets the cached title, so a reattached/recreated transport can emit its first title again.
- Risk: if an agent encodes meaningful state only in changing braille glyphs while the normalized semantic title is unchanged, that per-frame glyph animation no longer reaches tab-title observers. That is intentional for CPU reduction; semantic working/idle state remains preserved.

## Verification
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/pty-transport-pi-coalesce.test.ts src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/pty-dispatcher-pi-routing.test.ts src/renderer/src/lib/agent-status.test.ts`

phase_script.append({
    "months": n,
    "phase": str(r["phase"]),
    "monthly_nav_change_pct": float(r["monthly_nav_change_pct"]),  # ← 只有這 3 個

缺任一環節都會出現「看起來改了實際沒改」的鬼狀態 — v18.286 中 Bug 1 + Bug 2 兩個都缺。

**Stacked on #115** — review/merge that first. The diff against #115's branch is small (1 commit, +695/-25 lines).

## Summary

Adds browser-based **bucket / access-key / cluster admin + S3 object browse + drag-and-drop upload** to the Garage stack, gated by **Authentik SSO via native OIDC**. Operators (and end-users) get a single SSO-protected URL instead of having to SSH to the NAS and run `garage` CLI commands.

Two structural pieces:
1. **Bump Garage v1.1.0 → v2.3.0** — required by garage-ui's `/v2/` admin API. Migration is in-place per upstream docs (data + layout compatible; only the deprecated `replication_mode` key drops — we already use `replication_factor`). Cluster is fresh (0 buckets, 0 keys, 0 data) so blast radius is essentially zero.
2. **New `garage-ui` workload + 2 new role subcommands** — `render-ui-config` writes the UI's `config.yaml` with embedded OIDC + admin_token + persistent Ed25519 JWT key (sessions survive restarts); `deploy-ui` runs `docker compose up -d` on drift. Spec-driven via a new `ui:` block in `spec/e4e-nas/garage.yml`; opt-in by block presence. UI-only tag `garage_ui` for targeted applies.

## UI choice

Surveyed three:

| | Noooste/garage-ui (chosen) | khairul169/garage-webui | Deuxfleurs/garage-webadmin (official) |
|---|---|---|---|
| OIDC native | ✅ explicit Authentik | ❌ basic-auth only | unknown |
| Maturity | v0.6.1 (2026-05-31) | v1.1.0 (Sep 2025) | "do not use yet" |
| File browse + upload | ✅ drag-and-drop | ✅ | unclear |

Chose Noooste because it's the only one that natively speaks OIDC — using khairul169 would require deploying a Traefik + Authentik forward-auth outpost (the very thing we ruled out for blast-radius reasons). Migration to the official `garage-webadmin` is tracked as a follow-up issue for when it leaves "do not use" status; bucket/key spec is declarative, so the swap is "redeploy + re-apply role."

author: westkevin12
body:
#### **Overview**

This Pull Request closes #1 , successfully fulfilling the micro-architectural advancements outlined in the subsystem roadmap:

1. **AVX-512 SIMD Vector Generation**: Upgraded the Python-based assembly code generator to emit explicit AVX-512 instructions, utilizing wide vector registers (`%zmm` variants) for 16-way concurrent doubleword processing in the locality-aligned matrix kernels.

2. **Intelligent Hardware Dispatch**: Reinforced the C timing harness with a compiler-level CPUID checking sweep to dynamically dispatch between native AVX-512 assembly and an optimized contiguous C fallback.

3. **Physical NUMA Allocation and Pinning**: Enhanced the Go concurrent scheduler daemon with direct memory-mapped buffer allocations (using page prefaulting via `MAP_POPULATE`) and invoked the Linux kernel `mbind` system call to pin buffers to physical sockets.

4. **Dynamic Telemetry & Quality Gates**: Integrated real-time dynamic Shields.io badges parsed directly from timing logs and refactored method structures to satisfy strict static analysis Cognitive Complexity limits.



---



### **Detailed Subsystem Implementation Notes**



#### **1. The Locality Subsystem: AVX-512 Vectorization & Safe CPUID Dispatch**

* **Vector Assembly Generator (`orchid/assembler.py`)**:

  * Advanced the `emit_locality` generator to output high-performance AVX-512 instructions.

  * In the inner loop `j`, 16 dense 32-bit integer elements of `B[k][j]` are loaded via `vmovdqu32` directly into vector register `%zmm1`.

  * The scalar constant `A[i][k]` is broadcasted to all 16 channels of `%zmm0` via `vpbroadcastd`.

  * Multiplies and accumulates doublewords concurrently: `%zmm1 = %zmm1 * %zmm0` (`vpmulld`), loaded into `%zmm2` from `C[i][j]` (`vmovdqu32`), accumulated (`vpaddd`), and written back to memory, incrementing the linear forward stride `j` by `16` elements per iteration.

* **Safe Runtime Capability Check (`locality/fair_harness.c`)**:

  * Integrated a native compiler-level CPUID check `has_avx512f()` utilizing `<cpuid.h>` to detect hardware features.

  * Built an optimized contiguous `I-K-J` fallback kernel `matmul_locality_fallback` in C.

  * Deployed a dynamic function pointer dispatch at runtime. On machines supporting AVX-512 foundation, it executes raw assembly; on machines without it (e.g. typical virtual machines and local laptops), it gracefully fallbacks to the C kernel, **guaranteeing 100% stable builds and completely eliminating `SIGILL` (Illegal Instruction) crashes.**



#### **2. The Parallel Subsystem: Physical NUMA Binding & Complexity Reduction**

* **Memory Prefaulting & Socket Binding (`scheduler/scheduler.go`)**:

  * Integrated anonymous page-aligned virtual allocations using `syscall.Mmap` with the `MAP_POPULATE` flag (value `0x8000`), forcing the host kernel to pre-fault page tables, completely neutralizing runtime page-fault scheduling latency.

  * Triggered the Linux native `mbind` system call (SYS_MBIND trap `237` on x86_64) using `syscall.Syscall6` to bind target virtual address ranges to distinct physical NUMA sockets via bitmask mapping.

  * Built robust fallback tolerances: if the target physical node is offline (e.g. `EINVAL` on single-socket hardware), if running in un-privileged containers (`EPERM`), or on virtual hypervisors (`ENOSYS`), it logs a warning, keeps the mapped pages active, and fallbacks gracefully.

  * Added `TestPhysicalNUMAAllocation` inside [scheduler_test.go](file:///home/west/github.com/westkevin12/RAMNET/ORCHID/scheduler/scheduler_test.go) to verify mapping boundaries, sizing, and direct memory writes.



#### **3. Developer Tooling: Dynamic Shields.io Telemetry Badges**

* **Dynamic Endpoint Pipeline (`orchid/aggregator.py`)**:

  * The statistical aggregator now outputs a flat JSON file at `evidence/reproduced/speedups.json` containing live calculated statistics on every execution loop.

* **Dynamic Badges (`README.md`)**:

  * Added badge strings with dynamic query links pointing to the raw JSON file hosted on GitHub:

  * Whenever timings are recalculated and pushed, the README badges dynamically update on the fly!

* **Workspace Isolation (`.gitignore`)**:

  * Configured a high-precision unignore filter to block all raw log files and benchmark dumps inside `evidence/` except the single telemetry endpoint file `speedups.json`:


---



### **Reproduced Architectural Verification Data**



Executing `make test` runs the entire build, assembly compilation, dynamic dispatch harness, and concurrent scheduler unit tests, showing **100% green passing results**:



#### **Locality Cache-Line Saturation Benchmarks**

*(Evaluated at matrix size $N=512$, alternating loops to eliminate persistent cache warm bias, and flushing 64 MiB L1–L3 cache lines between iterations)*



* **Minimum Speedup Achieved**: **`3.893x`** (previously `2.230x` baseline)

* **Median Speedup Achieved**: **`3.929x`** (previously `2.303x` baseline)

* **Maximum Speedup Achieved**: **`4.156x`** (previously `2.502x` baseline)

* **Mean Speedup Achieved**: **`3.982x`** (previously `2.343x` baseline)



#### **Go Concurrent Bank Scheduler Simulation**

* **Deterministic Serial Cycles**: `4,925,668` (Baseline)

* **Deterministic Parallel Cycles**: `1,666,401`

* **Go Parallel Speedup Efficiency**: **`2.956x`** (highly aligned to the absolute theoretical $3.0\times$ physical limit across three banking channels).



---



### **Verification Checklist**

* [x] Python assembly emitter generates correct AVX-512 packed doubleword instructions (`vpbroadcastd`, `vmovdqu32`, `vpmulld`, `vpaddd`) and linear leaps.

* [x] Dynamic CPUID check `has_avx512f` safely routes non-AVX-512 host environments to the C-based fallback.

* [x] Go scheduler locks, mmaps, and binds simulated memory channels to host NUMA physical nodes.

* [x] README is fully fed by dynamic Shields.io JSON badges.

* [x] `make test` passes successfully in Go and C pipelines.

Two ordering bugs in the per-agent Secret writer:

author: nursedude
body:
## Summary

Phase 1B of the Windows-first roadmap: a **Windows-native keep-alive** for the Reticulum stack. MeshForge's watchdog assumes `systemd --user`, which doesn't exist on Windows — so this rebuilds keep-alive on **Task Scheduler**: a logon-triggered task with **restart-on-failure**, no admin required (runs in the user's interactive session at `RunLevel Limited`).

## What changed (`pwsh/services.ps1`)

- **`Enable-RnsdAutoStart`** upgraded from a plain logon task to a watchdog: `New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -RestartCount 3 -RestartInterval 1min`, no execution-time-limit, single-instance. It now also **offers to start the task immediately** so it can be tested without logging off.
- **New `Enable-MeshChatXAutoStart` / `Disable-MeshChatXAutoStart`** — same pattern for `meshchatx --headless` (web UI on `https://127.0.0.1:8000`).
- **New `Get-RnsAutoStartStatus`** — shows whether each keep-alive task is enabled + last run/result.
- Shared `$Script:RnsdTaskName` / `$Script:MeshChatXTaskName` constants.
- **Services menu**: new MeshChatX auto-start entries + status view; header now shows keep-alive state.
- **`Stop rnsd`** now honestly warns when keep-alive is active (the task will restart the daemon; disable auto-start first to keep it stopped).

## Design notes

- **No admin / no stored credentials** — `LogonType Interactive`, `RunLevel Limited`.
- Restart-on-failure means an intentional stop won't stick while auto-start is enabled — surfaced explicitly in the Stop path and the status view.
- A console window may briefly appear for the logon task; the Phase 3 tray supervisor will supersede this. Tracked as a known cosmetic item.

## Tests

`services.tests.ps1`: function count 10→13, constant-refactor assertions, restart-on-failure + start-now checks, new Describe blocks for the 3 new functions, menu wiring + renamed section.

## Verification

Local: lint clean, smoke 103, ShellCheck clean, brace-balanced, no trailing-space-after-backtick. **PowerShell-Syntax + Pester validate in CI** (no local `pwsh` available).

The CUDA kernel for _embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_backward used AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF, which covers float, double, and float16 but not bfloat16. author: 7rikazhexde
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #483 addressing two requests:
1. Prevent recurrence of dependency/runtime mismatches in the example CI (#484)
2. Keep action usage examples pinned to the latest released version, as a versioning rule

## Changes

### CI log visibility (go / nodejs / ruby / rust test workflows)
Run example tests **directly** instead of `output="$(cmd)"; echo "$output"`. Under `set -e -o pipefail` a failing test aborted **before** the echo, hiding the failure output (this cost an extra CI round in #483). `output` was never consumed downstream.

### Dependabot policy (`.github/dependabot.yml`)
Example ecosystems (`npm` / `bundler` / `gomod` / `cargo`) are now **weekly** and **ignore major-version bumps**, because a major bump can raise a dependency's required language runtime above the example test matrix (e.g. `parallel 1.x → 2.1.0` needing Ruby >= 3.3). The shipped `pip` package and `github-actions` keep daily updates including majors.

### Usage version sync + rule
- Update every `uses: 7rikazhexde/json2vars-setter@vX.Y.Z` reference across README, docs and example workflows from `v1.0.2` → **`v1.0.4`** (they had lagged since 1.0.2).
- Automate it: new **Sync action version references** step in `update-version-and-release.yml` rewrites all references to the version being released and includes them in the bump commit.
- Document the rule in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Note on "a uv-like tool"
A Ruby equivalent of `uv` would **not** have prevented #482 — Ruby already has Bundler + `Gemfile.lock` and the lock worked. The root cause was the gap between the example's supported runtime range and a dependency's required runtime range, which these Dependabot/CI guardrails address directly.

Closes #484

author: andregoepel
body:
## Problem

The public landing page (`/`) rendered through the full Blazor Server interactive
pipeline. As a result, first paint waited on the SignalR circuit, and content was
hidden (`opacity:0`) until JS ran *after* the circuit connected — causing a slow,
flickering first render and weak Lighthouse scores.

## Change

Render `/` as **static SSR with no Blazor circuit**:

- **`App.razor`** branches on the route. For `/` it emits a lean document — font
  preload, marketing CSS only, an inline no-flash theme script, static `HeadOutlet`
  and `Routes`, and `site.js`. **No Radzen theme/JS, no `blazor.web.js`.** Every other
  route keeps the interactive-server pipeline unchanged.
- **`PortfolioLayout.razor`** is now pure static SSR — no `IJSRuntime`, no
  `OnAfterRenderAsync`, no event subscription. Resolves language server-side and loads
  only that language's content, once.
- **`SiteLanguage`** (new) resolves language with no client round-trip: `ag-lang`
  cookie → `Accept-Language` header, so the server renders the correct language on
  first paint.
- **`SiteHeader.razor`** toggles moved from Blazor `@onclick` to `data-*` attributes
  wired by vanilla JS; takes a `Lang` parameter for active state.
- **`site.js`** gains `boot()` (runs on load, wires toggles, runs `initAll`),
  client-side `setTheme` (localStorage, no reload) and cookie-based `setLang` (reload
  so the server re-renders the chosen language).
- **`ContentService`** is now `IMemoryCache`-backed (10 min, invalidated on save) to
  keep Postgres off the render path.
- **`app.css`** gates `.reveal { opacity:0 }` on `html.js`, so content is visible even
  with JS disabled/slow (no permanently-invisible hero).

## Results

Lighthouse on `/`: Performance **100**, Accessibility **100**. (SEO/Best-Practices
follow-ups — robots.txt, meta description — tracked separately.)

## Notes

- Switching language does a full page reload (cookie + `location.reload()`), since the
  page re-renders statically. Theme switching stays instant (no reload).
- `ErrorLayout` still uses the post-render JS-interop theme pattern (same flicker class,
  on error pages) and `SiteStateService` is now unused by the live flow — left as-is.

## Verification

- `dotnet build` — succeeds.
- `dotnet csharpier format` — applied.
- Tests — **94 passing** (Website 11, AppFoundation 17, Identity.Blazor 66).

author: h0lybyte
body:
## Summary

Hot-path optimization for the Lua mod. **No version bump** — still 0.2.0. No prototype changes.

### Before

| Loop | Cost per tick |
| --- | --- |
| Follow (1 Hz) | `find_entities_filtered{name = SPIDER_ALLY}` × every surface |
| Sprint (3 s) | `find_entities_filtered{name = {SPIDER, SPIDER_ALLY}}` × every surface |
| Nervous (15 s) | `find_entities_filtered{name = {SPIDER, SPIDER_ALLY}}` × every surface |

Cost scaled with surface count even on empty planets where nothing was happening.

### After

| Loop | Cost per tick |
| --- | --- |
| Follow (1 Hz) | Iterate `storage.allies` keys + `game.get_entity_by_unit_number` (O(1) in 2.0). Lazy player→surface bucket only when an ally has no recorded owner. |
| Sprint (3 s) | Compute "active surface set" from `game.connected_players` once, skip surfaces not in the set. |
| Nervous (15 s) | Same active-surface gate as sprint. |

Empty planets / dormant space platforms now cost a single hashmap lookup per loop firing instead of a full entity scan.

### Ally registry

`storage.allies[unit_number] = surface_index`

- Set on hatch (inside the existing 1 Hz hatch sweep, where the LuaEntity is already in hand).
- Cleared on death alongside `storage.ally_owners`.
- Bootstrapped via a one-shot `rebuild_ally_registry()` from `on_configuration_changed` when the field is missing — saves that predate the registry pick it up without manual intervention.
- Self-cleaning: the follow loop prunes stale entries on the fly if the entity disappears via a path other than `on_entity_died`.

### Internal consistency

This branch bundles the follow-tuning fixes from #11609 (REST_DIST_SQ=4, `by_damage` distraction, radius=2, 128-tile tracking, `allow_destroy_friendly_entities=false`) so the perf refactor isn't sitting on top of the broken follow code. The two PRs are mergeable in either order; whichever lands second is a no-op for those tunings.

## Test plan

- [x] `./kbve.sh -nx kbve-spider:test` → PASS.
- [x] `luac -p control.lua` → clean.
- [ ] CI re-runs `kbve-spider:test` clean.
- [ ] Manual: hatch ally, walk, ally trails (registry path).
- [ ] Manual: place 5 allies, run the game for 5 minutes, watch /show-time-usage — control.lua should idle at near-zero on the host because the follow loop only touches valid ally unit_numbers and the sprint/nervous loops skip the unpopulated surfaces.

author: amalc
body:
## What

Auto-routes deploy-class workflows to `tier: ondemand` at submit time, so no repo needs a per-pipeline `tier:` knob and none can drift onto spot. Resolves #266 (Option C).

## Why

The original Peregrine intent — deploy/promote/auto-tag run on ondemand *without anybody doing anything* — was never built as a mechanism. It got hand-applied as per-repo `tier: ondemand` YAML, which drifted: repos that forgot it (peregrine-messaging, peregrine-sentinel) routed release pipelines to spot and were clobbered by a mid-promote preemption.

This matters because the killed-workflow re-queue (`server/rpc/rpc.go`, #224/#225/#235) **deliberately won't restart a workflow that already did observable work** — so a spot preemption *during* a promote/deploy is fatal, not recoverable. `ondemand` (non-preemptible) is the correct lever for the deploy class.

## Changes

- **`pipeline/tier.go`** (new, 100% coverage):
  - `ShouldForceOndemand(name, isTag, patterns)` — pure classifier: true on a tag event, or when the workflow name contains a deploy pattern (case-insensitive substring, matching the scaler's `IsDeployPipeline`).
  - `DeployPatterns()` — reads `WOODPECKER_TIER_DEPLOY_PATTERNS` (comma-separated), default `deploy,promote,version-bump`. `sync-back` excluded (idempotent housekeeping, stays spot).
- **`server/pipeline/create.go`** — `rewritePipelineTier` runs **before** `validatePipelineLabels` (so the forced `ondemand` validates — and even repairs a deploy workflow that carried a dead tier) and before enqueue (so the rewritten `item.Labels` propagates into the task routing filter via `queue.go`'s `maps.Copy`). **Always overrides** an explicit label — a repo cannot route a release pipeline to spot, even by mistake. Skipped workflows untouched. `rewritePipelineTier` at 100%.

## Policy reconciliation

This is the precise/central mechanism the spot-default guardrail (**scaler#1175**, global CLAUDE.md tier table) always assumed — it replaces both the drift-prone per-repo knob *and* the over-provisioning blanket-ondemand reaction that prompted that guardrail. The global-rule table that lists `promote`/`version-bump` as spot describes the pre-classifier stopgap; a reconciliation issue is filed against `global-claude` (linked in #266).

## Acceptance (#266)

1. ✅ A `promote.yaml` with no `tier:` → ondemand automatically (name contains "promote").
2. ✅ A deploy-pattern workflow with explicit `tier: spot` → rewritten to ondemand (always-override, per decision).
3. → `CountTierMismatches` in scaler should trend to 0 once deployed (consumer-side observation).

## Tests

`pipeline/tier.go` table tests (tag-wins, substring/case, blank-pattern safety, env parse + default fallback, forced-value-is-a-known-tier). `rewritePipelineTier`: deploy-class forced, tag forces all, explicit-spot overridden, nil-map created, skipped untouched, forced-value validates.

Closes #266.

author: toastmanau
body:
## Summary

Adds a sibling to `docker/` for hosts where running Docker is overkill — SBCs (Pi, Orange Pi, NanoPi) and small bare-metal mini PCs serving a home LAN. Same `config.json5` source of truth, same `/rpc/{slug}` proxy pattern keeping upstream URLs out of the browser.

- **`caddy/generate-caddy-config.sh`** — mirrors `docker/10-config-from-json5.sh`. Reads `config.json5`, emits a `Caddyfile` and the redacted `config.public.json5`. Same validation (slug regex, required fields), same redacted output shape.
- **`caddy/install.sh`** — one-shot installer for Debian/Ubuntu: installs `caddy` + `jq` + `json5`, runs the generator, deploys `dist/` to `/var/www/explorer-lite`, validates, enables `caddy.service`, and runs four loopback smoke tests.
- **`caddy/README.md`** — when to use Caddy vs Docker, hardware sizing table, install + update flows, security model, troubleshooting.
- **`README.md`** — new Deployment section linking both paths.

## Why

The existing Docker deploy is great for servers already running Docker, but it asks for ~100 MB+ RAM (container + engine) plus image storage. A native Caddy install lands at ~50 MB RSS / ~44 MB disk and works comfortably on a Pi Zero 2 W. The Docker setup itself is untouched.

## Reference deploy

Tested on **Orange Pi 5+ 16 GB** (Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64). After warmup serving the testnet config:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Caddy RSS | 48–51 MB |
| CPU at rest | 0.1% |
| Disk (binary + webroot) | ~44 MB |
| Static asset latency (loopback) | 1.5–3.7 ms |
| Static bundle size | 706 KB (193 KB gzipped) |

## Design choices

- **No new dependencies on the codebase itself.** Pure shell + jq + json5 (same deps as the Docker entrypoint), invoked at install time on the host. The TypeScript app is untouched.
- **Generator over hand-written Caddyfile.** Single source of truth (`config.json5`) drives both nginx (Docker) and Caddy (native), so adding a network in one place propagates everywhere.
- **Intentional differences from Docker.** No built-in rate limiting (Caddy core lacks `limit_req`); no Cloudflare real-IP allowlist. README documents these explicitly — the native install targets LAN/private deployments. Public-internet operators should add `mholt/caddy-ratelimit` or front it with their own proxy.

## Test plan

- [x] `generate-caddy-config.sh` runs cleanly against `public/config.example.json5` (5 networks, 2 stats endpoints)
- [x] Generated Caddyfile passes `caddy validate` with zero warnings on Caddy 2.x
- [x] Generated `config.public.json5` is byte-for-byte equivalent in shape to what `docker/10-config-from-json5.sh` produces
- [x] End-to-end install on real hardware (OPi5+ aarch64, Ubuntu 24.04): browses correctly, RPC round-trips work, blocked paths return 404
- [ ] (reviewer) Try `install.sh` on a different SBC class (Pi 4 / Pi Zero 2 W) to confirm portability
- [ ] (reviewer) Try with a multi-network `config.json5` (mainnet + testnet)

author: battermanz
body:
## Summary

This PR merges `development` into `main` to cut **v1.0.0**, the first release of Docktornet — a Docker/Podman label-driven reconciliation engine for Nginx Proxy Manager, Cloudflare DNS, and Gatus.

It comprises **95 commits / 60 files / ~19,900 insertions**, representing the entire v1 build from empty workspace to a deployable, production-grade system.

## What Docktornet does

An **agent** runs on each Docker/Podman host, reads `docktornet.*` container labels, and pushes a snapshot to a central **server**. The server persists snapshots in SQLite and continuously **reconciles** external systems to match the desired state declared by labels:

- **Nginx Proxy Manager** — proxy hosts
- **Cloudflare** — DNS records
- **Gatus** — uptime monitor endpoint files (+ Telegram alerts)

## Highlights by area

### Core (`crates/core`)
- Typed `docktornet.*` label parser → `Snapshot`, `ContainerEntry`, `MachineId`, `service_id`
- NPM / Cloudflare DNS / Gatus integration label structs, with typo warnings

### Agent (`crates/agent`)
- Env-driven config; lists containers from both Docker and Podman sockets
- Builds snapshots filtered to `docktornet.*` labels
- Pushes to server with bounded exponential backoff + periodic poll loop
- Serves both runtimes from one agent via `group_add`

### Server (`crates/server`)
- SQLite (WAL) with migrations; bearer-token auth middleware
- `POST /api/v1/snapshot` ingest routed through the reconciler
- `/healthz` endpoint + SIGTERM graceful shutdown
- Periodic full-resync verify-and-repair loop
- Warns on a machine id arriving from multiple source IPs

### Reconciliation engine
- Derives intended services from snapshots; tracks external resources in DB
- Dry-run skeleton → live reconcile; diff and resync paths serialized via a shared mutex
- Idempotency hardening: skip writes already in sync, adopt existing NPM hosts on create conflict, prevent NPM overload from bulk reconciles

### Integrations
- **NPM**: proxy-host client, wildcard/cert-case matching, configurable forward host, sensible secure defaults (block exploits, websockets, HSTS subdomains)
- **Cloudflare**: DNS client + record reconciliation, get-by-id support
- **Gatus**: managed endpoint file lifecycle, Telegram alerts, group override, custom alert provider, clean endpoint names, optional `name` label

### Deploy & ops
- Rootless **distroless** Dockerfiles (agent + server) built via cargo-chef
- Compose files (main host, agent, smoke), deployment guide, v1 cutover runbook
- External-state backup script; smoke-test compose + fixtures
- v1.0.0 version bumps; private registry; `.env.example` annotated with required/optional + defaults

### Docs
- v1 design spec, implementation plans, README, full container-label reference

## Test plan
- Workspace builds; unit + end-to-end snapshot push tests included
- Smoke-test compose stack with data fixtures for local verification

body: **Owner QA finding #1** on the live `/onboarding/wedding` flow: the budget look-photo (and the pax + feel photos, same pattern) sat at the **top** of a tall figure with an empty gradient band below — the image wasn't filling the frame. ## Root cause The React port's `` renders an **id-less** ``, but the prototype CSS keyed the fill behavior on element **IDs** (`#budgetphotoimg`/`#paxphotoimg`/`#feelphotoimg {position:absolute;inset:0;object-fit:cover}`). Those id selectors never matched, so the image fell back to natural-aspect-at-100%-width and left the figure's gradient background showing below. welcome + picker were unaffected — their fill rules use the **tag selector** (`.welcomehero img` / `.pp-photo img`), which DO match `HeroImg`. ## Fix Add the same proven tag-selector fill rule for the three affected figures: ```css .pba .budgetphoto img,.pba .paxphoto img,.pba .feelphoto img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;opacity:0;transition:opacity .45s ease;} .pba .budgetphoto img.loaded,.pba .paxphoto img.loaded,.pba .feelphoto img.loaded{opacity:1;} ``` All three are `position:relative` with resolved heights, so absolute-inset-cover fills them. Pure CSS — `role`/`kind`/`faith` untouched (different layout). Build ✓ · rule confirmed in the compiled route CSS. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
