author: stuckj-claude-bot
body:
Closes #9.
Closes #10.

> **Auto-close note:** this PR is stacked on `cb-010-011-companion-config`. GitHub only fires `Closes` keywords when a PR merges into the default branch (`main`). Merge #72 first — GitHub retargets this PR's base to `main` — then merging this PR closes #9 and #10.

## Summary
Second half of the Phase 1 server core — the "client-facing" layer — **stacked on PR #72** (CB-010/011). Review/merge #72 first; this PR's diff is against that branch.

- **CB-012 — WebSocket API server** (`internal/api`)
  - `/ws`: `hello` → initial `state` snapshot → command/subscription handling, per `docs/protocol.md` v1. Multiple concurrent clients via a hub.
  - **Command routing** (`dispatch.go`): `camera` preset, `scene` set, `audio` set_mute, `streaming`/`recording` start·stop, `slides` next·prev — resolved against the config presets and actuated through the Companion client. `ack` is sent **before** any resulting `state-delta`; rejections become `nak`s with protocol §8 codes (`unknown_target`/`unknown_action`/`unknown_preset`/`unknown_channel`/`device_unavailable`/…).
  - `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` (topic-filtered deltas), `get_state` re-sync, `ping`/`pong`.
  - `/ws/meters` reserved for Phase 2 (CB-021) — accepts and holds connections now.
  - Per-client bounded send buffer (slow consumers are dropped and reconnect), server→client ping keepalive, graceful shutdown that closes all clients.
- **CB-013 — state aggregation** (`internal/state`)
  - Typed `State` mirroring `protocol.md` §4 (camera/obs/slides/stream/audio).
  - `Store` assigns a **monotonic rev** and computes **sparse JSON-Merge-Patch deltas**; broadcasts only on a real change.
  - Pluggable `Poller` + `Source`: refreshes background sources on a configurable interval (default ~1s) and applies them through the *same* Store path, so direct OSC (Phase 2) plugs in without reworking the broadcast machinery.

## Phase-1 milestone
This completes design §5's Phase-1 goal end-to-end: a client can connect and trigger Companion buttons for **scene switching, stream/recording start-stop, and camera presets**, routed through the server, with live state reflected back.

## Notable decisions (flagged for your review)
- **No state sources wired by default.** Companion's HTTP API has no button-state read endpoint (see #72), and real Companion *variable* names are deployment/module-version specific. Rather than bake in guesses, the poller ships with **zero sources** in Phase 1 — state is driven by the server's own command handlers (optimistic local state). The `Poller`/`Source`/`CompanionVarSource`-style plumbing is complete and tested with fakes, ready for known variables and Phase 2 OSC. *If you'd prefer I wire a configurable OBS-variable poll now, say the word.*
- **Subscription filtering vs. rev-gap detection.** `rev` is global/monotonic; deltas are filtered to each client's subscribed topics. A client on a *narrow* subscription can therefore skip revs and may trigger a `get_state` re-sync — a known sharp edge of the spec's gap rule under topic filtering. Most clients use the default all-topics subscription where it doesn't arise. Documented in `hub.go`; flagging in case you want different semantics.
- **Origin policy:** `/ws` and `/ws/meters` use coder/websocket’s default origin check (no `OriginPatterns`). Requests with no `Origin` header (the native client, including remote over Tailscale) and same-host browsers are allowed; cross-origin browser requests are rejected — the cross-site-WebSocket-hijacking defense for an API with no in-protocol auth in v1 (protocol.md §1). A cross-origin web client is intentionally unsupported in v1; a future web build gets an origin allowlist or the deferred token handshake.

## Verification
`go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` green. New tests: `api` integration tests over a **live** WebSocket (hello/state lifecycle, ack-before-delta ordering, naks, topic filtering, `get_state`, ping/pong, unknown-type ignore); `state` unit tests for rev/delta/snapshot/diff and poller change-detection/error-tolerance. Windows cross-build (`GOOS=windows`) passes; manual startup smoke binds `/ws` + `/ws/meters` (both return 426 to plain GETs, as expected). Race detector wasn't run locally (no cgo/gcc in this env) — CI uses plain `go test` too; the store/hub are mutex-guarded by design.

body:
Follow-up to #407. Verifying the live deployment after #407 merged: the device-plugin domain fix, image-tag fix, and open-webui removal all worked — but the LiteLLM Pod now reveals a **memory limit too low** for v1.86.2.

## Issue

With the corrected `v1.86.2` image, `litellm` pulls fine but crashloops with **OOMKilled (exit 137)** before it can emit any logs:

```
Reason: OOMKilled   Exit Code: 137   (x2 restarts, BackOff)
limits.memory: 1Gi
```

LiteLLM v1.86.x loads the full provider map + a Prisma engine and runs DB migrations at startup, exceeding 1Gi.

## Fix

- `limits.memory`: 1Gi → **2Gi**
- `requests.memory`: 256Mi → **512Mi** (so the scheduler reserves real headroom)

## Verification

- `scripts/render-validate.sh` → **EXIT=0**.
- Confirmed on the cluster that **#407's device fix worked**: the node now advertises `squat.io/tenstorrent: 1`, and `model-tt-llama` schedules onto `shion-ubuntu-2605` — its only remaining blocker is the intentional `REPLACE_*` placeholder image (`InvalidImageName`), exactly as designed. `open-webui` is gone.

After this merges, `litellm` should reach Ready; the only not-Ready workload left will be `model-tt-llama`, pending the Phase-2 host work + placeholder fill-in per `scalable-llm/README.md`.

author: huhuanming
body:
## Symptom

Android release builds intermittently fail with:

```
FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.
* What went wrong:
Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly (it may have been killed or may have crashed)
```

No stack trace, no JS heap-OOM message — silent `SIGKILL`, the signature of the kernel/cgroup OOM killer. Always dies at the same point: right after `Main graph built`, during `Building background graph...`.

## Why it's not a code regression

`x` daily builds alternate green/red with **no build/dep/script changes between them**:

| build | result |
|---|---|
| 68 | ✗ |
| 69 | ✓ |
| 70 | ✗ |
| 71 | ✗ |
| 73 | ✗ |

Green sandwiched between reds = a **marginal OOM**, not a single bad commit. The clean linear x-window (build 71→73) touches zero build/native/dependency files.

## Root cause

`scripts/unionBuild.js` holds the **main graph (~13.5k modules) and the background graph in memory at the same time** (both are required for the cross-graph segment-ownership computation). The build already runs on the EAS **`large`** class (32 GB) — forced via `--resource-class large` in `release-android.yml`, which overrides `eas.json`. But Metro's default `maxWorkers` scales with CPU:

```js
// metro-config/src/defaults/getMaxWorkers.js
maxWorkers = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(cores * (0.5 + 0.5*Math.exp(-cores*0.07)) - 1))
```

→ **6 transform-worker processes** on the 8-vCPU `large` machine. Node main + 6 workers + Gradle daemon + Kotlin daemon push peak RSS to the 32 GB ceiling, tipping over intermittently.

**Adding hardware can't fix it:** `large` is the EAS Android ceiling, and more vCPUs just spawn more workers. The only lever is reducing the dual-graph peak.

## Fix

Cap Metro to **2** transform workers during the union build (override via `UNION_BUILD_MAX_WORKERS`), gated to **EAS Android only** (`args.platform === 'android'` + `EAS_BUILD`/`EAS_BUILD_RUNNER`) so local and iOS bundling keep full parallelism. Costs a bit of bundling wall-clock; buys memory headroom.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger `release-android` and confirm the EAS Android build logs `Union build: capping Metro maxWorkers=2 ...` and completes past `Background graph built`.

---
_Supersedes the original approach in this PR (setting `eas.json` `resourceClass: large` + raising Gradle `-Xmx`), which was a no-op: CI already forces `--resource-class large`, and the build was already OOMing on 32 GB. Those changes have been reverted; this PR now contains only the worker cap._

author: connor-adams
body:
## Bug

`buildT1` (`backend/src/tax/engine/t1.ts:217`) added **employment** CPP and EI to `totalPayable` (L43500):

```ts
const totalPayable = sumD([federalTax, onTax, onSurtax, ohp, cppEmployee, eiEmployee, oasRepayment]);
```

On a real CRA T1, line 43500 does **not** include employment CPP/EI — those are remitted via payroll (T4 box 16/18). Their only T1 effect is the 15% non-refundable credit, which the engine already applies (line ~140). By also adding them to `totalPayable` without crediting the withheld amounts, the engine **overstated `refundOrOwing` (L48500) for every taxpayer with employment income** — turning real refunds into balances owing. (It also computed EI even for EI-exempt employees, e.g. non-arm's-length family employment.)

## Fix

Remove `cppEmployee` / `eiEmployee` from the `totalPayable` sum only:

```ts
const totalPayable = sumD([federalTax, onTax, onSurtax, ohp, oasRepayment]);
```

They're still computed, still drive the line-140 credit, and still reported in `totals.cppContrib` / `totals.eiPremium`. Only the payable sum changes.

## Impact

author: youtube-at-vach
body:
💡 **What:**
Replaced blocking `self.msleep()` calls in the `SweepWorker` background thread with non-blocking `QEventLoop` constructs paired with `QTimer`s.

🎯 **Why:** 
The previous implementation utilized a hard polling sleep (`self.msleep(10)`) which hard-blocks the thread's event delivery loop and tied up processing. Similarly, the settling sleep hard-blocked the execution. Refactoring this to a non-blocking `QEventLoop` prevents GUI lockups and allows other asynchronous events to safely process inside the worker thread while it yields waiting for the capture event.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
In a local benchmark of the 100-step sweep capturing module logic mock, the test execution time dropped by **84%**, plunging from ~3.38 seconds down to ~0.54 seconds. The event loops drastically cut out wasted blocking time while still preserving the exact necessary timeouts.

author: quanticsoul4772
body:
## Summary

Graph finding #1: **the graph was never persisted.** Every `reasoning_graph` operation only saved a one-line thought summary — the `graph_nodes`/`graph_edges` tables were write-dead. Consequently:

- `resolve_content` (driving an op by `node_id` instead of `content`) always failed — the node table was empty.
- The `state` operation's `build_graph_state_from_storage` always returned an empty graph.

## Changes

Wire persistence into each operation:

| Op | Writes |
|----|--------|
| `init` | root node |
| `generate` | each child node + edge from parent |
| `score` | updates the node's stored score |
| `aggregate` | synthesis node + edge from each input |
| `refine` | refined node + edge from the original |
| `prune` | deletes pruned nodes |

**Node-ID namespacing.** `graph_nodes.id` is a global primary key, but models reuse short IDs (`root`, `c1`, …) across sessions. Nodes are now stored under `{session}::{model_id}`. `resolve_content` namespaces lookups; `build_graph_state_from_storage` strips the prefix so the model still sees its original IDs. `INSERT OR REPLACE` makes writes idempotent (re-`init`, re-`score`).

**Best-effort.** All graph writes are logged, not propagated — a storage error never discards a reasoning result already returned (matches the existing `save_thought` pattern). Foreign keys are enforced (sqlx default), so an edge to a not-yet-persisted node is simply dropped with a warning rather than failing the op.

**StorageTrait.** Exposed `update_graph_node_score` and `delete_graph_node` (SqliteStorage already had them; they weren't reachable through the trait) — added both forwarders and the doctest mock.

## Tests

8 new end-to-end tests against real in-memory `SqliteStorage` verify round-trip writes, per-session namespacing, score updates, node deletion, `node_id` resolution, and prefix-stripped state. Existing mocked tests get permissive (`times(..)`) write expectations.

- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo test` — 2499 lib + 21 integration + 87 + 35 + 21 doc ✅

body:
Adds per-key TTL via a two-tier expiration model:
- Lazy: GET/exists/size return miss for keys whose expires_at has passed; read path is side-effect-free (no tombstone written)
- Active: background sweeper samples up to 100 live keys per tick, calls router.delete() on expired ones — writes Phase-2 tombstone and fans out to replicas so all copies expire identically

expires_at is an absolute epoch-seconds float computed once by the write leader and carried unchanged through the replication fan-out so replicas expire at the same wall-clock moment.

- engine: put/put_versioned gain expires_at param; get/exists/size check expiry; get_expired_keys() samples for active sweeper; keys_expired_total and sweeper_runs_total Prometheus counters
- wal: append gains expires_at param; _apply_entry restores it on replay
- router: put() gains ttl_seconds param; fan-out carries expires_at
- main: KeyValue model gains ttl_seconds + expires_at; sweeper background loop every 60s; sync_from_peers carries expires_at in live entries
- 20 new TTL tests; 3 existing snapshot/router assertion updates

author: jasonkeyil
body:
## Summary

`MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2.verify` skips attention-backend metadata init on the non-cuda-graph target-verify path, leaving it uninitialized. This is the multi-layer counterpart of the single-layer fix in #26244, which was not applied here.

## Root Cause

The shared `EagleVerifyInputV2Mixin.prepare_for_v2_verify` only sets up attention metadata for the cuda-graph path (via `replay_prepare`); on the non-cuda-graph path it intentionally **defers** the init to `forward_extend` (which runs after `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads the batch). The pre-#26244 in-method `init_forward_metadata` was removed in #26244:

```python
# eagle_info_v2.py prepare_for_v2_verify
if can_run_cuda_graph:
    graph_runner.replay_prepare(verify_forward_batch)
# Non-cuda-graph: defer init to forward_extend ... (init removed in #26244)
return verify_forward_batch, can_run_cuda_graph
```

For `forward_extend` to actually run that init, the worker must call the target with `skip_attn_backend_init=can_run_cuda_graph`. #26244 fixed the single-layer worker (`eagle_worker_v2.py`) accordingly, but the multi-layer worker still passed `skip_attn_backend_init=True`:

```python
# multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py (before)
forward_batch_output = self.target_worker.forward_batch_generation(
    ...
    is_verify=True,
    skip_attn_backend_init=True,   # always skips
)
```

So on the non-cuda-graph verify path neither `prepare_for_v2_verify` nor `forward_extend` initializes the backend, leaving pre-pad shapes (e.g. tripping the DSv4 indexer shape match — the exact failure #26244 describes).

The multi-layer file predates #26244 and this line has always been `True`; it was simply missed when the shared init was removed.

## Fix

Pass `can_run_cuda_graph` (already computed a few lines above from `prepare_for_v2_verify`), matching the single-layer worker:

```python
skip_attn_backend_init=can_run_cuda_graph,
```

- cuda-graph path: skip (replay_prepare already initialized) — unchanged behavior.
- non-cuda-graph path: do not skip, so `forward_extend` runs the post-pad init.

## Test Plan

Affects multi-layer EAGLE v2 (multi-layer MTP, spec-v2) on the non-cuda-graph verify path (e.g. `--disable-cuda-graph` or uncaptured batch sizes). I do not have a multi-GPU/spec environment to reproduce locally; the change is structurally identical to the single-layer fix in #26244 and relies on the same `can_run_cuda_graph` already in scope. Requesting CI / a maintainer with a spec-decoding setup to validate.

body:
## Description

Fixes #10305

`get_class_tag` and `get_tag` return `None` when a tag is explicitly set to `None` in `_tags` (e.g. `"python_version": None`), even when a non-None `tag_value_default` is provided.

### Root cause

`_get_class_flag` / `_get_flag` in `skbase` use `dict.get()`, which returns the stored `None` value instead of the default when the key exists with value `None`:

```python
# skbase _tagmanager.py
collected_flags = cls._get_class_flags(flag_attr_name=flag_attr_name)
return collected_flags.get(flag_name, flag_value_default)
# Returns None when flag_name exists with value None, ignoring flag_value_default
```

### Fix

In `TagAliaserMixin.get_class_tag` and `TagAliaserMixin.get_tag`, after calling `super()`, check if the result is `None` and a non-None default was provided. If so, return the default. This treats `None` as "not set" for the purpose of default value fallback.

### Reproducer

```python
from sktime.base import BaseObject

class MyObj(BaseObject):
    _tags = {"my_tag": None}

# Before fix: returns None
```

author: marlboro-red
body:
## What this is

**Odin** is a library-first, durable workflow engine that orchestrates autonomous
coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI) to do software work
without supervision. You describe a workflow in YAML (with code-hook escape hatches),
pin a provider per step, and Odin runs it — planning, implementing, self-reviewing,
opening a PR — with every step checkpointed so a crashed run resumes where it left off.

**It runs end-to-end today:** `odin run workflow.yaml --repo . --param who=alice`
provisions a git worktree, walks the step DAG, captures the diff, checkpoints to SQLite,
and prints a per-step summary.

## What's in this PR (7 commits)

| Commit | Milestone |
|--------|-----------|
| Foundation | Workflow IR, validator (26 `ODIN###` diagnostics), templating + static ref-checking, the five integration traits + registry + engine façade, `odin validate` |
| M3 | Async subprocess runner (timeout/cancel/streaming) + `ClaudeProvider` (verified against the live `claude` CLI) |
| M2 | `WorktreeWorkspace` + `SlotPoolWorkspace` (blocking claim/reset/release) over the real `git` CLI |
| M4a | `SqliteStore` — durable, crash-resumable run state |
| M4b/c | The **executor**: topo DAG walk → render → dispatch provider/run/action → gates → DIFF capture → checkpoint; `resume_all` continues incomplete runs |
| `odin run` | The engine wired into the CLI |
| Review fixes | All 17 findings from an adversarial review applied (see below) |

## The integration surface

- **In** → `RunInput` (typed `params` + free-form `trigger_payload`).
- **Out** → `RunSummary` (status, per-step results, usage, structured `side_effects`).
- **Extend** → implement one of five small object-safe traits (`Provider`, `Workspace`,
  `Store`, `Action`, `Trigger`). A new coding-agent is one file.
- **Feature-gated** so a parse-only embedder pays nothing for tokio.

## Quality

- **129 tests** (unit + per-rule + real-git-repo integration + CLI binary tests).
- **clippy `pedantic` with `-D warnings`**, `unsafe` forbidden, edition 2024.
- rustdoc clean; every feature combination builds independently.

## Reviewed

Two adversarial multi-agent reviews were run (foundation, then M2–M4). The M2–M4 pass
caught a real **resume blocker** (the persisted DIFF was dropped on crash-resume) and
majors (a timeout/cancel hang, the DIFF missing agent-created files, non-resilient
crash recovery, a slot-pool double-free). All 17 confirmed findings are fixed, each with
a regression test. The shell/template trust boundary and resume-idempotency caveat are
documented in [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

## Not yet (next milestones)

Codex/Copilot provider adapters, built-in actions (`github.open_pr`), LLM-as-judge,
retry, and the daemon's event triggers.

Tests whether the PKB1 × bitfield combinatorial destabilizer (just-confirmed byte-identical across 8 runs by nezuko #2214/#2222) is SPECIFIC to PROJ-ONLY (bitfield=7) or GENERALIZES to other partial-exclusion bitfields.**

author: pgd3311
body:
## What this fixes
Users reported the dish-detail page showing **fewer votes than the home ranked list** (Dirty Banana: list 5 / detail 1; Apple Fritter: list 5 / detail 3). Root-caused to **two coupled, undocumented production issues** — **45 of 138 dishes** had undercounted votes. Both fixes were applied to the live DB today and are committed here to end repo↔live drift.

## Root cause 1 — undocumented 3-day account-age vote gate
The **live** `update_dish_avg_rating()` trigger counted a vote toward `dishes.total_votes`/`avg_rating`/`weighted_vote_count` only if `auth.users.created_at <= NOW() - INTERVAL '3 days'`. This clause existed **only on prod** — not in `schema.sql` or any migration. It was:
- **inconsistent** — `get_ranked_dishes` (the list) counts all votes, no gate;
- **architecturally stale** — gate is time-based but only recomputed on a vote *write*, so a vote from a <3-day account is never re-counted when the account ages;
- **launch-toxic** — most accounts are <3 days old, so the majority of real votes were hidden and new-user-only dishes dropped out of rankings.

**Fix:** remove the gate (keep the 0.5× `ai_estimated` weighting) so `total_votes` is the real, time-independent count, consistent with `get_ranked_dishes`; backfill all dishes. Anti-sybil, if still wanted, belongs as a **ranking-time weight**, not by hiding the count.

## Root cause 2 — dish-name CHECK silently blocking votes
`dishes_name_content_filter_check = CHECK (NOT is_offensive(name))` (added `NOT VALID` 2026-04-24) re-validates the **whole row on every UPDATE**. So the vote trigger's `UPDATE dishes SET total_votes…` rolled back for any dish whose name tripped `is_offensive()` — e.g. the real product **"Smack My Ass Hot Sauce"** — meaning users **could not vote on it at all**, and the backfill failed on it.

**Fix:** replace the CHECK with a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF name` trigger — name is validated on insert/rename only, never on unrelated column updates. New offensive names still blocked; input-time `validateUserContent` remains the first line.

## Verification (live)
After running: `still_stale = 0` (was 45), Dirty Banana = 5, Apple Fritter = 5, and the hot-sauce row is updatable/votable again.

## Scope / rollout
**Backend-only.** Live for all users (web + iOS, any binary) immediately — no app build / no 1.9 needed. Both migrations Codex-reviewed (gpt-5.4). Each has a `-- ROLLBACK:` block.

## Not changed (flagged to Denis, #182)
The same CHECK-on-UPDATE pattern exists on `restaurants.name`, `profiles.display_name`, `votes.review_text`. Lower-risk (no high-frequency trigger writes them like votes write dishes), so left for a deliberate call rather than scope-creeping this PR.

author: reasonofmoon
body:
💡 What: Optimized the HTML5 Canvas rendering loop in `Visualizer.tsx` by pre-calculating the 256 possible `CanvasGradient` objects outside the `requestAnimationFrame` loop, adding a short-circuit break for off-screen elements, and fixing a hydration mismatch in the idle state.

🎯 Why: The Web Audio API provides frequency data as a `Uint8Array` bounded strictly between 0 and 255. Previously, a new `CanvasGradient` object was being created, mapped, and allocated *per bin per frame* (e.g. 1024 bins * 60fps = ~60,000 objects allocated per second). This caused significant garbage collection (GC) pressure and main thread blocking. Additionally, iterating over all bins even when they exceeded `canvas.width` was wasting CPU cycles.

📊 Impact: Massively reduces object allocation per frame from O(n) to O(0) inside the draw loop. Avoids thousands of redundant calculations for off-screen elements. Prevents unnecessary React re-renders on the client due to Next.js hydration mismatches caused by `Math.random()`.

🔬 Measurement: Verify by profiling the Main Thread using Chrome DevTools Performance tab while the Visualizer is playing. Observe a significant drop in "Minor GC" events and a lower frame rendering time. Verified visually via Playwright screenshot that functionality and styling remain identical.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [18376780333553605700](https://jules.google.com/task/18376780333553605700) started by @Reasonofmoon*

## Summary by Sourcery

Optimize the audio visualizer canvas rendering loop and fix a deterministic idle-state display while documenting the performance improvement pattern.

Bug Fixes:
- Make the visualizer idle state deterministic to avoid Next.js hydration mismatches caused by non-deterministic heights.

Enhancements:
- Reduce canvas rendering overhead by precomputing gradient styles for all possible frequency values and short-circuiting off-screen bars in the visualizer loop.

Documentation:

author: sa3eed3ed
body:
## Summary

This adds an optional `iap` authentication method for deployments that run behind [Google Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy](https://cloud.google.com/iap/docs/concepts-overview).

When OpenRelik is deployed behind IAP (a common setup for internal/BeyondCorp-style deployments on GCP), the proxy has already authenticated the user before any request reaches the server, and IAP policy (including Google Groups) already controls who gets through. Today such deployments still have to run a second OAuth flow inside OpenRelik via the `google` auth method, which means provisioning a separate OAuth client and maintaining a duplicate allowlist.

Trusting a plain identity header from a proxy would be insecure (headers can be spoofed if the backend is ever reachable directly), so this implements GCP's documented approach instead: validating the **signed** `X-Goog-IAP-JWT-Assertion` header that IAP attaches to every proxied request ([Securing your app with signed headers](https://cloud.google.com/iap/docs/signed-headers-howto)).

## Technical details

- New `src/auth/iap.py`, closely mirroring the structure of the existing `oidc.py`:
  - `GET /login/iap` validates the assertion and issues the standard OpenRelik JWT cookies, then redirects to the UI. Since IAP adds the header to every request, there is no redirect dance — validating the header is the whole login flow.
  - Verification uses `google.oauth2.id_token.verify_token` (the `google-auth` dependency already used by `google.py`) against IAP's public JWK endpoint, checking signature, expiry, audience and issuer.
  - Users are auto-provisioned on first login like the `google`/`oidc` methods (`auth_method="iap"`). IAP assertions carry no profile claims, so the email doubles as display name.
- New `[auth.iap]` config section (documented in `settings_example.toml`):
  - `audience` — the expected assertion audience shown in the IAP console
  - `allowlist` / `public_access` — same semantics as the other methods. Note `public_access = true` here does not expose the server publicly: only identities IAP has authenticated and authorized can carry a valid assertion, so deployments can fully delegate access control to IAP policy.
  - `certs_url` — override of the verification-key URL, for testing against locally minted assertions
- Conditionally imported/mounted in `main.py` exactly like the `oidc` method, so existing deployments are unaffected unless `[auth.iap]` is configured.
- Adds a `pyjwt[crypto]` dependency: IAP publishes its verification keys in JWK format, and `google-auth` delegates JWK-set verification to PyJWT (its x509-PEM path used by the existing `google` method does not need it). This matches the dependency set in GCP's own signed-header validation samples.
- The login UI needs no changes: setting `OPENRELIK_AUTH_METHODS=iap` renders a generic login button for the method.

## Testing

- Unit tests in `src/tests/auth/iap_test.py` following the structure of `oidc_test.py`: assertion validation (valid, invalid signature, wrong issuer), allowlist/public-access authorization, missing header, missing email claim, and user provisioning for new and existing users. Full test suite passes (373 tests).
- Verified end to end against a running stack with simulated IAP: a local proxy that mints ES256-signed assertions (same shape as real IAP, with a JWKS endpoint the server verifies against via `certs_url`). Confirmed: requests without/with-invalid/with-wrong-audience assertions are rejected with 401, valid assertions log in and provision the user, and the browser flow through the proxy works end to end including cookie-based API access afterwards.
- Additionally validated on GKE behind real Identity-Aware Proxy (GCE ingress, BackendConfig-enabled IAP, backend-service audience): live assertions verify against IAP's published JWK keys and users are provisioned from the asserted identity.

author: jsmestad
body:
## What

`Minga.Integration.FileOpenFromAgentTabTest` intermittently fails on CI: after opening a file from the agent tab, the `i# <Esc>` insert doesn't land and the assertion sees the un-commented line. It passes in isolation and only fails under concurrent load.

## Root cause

Test isolation, not a product bug. `start_editor_in_agent_mode/1` started the editor **without** an `events_registry` or `sidebar_registry`, so `EditorState` fell back to `Minga.Events.default_registry()` (global) and the global sidebar table. The editor subscribes to ~25 global event types (`:buffer_changed`, `:option_changed`, `:log_message`, renders, …), so under load, broadcasts from other async tests were delivered into this editor and interleaved with the keystrokes, dropping the edit. The co-occurring `DiredTest` render crash (`Cell.new(0, -39, …)`) seen in the same job is the same shared-state contamination from another angle.

The standard `start_editor` helper already isolates both registries per test; the agent-mode helper didn't.

## Fix

Isolate the event and sidebar registries per test in `start_editor_in_agent_mode`, mirroring `start_editor`, and thread the events registry into the file buffer. No production code changes — the production behavior is correct; the test harness was sharing global state.

## Validation

- Both tests in the file pass in isolation.
- Confirmed under load: with CPU saturation (`yes` × cores), the full integration suite at `--max-cases 16` passed (85 tests), no agent-tab failure, and the Dired render crash did not recur.

Surfaced while running CI for #2136 (which carries the same fix so its own checks stay green); extracted here so it can merge independently.

## Summary

Major expansion of UnrealClaude MCP tooling — 16 new tools, 3 enhanced input operations, and 6 sprints of capability upgrades. All tools compile clean on UE 5.5.

### Sprint 5: 12 New MCP Tools + Enhanced Input Batch API

**🔴 High Priority (direct pain points)**
- **`world_settings`** — Get/set GameMode override, gravity, kill Z, world scale. Eliminates manual World Settings fighting.
- **`project_settings`** — Read/write default game mode, maps, GameInstance, input settings. First-ever project settings access via MCP.
- **`build`** — Live Coding hot_reload + compile_blueprint + compile_all_blueprints. No more leaving the session to compile.
- **`class_defaults`** — Batch get/set Blueprint CDO properties with full UE reflection (bool, int, float, string, struct, enum, soft refs). Replaces one-at-a-time CDO editing.
- **`create_cpp_class`** — Scaffold C++ class with correct UE5 boilerplate (14 base class shortcuts: Actor, Pawn, Character, GameModeBase, PlayerController, etc.). Generates .h + .cpp with UCLASS, GENERATED_BODY, BeginPlay/Tick stubs, optional root component, extra UPROPERTY declarations.

**🟡 Medium Priority (workflow gaps)**
- **`import_asset`** — Import FBX/PNG/PLY/etc into Content Browser (single + bulk). Uses UAutomatedAssetImportData.
- **`widget_blueprint`** — Create UMG Widget Blueprints with auto-creation of BindWidget-matching child widgets from C++ parent class.
- **`actor_search`** — Advanced actor search by class, tag, name pattern, component type, property value, and spatial radius. All filters combine with AND logic.
- **`enhanced_input` `create_imc_from_config`** — Create full IMC from JSON config in ONE call. Replaces 20+ separate add_mapping + add_modifier calls. Accepts action names or paths, string or object triggers/modifiers.
- **`enhanced_input` `remove_trigger` / `remove_modifier`** — Remove trigger/modifier by index from mappings.

**🟢 Lower Priority (nice to have)**
- **`data_table`** — Full CRUD for DataTable rows with struct field reflection.
- **`curve`** — Create/edit CurveFloat, CurveVector, CurveLinearColor. Add keys, evaluate, bulk set.
- **`collision`** — Get/set collision profiles, per-channel responses, list available profiles and channels.
- **`sequencer`** — Create LevelSequence, bind actors, add transform keyframes, query tracks, set playback range/rate.

author: sagivby
body:
Implements **Phase 2** of the multi-tenant migration (epic #6). Moves all per-host drafting config out of global files/env into per-tenant DB rows, editable in a new **Settings** page.

> **Stacked on #7 (Phase 1).** Base is `phase-1-auth-tenant-model` so this diff shows only Phase 2. After #7 merges to `main`, GitHub auto-retargets this PR to `main`. **Merge #7 first.**

## What changed
- **`config.py`** (new) — `tenant_settings` table (`host_name`, `units_json`, `template`, `from_email`, `reply_channels`). `get_settings`/`save_settings`/`get_units`/`validate_units`, embedded `DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`, and `seed_tenant(from_legacy=)`.
- **`models.py`** — `ensure_operator` seeds tenant 1 from the legacy `units.json` / `response_template.md` / `HOST_NAME` / `REPLY_CHANNELS` / `FROM_EMAIL` (idempotent); `create_user` seeds fresh-tenant defaults.
- **`responder.py`** — config-driven: `evaluate_lead(item, tenant_id, …)`; dropped `UNITS_PATH`/`TEMPLATE_PATH`/`HOST_NAME` reads; the cached system prompt is now per-tenant.
- **`runner.py`** — `_channels(tenant_id)`; draft/send carry `tenant_id`; passes the tenant's `from_email`.
- **`mailer.py`** — `send_email(…, from_email=)` sets a per-tenant `From:`; SMTP host/user/pass stay a **shared relay**.
- **`dashboard.py` + `settings.html`** — `/settings` (units **JSON textarea** + template + identity), units validated on save (errors re-render without losing edits), header **Settings** link.

## Design decisions
- **Units = validated JSON textarea** (power-user "template editing" level; minimal UI — structured CRUD deferred to Phase 5 onboarding).
- **Per-tenant `from_email` + `reply_channels`; shared SMTP relay.** Full per-tenant SMTP creds + encryption belong with Phase 3's credential work.

## Verification
- Operator config seeded from legacy: `host_name=Sagiv`, **2 units**, `platform,email` ✅
- **Two tenants → different drafting prompts, no cross-leak** (mocked client, no API spend): tenant 1 prompt has "Sagiv"/DC and not "Dana"; tenant 2 has "Dana"/Austin and not "Sagiv" ✅
- `/settings` GET prefilled; valid POST persists; **invalid units JSON re-renders with the parse error and does NOT save** ✅
- No drafting path reads `units.json` / `response_template.md` / `HOST_NAME` / `REPLY_CHANNELS` ✅
- Operator config restored to original after testing ✅

## Reviewer notes
- `units.json` / `response_template.md` are kept as the operator's seed source + reference; they're no longer read during drafting.
- The cached Anthropic system prefix is per-tenant now — still cache-effective across a tenant's repeated drafts, just not shared across tenants (correct for isolation).

Closes #2

author: sa3eed3ed
body:
## Summary

This adds support for Anthropic's Claude models with two new providers:

- **`anthropic`** — the Anthropic API (`api.anthropic.com`), authenticated with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- **`anthropicvertex`** — the same models served from **Vertex AI Model Garden**, authenticated with Application Default Credentials (GKE Workload Identity, attached service accounts). Deployments on Google Cloud get Claude with **no API key to provision, store, or rotate** — access is controlled with IAM like any other Vertex model.

## Technical details

- `providers/anthropic.py` mirrors the structure of the existing `openai.py` (chat session with history, backoff on rate limits/API errors, `to_dict` config exposure). `providers/anthropicvertex.py` subclasses it, swapping only the client construction for `AnthropicVertex`.
- **Exact token counting**: `count_tokens` uses the API's counting endpoint instead of a local approximation, with a conservative estimate as fallback — improving the chunker's packing decisions in `generate_file_analysis`.
- **Prompt caching**: system instructions are sent as content blocks marked `cache_control: ephemeral`, so workloads that repeat the same instructions across many calls (per-chunk analysis of large files) reuse the cached prefix instead of reprocessing it.
- Configuration follows the existing `PROVIDER_CONFIG` convention:
  - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL`
  - `ANTHROPICVERTEX_PROJECT_ID`, `ANTHROPICVERTEX_REGION`, `ANTHROPICVERTEX_DEFAULT_MODEL`
- One dependency added: `anthropic[vertex]`.
- Purely additive — no changes to existing providers or the interface.

## Testing

- `tests/test_anthropic.py` covers both providers following the `test_googleai.py` mocking style: initialization and auth wiring, generation config, generate (with/without system instructions, object mode), multi-turn chat history, exact token counting and its fallback path, context-window resolution, and that the Vertex provider builds its client from project/region with no API key. Full suite passes (39 tests).
- Live-verified end to end against Claude Sonnet 4.6 on Vertex AI (global endpoint) with Google Cloud credentials only: `generate`, multi-turn `chat` with history, `count_tokens` (exact API counting), and `generate_file_analysis` through the chunker. This run also caught and fixed a real-API constraint: current Claude models accept a single sampling control per request, so the provider forwards only `temperature`.

author: sarub0b0
body:
## Summary

Migrate the Network tab from `substring_applicator("NAME")` to the column-aware filter framework, completing the migration started in PR #992 (Pod) and PR #997 (Config). The Network view aggregates six+ resource types (Ingress, Service, Pod, NetworkPolicy, Gateway, HTTPRoute), so `kind:` becomes the most useful new filter dimension.

Since this PR removes the last consumer-facing use of `substring_applicator`, the function and its tests are deleted as proximate cleanup.

## New filter capabilities

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nginx` | bare value → `NAME` include (regex) — same as before |
| `kind:Service` | only Services |
| `!kind:Pod` | exclude Pods |
| `kind:Ingress kind:HTTPRoute` | KIND in (Ingress, HTTPRoute) — same-column OR |
| `kind:Service name:web` | AND across columns |
| `age:1d` | filter by AGE value |
| `label:app=nginx` | server-side labelSelector, applied to **every** sub-fetch URL (per namespace × resource type) |

## NAMESPACE Z-model

Mirrors Pod #992 / Config #997. `namespace:default` returns the guidance message `"namespace is selected via the namespace selector, not the filter"` rather than the generic unknown-column error. Namespace is a scope, not a row attribute.

## Plumbing

- `NetworkMessage::Filter(Option<String>)` added
- `SharedNetworkFilter = Arc<RwLock<Option<String>>>` added to `workers/kube/controller.rs`, wired into `NetworkPoller` alongside `shared_target_namespaces` and `api_resources`
- Controller's main loop routes `Kube::Network(NetworkMessage::Filter(sel))` into `shared_network_filter`
- `fetch_table` now takes `label_selector: Option<&str>`; `polling` and `fetch_resource` thread it through; the URL is built per-resource with the encoded labelSelector appended when non-empty
- Per-sub-fetch URL: `?labelSelector=<percent_encoding::utf8_percent_encode(_, NON_ALPHANUMERIC)>` (consistent with PR #996)
- `network_filter_help_widget` new dialog (Network-specific examples), registered in `window.rs`
- `NetworkTab` grows `network_filter_help_dialog: Widget<'static>` field

## substring_applicator cleanup (in-scope)

Before this PR, `substring_applicator` was the legacy filter API used by Config / Network (Pod migrated in #992). With Network switching to `network_filter_applicator`, it is no longer used anywhere. Removed:

- `pub fn substring_applicator(column: &str) -> TableFilterApplicator` in `src/ui/widget/table/filter_applicator.rs`
- 8 unit tests for `substring_applicator`
- `invoke_parser` test helper (used only by those tests)
- The `pub use` re-export in `src/ui/widget/table.rs`

This is bundled here because this PR is the proximate cause of the dead-code condition; leaving it for a follow-up would mean shipping a warning in the next main commit.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build`: clean (only pre-existing `try_from_kubeconfig` warning)
- [x] `cargo test --all`: 701 passed / 0 failed (was 698 + 11 new Network tests − 8 removed substring tests = 701)
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets`: no new warnings
- [x] `cargo +nightly fmt --check`: clean
- [x] Manual GKE smoke verified:
  - [x] Bare value `bbt-cafe` in the Network tab narrows rows whose NAME contains `bbt-cafe` (mixed kinds, no regression)
  - [x] `kind:Service` shows Services only (58/179)
  - [x] `!kind:Pod` excludes Pods (86/179 → Services + HTTPRoutes)
  - [x] `kind:Service kind:HTTPRoute` applies OR-in-list (86/179, same as the previous exclusion)
  - [x] `kind:Service name:bbt-cafe` applies AND across columns (3/179)
  - [x] `namespace:default` returns the guidance message
  - [x] `label:app=bbt-cafe-api` applies the server-side filter per sub-fetcher — kubetui returns the same set as `kubectl get pod,svc,httproute -n latest -l app=bbt-cafe-api` (Pod-only in this case, since only the Pod carries the label; confirms the server-side filter is applied independently to each kind)
  - [x] `?` or `help` in the filter input opens the Network Filter Help dialog (title, terms, examples, namespace notice all present)
  - [x] Filter persists across the 1-second poll loop
  - [x] Esc clears the filter and the table returns to the full set

## Test coverage added

10 cases for `parse_network_filter`:
- empty input
- bare value → NAME include
- builtin columns (kind: include / !kind: exclude)
- age accepted
- label selector capture
- unknown column → error
- namespace → guidance message (NOT generic unknown-column)
- label keyword bypass (`label:` is not treated as a column lookup)
- quoted value with whitespace
- data: rejected (regression case — DATA belongs to Config, not Network)

1 case for `network_filter_applicator`:
- constructs without panic

## Related

- PR #992 — Pod column-aware filter
- PR #996 — labelSelector URL encoding (same `utf8_percent_encode` applied here)
- PR #997 — Config column-aware filter
- This PR completes the column-aware filter migration for all aggregated-view tabs

body:
## Summary

Visiting the app could render a permanently blank page when resolving the current user failed with anything other than an HTTP 401.

The global router guard calls `setUser()` and handles rejections with `error.response.status === 401`. For failures that carry no response — network errors, or cross-origin requests blocked before a response exists (common behind authenticating proxies that keep per-host sessions) — `error.response` is undefined: the handler throws, `next()` is never called, the navigation stays pending, and the user sees a blank screen.

## Fix

Route to the login page on any user-resolution failure. The login page is the correct destination for every failure mode here, and navigation always resolves.

## Testing

Full test suite passes (434 tests). Manually reproduced the blank page by making the user-resolution request fail without a response, and verified the guard now lands on the login page.

body:
## Overnight cleanup — autonomous PR (9 of 10)

One of ten independent, disjoint cleanup PRs (theme: **net LOC reduction via de-duplication and dropping code/comments that don't earn their keep**).

### Issue — the same invariant decoded in two places
"Decode a SQLite BLOB column into a 32-byte `Hash`, erroring with `FromSqlConversionFailure` when the length isn't 32" was written twice with identical shape and error message: `kv.rs::row_to_entry` (building an entry's `value_hash`) and `gc.rs::read_roots` (building each GC root). Two hand-maintained encodings of the single invariant "the `value_hash` column is exactly 32 bytes".

### Fix shape
Extract one `pub(crate) fn hash_from_blob(&[u8]) -> rusqlite::Result<Hash>` in `kv.rs` (which already owns the entries-table column mapping) and call it from both sites. The helper uses `try_into` for the length check rather than the manual `[0u8; 32]` + `copy_from_slice`. `read_roots` keeps its narrow `SELECT value_hash` query — only the decode is shared.

### Verification
- `cargo fmt -p sunset-store-fs` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p sunset-store-fs --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passes
- `cargo test -p sunset-store-fs --all-features` — passes, including the 16-test conformance suite and the GC tests `gc_blobs_keeps_reachable_drops_orphans` / `gc_blobs_continues_past_corrupt_reachable_blob` (which exercise `read_roots`).

**Net −6 LOC** (+14 / −20).

body:
### Severity
Medium

### Vulnerability
The `nginx/nginx.conf` file contained slightly relaxed security headers. The `Content-Security-Policy` explicitly allowed `'unsafe-inline'` in `script-src`, which could potentially allow attackers to execute injected cross-site scripting (XSS) payloads. Additionally, the `X-XSS-Protection` header was set to `"1; mode=block"`, which is deprecated and can theoretically be abused by attackers to introduce new vulnerabilities or cause unexpected behaviors (XS-Leaks).

### Impact
If a vulnerability allowing script injection existed, `'unsafe-inline'` would allow that script to execute. The deprecated `X-XSS-Protection` configuration might cause legitimate scripts to fail or expose side channels.

### Fix
- Updated `X-XSS-Protection` to `"0"` in accordance with modern security standards (OWASP, MDN).
- Removed `'unsafe-inline'` from the `script-src` directive in the `Content-Security-Policy`.

### Verification
- Verified by running the production build (`pnpm build`) to ensure there are no syntax regressions.
- Verified test suite passes locally (`pnpm run test:run`).

```bash
cosign verify \
```

```bash
cosign verify \
```

author: kroisse
body:
## Summary

trunk-ir transforms (backend lowering, outside the shared-pipeline verifier guard from #713) disposed of ops with `remove_op_from_block`/`detach_op` only, leaving their operand use-chain entries on still-live values (#710 **Class A**). This PR switches the dispose-intent sites to `erase_op` (= detach + the step-1-strengthened `remove_op`).

## Changes

- **`inline`** — regular call (RAUW'd) and tail call (terminator, no results).
- **`resolve_unrealized_casts`** — same-type and materialized cast replacements (RAUW'd).
- **`scf_to_cf`** — yield/continue/break → `br` replacements (terminators).
- **`global_dce`** — unreachable `func.func` removal; `erase_op` now also clears the dead body's operand use-chains. Func scopes are independent (SSA), so this can't affect reachable functions.
- **`canonicalize`** — collapse the existing `detach_op` + `remove_op` orphan cleanup to `erase_op` for consistency.

## Excluded (move/reorder — must NOT erase)

- `scf_to_cf` scf-op disposal at 156/201/277: `detach_op` happens **before** `inline_region_blocks` moves its region blocks into the parent, so `erase_op` would clear the moved ops' use-chains.
- `canonicalize` body-op hoisting (re-attached, not disposed).

## Verification

- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace` (1356) green — including `e2e_native`/wasm e2e that exercise these backend transforms, and `inline`/`scf_to_cf`/`global_dce` unit tests.
- [x] Risk sites (inline tail-call, global_dce func) erase without tripping `remove_op`'s result-use assertion.
- [x] Pre-commit hook (clippy + fmt + full suite) — passed.

Behavior-preserving.

## Scope

Completes #710 Class A across the codebase: step 2 (#712, tribute-passes) + this step 2b (trunk-ir transforms). Class B was fixed in step 1 (#711); the shared pipeline is guarded by step 3 (#713).

Part of #710.

author: sa3eed3ed
body:
## Summary

Adds Google Cloud IAP support and a single-host ingress mode to the OpenRelik chart, plus a fix for a broken BackendConfig reference.

- **IAP support** (`config.iap.*`): when enabled, the rendered `settings.toml` gets an `[auth.iap]` section (for OpenRelik server builds with the `iap` auth method), the frontend advertises the `iap` login method, and both GCE BackendConfigs enable IAP from an existing OAuth-client Secret. This lets deployments delegate access control to IAP policy (e.g. Google Groups) with the app cryptographically validating the signed proxy assertions.
- **Single-host mode**: when `openRelikFrontendHost` and `openRelikAPIHost` are set to the same value, the ingress renders one host with API path routing (`/api/*`, `/auth/*`, `/login/*`, `/openapi.json`, `/docs`) and the UI as default. A single origin avoids cross-origin cookie and CORS handling, which matters behind per-host-session auth proxies such as IAP. Paths use `ImplementationSpecific` because GCE expands a `Prefix` rule for `/p/` into both `/p` and `/p/*`, which would capture the frontend's own `/login` route. The managed-certificate template skips the duplicate domain in this mode.
- **Bugfix**: the nginx Service annotation referenced `...-openrelik-backend-config` for port 8711, a BackendConfig this chart does not create (it creates `...-openrelik-frontend-backend-config`), so the frontend port silently received no BackendConfig at all.

## Testing

Deployed on GKE Autopilot with a GCE ingress, Google-managed certificates and real IAP: both ports verified IAP-gated (302 with `x-goog-iap-generated-response`), the frontend's `/login` route serves the UI while `/login/iap` reaches the API, and an end-to-end workflow (login through IAP, upload, worker execution) passes against the deployment. `helm template` output verified for both single-host and two-host configurations, with the other charts disabled and enabled.

author: choiceoh
body:
## Summary

The right **session drawer** was supposed to open by a right-to-left edge swipe (added in #1903) but never did — only the top-bar button worked.

**Root cause:** the right drawer is a `ModalNavigationDrawer` (RTL-flipped) nested *outside* the left nav drawer, with the content inside the **inner left drawer**. Both default to `gesturesEnabled = true`, and the inner left drawer's horizontal-drag detector wraps the content and **swallows horizontal drags**, starving the outer (session) drawer's open-gesture. The RTL flip alone can't fix a nested-drawer gesture conflict.

**Fix:** detect the right edge explicitly on the content's *parent* Box (a child of the inner drawer, so it sees horizontal drags first). A leftward drag starting within 32dp of the right edge — and only when both drawers are closed — opens the session drawer and consumes the drag. Everything else passes through:
- vertical list scrolling unaffected (parent sees events after the child list consumes vertical drags),
- taps / FAB unaffected (we only consume once a leftward drag passes the trigger),
- the left drawer keeps its built-in left-edge gesture (the edge check bails for left-edge downs).

## Test
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- ⚠️ **Gestures can't be verified in the headless render harness** — needs on-device confirmation. The edge width (32dp) / trigger (24dp) are easy to tune, and I can switch to a drag-follow (drawer tracks the finger) instead of trigger-open if preferred.

body: ## What's broken on the demo site A full-page screenshot audit of every page on https://alshedivat.github.io/al-folio/ surfaced two user-visible bugs introduced or exposed by the v1 upgrade. ### Bug 1 — Repositories page: all stat cards show broken alt-text (HIGH) Both external services are currently unavailable: - `github-readme-stats.vercel.app` → HTTP 503 `DEPLOYMENT_PAUSED` - `github-profile-trophy.vercel.app` → HTTP 402 Every `` on the repositories page fails to load, rendering as a list of broken-image alt-text strings. The templates had no `onerror` fallback. **Fix (in al_folio_core):** `onerror="this.closest('.repo').style.display='none'"` on every stat-card image in `repo.liquid`, `repo_user.liquid`, and `repo_trophies.liquid`. When a service is unavailable the entire card hides gracefully; when it comes back up cards render normally. ### Bug 2 — `.af-popover` / `.af-tooltip` completely unstyled (MEDIUM) `tooltips-setup.js` (active by default, since bootstrap-compat is disabled) creates `.af-popover` and `.af-tooltip` elements as its vanilla fallback — for example when hovering the author-info circle icon (ⓘ) on the publications page. These class names had **no CSS rules at all** in `al_folio_core`: no `position`, no styling, no `z-index`. The tooltip/popover appeared as invisible, unpositioned text nodes appended to `document.body`. (The theme's `_utilities.scss` only defined `.popover` — Bootstrap's class — which is irrelevant without bootstrap-compat loaded.) **Fix (in al_folio_core):** Added `position: absolute`, `z-index: 1070/1080`, and theme-color styling to both classes. The purgecss safelist in al-folio already protects both names so they survive the deploy pipeline. ## Changes - `Gemfile` / `Gemfile.lock`: bump `al_folio_core` 1.0.10 → 1.0.11 ([PR #19](https://github.com/al-org-dev/al-folio-core/pull/19), now merged and released) ## Scope All other pages screenshotted look correct. No other CSS/layout regressions were found beyond these two. The screenshot audit also confirmed: - The `var(--spacing)` Tailwind fix from #3634 is working correctly in production. - `main.css` cache-bust hash (`9278fad1…`) is stable and non-empty. - All blog posts, CV, teaching, people, projects, books pages render as expected. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mikegilchrist
body:
## Summary

Implements issue #28 (phi prior anchor option) and extends it into a full composable phi prior specification API.

- **Mode constructors**: `constrained(statistic, value)`, `fixed(value)`, `estimated(prior)`
- **Prior constructors**: `prior_uniform()`, `prior_normal()`, `prior_student_t()`, `prior_exponential()`
- **Five anchor statistics**: mean, median, mode, variance, sd — each with a closed-form `mPhi` formula in `Parameter::computeMPhi()`
- **Backward compatible**: all prior calling patterns (`sphi=1`, `sphi=NA`, `phi.prior.constraint="median"`) continue to work; `phi.prior.constraint` deprecated with warning
- **C++ members**: `phiMuMode`, `phiMuFixed`, `phiConstraintValue`, `sphiPriorType/Low/High`, `phiFloor/Ceiling` — all persisted in restart files
- **140 tests** in `testPhiPrior.R` covering formula math, constructor validation, getter/setter round-trips, MCMC smoke tests, and restart round-trips

## Key design decisions

- `phi.mphi` / `phi.sphi` argument names match C++ `mPhi`/`sphi` (log-space meanlog/sdlog)
- Mode constructors are unqualified (`constrained`, `fixed`, `estimated`); prior constructors are prefixed `prior_` to avoid rstanarm/brms namespace collisions
- Default: `phi.mphi = constrained("mean", 1)`, `phi.sphi = estimated(prior_uniform(0, 10))` — same as before for mean anchor, new default prior bounds for sphi
- `estimated()` for `phi.mphi` is reserved (deferred: needs new MCMCAlgorithm update step)

## Test plan

- [ ] `R CMD check` on clean tree
- [ ] `NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/testPhiPrior.R')"` — 140 pass
- [ ] Verify `sphi=NA` and `sphi=1` legacy behavior unchanged in existing downstream scripts

Closes #28

author: atsuoishimoto
body:
Closes #8.

## What

Make the `[[tool.pyappdist.targets]].format` key **required** and validate it against the platform OS.

- `format` no longer defaults to `"msi"`. A target with no `format` now raises `ConfigError` at config load.
- `format` must match the platform's OS — `msi`/`msix` → windows, `linux` → linux. A mismatch (e.g. `format = "msi"` on `linux-x86_64`, or `format = "linux"` on `windows-x86_64`) is rejected at load with a precise message, instead of building part-way and failing late (the original symptom in #8: `error: MSI generation requires ... manufacturer`).

## Why

Per #8, `format` and `platform` were independent, so a `linux-x86_64` target that omitted `format` silently ran the MSI path and failed at the very end. The target *name* is just a label and never influenced the format, which was surprising. This makes the intent explicit and fails fast.

This implements #8 with the **required-key** approach (chosen over the platform-aware-default alternative floated in the issue).

## Changes

- `src/pyappdist/config.py`: add `_FORMAT_OS = {"msi": "windows", "msix": "windows", "linux": "linux"}`; in `_parse_targets`, require `format` and validate it against `target.os`.
- Add `format = "msi"` to every Windows target in `samples/*` and `e2e/smoke` (the `msix`/`linux` targets already set it).
- `tests/test_config.py`: parametrize the format in the test templates; replace `test_format_default_msi` with `test_format_required`; add `test_format_platform_mismatch`.
- Docs: `docs/configuration.rst`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — mark `format` required, drop "(default)", remove the obsolete "msi-on-linux builds image-only" note.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest -q` → 67 passed.
- Negative checks: missing `format`, `msi` on linux, and `linux` on windows each raise a clear `ConfigError` at load.
- All `samples/*` + `e2e/smoke` configs load with the expected per-target formats.

author: lebiraja
body:
Full re-engineering of `@lebiraja/plugintool` addressing the ~25 issues from the audit. **15 commits**, organized in 8 phases. Full catalog in `docs/FIXES.md`.

## Why
The app didn't work in Docker (env vars set but never read), the three core pipelines (search/RAG/deep-research) were partially broken, and the frontend needed a redesign. This PR makes search, RAG, and deep research work end-to-end with streaming; rebuilds the backend on dependency injection with tests; makes the npm package's API URL configurable; and redesigns the frontend on shadcn/ui + Magic UI.

## Highlights

**Docker / config** — `config.py` binds the env vars compose actually sets (`AliasChoices`: `OLLAMA_URL`/`OLLAMA_HOST`, `MONGODB_URL`/`MONGO_URL`/`MONGODB_URI`). Services read URLs from `settings`. Frontend served by nginx proxying `/api` → backend (no CORS, SSE-friendly). `.env.example` authored.

**RAG** — consolidated into one session-aware ChromaDB-only `rag_service` (device auto-detect kills the CPU crash; OCR/CSV absorbed; `DocumentProcessor` deleted). Frontend now uploads to `/api/sessions/{id}/upload`, so RAG actually retrieves uploaded files.

**Search** — settings-driven Serper key, bounded scrape concurrency, correct cache TTL, DDG off the event loop, normalized results.

**Deep Research** — Mongo-persisted (survives restart), request-local counters via `contextvars` (no races), real SSE stage-progress streaming.

**Chat / sessions** — Ollama on `/api/chat` (proper multi-turn), `stream_chat` + `/message/stream` SSE, coalesced single-write `add_message`, fixed `generate_title` signature mismatch.

**Backend arch** — FastAPI DI (single shared services), `lifespan` (not `on_event`), central exception handlers (no `str(e)` leakage), request-logging middleware.

**Frontend** — full shadcn/ui + Magic UI redesign (refined-dark), configurable API (`VITE_API_URL` / `configureApi` for npm consumers), live token + research streaming, dead files removed, `any`/`console.log` gone.

author: ptrlrd
body:
## Why

Tonight's "profile went from 106 runs to 3" report. The 104 runs were intact in Mongo; the bug had to be between origin and browser. Clearing CF cache fixed it.

Tracing the actual cache directive on the endpoint:

```python
# backend/app/main.py — CORSStaticMiddleware
elif path.startswith("/api/"):
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "public, max-age=300, s-maxage=3600"
```

`/api/auth/runs`, `/api/auth/me`, `/api/auth/stats` all fall under this branch. The origin was telling Cloudflare to cache per-user authed responses for one hour at the edge. That's how a profile request can end up serving someone else's data, or a stale snapshot of your own, from a CF PoP.

Today CF bypasses these anyway via its cookie-presence heuristic, which is why this hadn't bitten harder. But the origin shouldn't depend on a CDN heuristic to keep auth data private. Belt-and-suspenders.

## What

One branch added to `CORSStaticMiddleware.dispatch`, placed before the generic `/api/*` fallback:

```python
elif path.startswith("/api/auth/"):
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "private, no-store"
```

- `private` keeps the response off shared caches (CDN, intermediate proxies).
- `no-store` keeps it out of any cache, including the browser disk cache. Each profile load goes back to origin.

## What it doesn't change

- `/static/*`, `/qa/*`, `/api/runs/*` (community runs feed), `/api/*` (entity data) — all unchanged. Those are public, cacheable, and the existing TTLs are correct.
- The cookie-presence bypass that CF applies today still applies. This is additive defense, not a replacement for it.

## Deploy

Backend image rebuild + restart on the box. No frontend changes, no migration.

author: chadonillo
body:
## ELI-911 — Apply ELI-903 zero-downtime + /tmp hardening to prod (`kube/base`)

Follow-up to **ELI-903 / PR #91** (commit `224bb020`), which fixed only the **dev overlay** and explicitly flagged: _"Prod (`kube/base`) carries the same latent risk → follow-up."_ This PR mirrors the hardening into **`kube/base`** so the prod overlay inherits it.

### What & why
`kube/base/deployment.yaml` (single file changed, +22/-1):

1. **Explicit zero-downtime `strategy`** — `RollingUpdate maxSurge:1 / maxUnavailable:0`.
   Base previously had **no `strategy` block**, relying on the implicit k8s default (`25%/25%`) which only *rounds* to a zero-downtime shape at `replicas:1` by luck. An overlay that overrode it (exactly what the old dev overlay did with `maxSurge:0/maxUnavailable:1`) — or any future replica bump — would empty the `paperclip` Service endpoint on every rollout/restart/eviction → external Traefik **502 on all routes incl `/health`** while the app is healthy internally. Pinning it guarantees a new **Ready** pod binds `:3100` before the old one is removed.
2. **`ephemeral-storage` requests `3Gi` / limits `5Gi`** — reserves node disk for the `/tmp` + `/app/data` emptyDir budget so a noisy `/tmp` cannot trip a node-level `DiskPressure` eviction (same 502 gap at `replicas:1`).
3. **`/tmp` emptyDir `sizeLimit` `1Gi → 3Gi`** — root fs is `readOnlyRootFilesystem:true`, so the app writes scratch/uploads to `/tmp`; the old `1Gi` cap evicted the pod. `data` left at `1Gi`.

Values are identical to PR #91's dev overlay, so `kube/overlays/dev` now just re-asserts the same values and merges cleanly.

### Validation
- `kubectl kustomize kube/overlays/prod` and `.../dev` both render clean (exit 0); prod shows `maxSurge:1/maxUnavailable:0`, `/tmp` `3Gi`, `ephemeral-storage` `3Gi/5Gi`; `data` unchanged at `1Gi`.
- Server-side dry-run against the live dev cluster: `deployment.apps/paperclip configured` (schema accepted). Only warning is a pre-existing `postgres`-container PodSecurity note, unrelated to this change.

### Deploy gating — IMPORTANT
- **Merge → main** triggers `dev-push.yml` → `_deploy.yml` **for dev only** (`namespace: paperclip-dev`). Dev already runs these exact values (PR #91), so the merge is a safe, zero-downtime re-apply.
- **Prod deploys only on pushing a `v*` tag** (`prod-tag.yml` → `_deploy.yml`, `environment: prod`, `namespace: paperclip`). **This PR does NOT cut a tag.** The production rollout — and thus the post-deploy endpoint verification on `paperclip.mareanalytica.com` — happens when a `v*` release tag is cut, which is the **board/prod-approval gate** per DeepSee prod-change policy.

### Post-deploy verification (to run by whoever cuts the `v*` tag, in the prod cluster)
1. `kubectl -n paperclip rollout status deploy/paperclip` completes without the endpoint going empty.
2. `kubectl -n paperclip get endpoints paperclip -w` stays populated across the rollout.
3. External `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://paperclip.mareanalytica.com/health` → `200` throughout.

No secrets/RBAC/data changes. No replica-count change (HA `replicas:>1` noted in ELI-911 as a larger, separate follow-up).

Closes the prod-hardening ask of **ELI-911** (parent **ELI-903**) once deployed.

body:
## Summary

- **Red Attempt button** in the ticking surface, left of the dynamic Flash/Send button. Fires `useSaveTick` with `status: 'attempt'` regardless of attempt count.
- **Comment field** is back. It was lost when QuickTickBar replaced the long-form log-ascent sheet; multiline `TextInput` now flows into the tick mutation.
- **Consensus grade chip** is centered in `InlineGradePicker` without being preselected. The climb's existing `difficulty` label (already `getGradeLabel(ROUND(display_difficulty))` on the backend) is matched to a `Grade.difficultyId` against the loaded grades list — no new GraphQL field needed.
- **One ticking surface everywhere.** `LogAscentSheet` is now a gorhom `BottomSheet` with a drag handle, pan-down-to-close, and a backdrop, wrapping `QuickTickBar` in `embedded` mode. The long-press FAB, the persistent queue bar's tick action, and the climb detail screen all open the same UI.

## Why the embedded prop

`QuickTickBar` is absolute-positioned + slide-in animated when used inside `PlayDrawer`'s board section. When used as the contents of a real bottom sheet, the parent owns positioning and entrance animation; `embedded={true}` drops the inline chrome so the sheet doesn't fight the bar.

## Centering math

Extracted into `inline-grade-picker-utils.ts` and unit-tested. The previous bug (\"scroll never lands\"):

1. `scrollTo` was being called before the `ScrollView`'s content size was known — native clamps the offset to a zero scrollable range. Fixed by gating on `onContentSizeChange`.
2. The focus chip's measured `x` lived in a ref, so the auto-scroll effect ran once at the wrong time and never re-ran with the real measurement. Fixed by bumping a `focusLayoutTick` state when the focus chip's `onLayout` lands.
3. Fallback path now leaves the gate open so a late chip measurement can still center; only locks once the real measurement was used.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a climb in PlayDrawer, short-press the tick FAB → QuickTickBar slides up inline; grade strip auto-centers on the consensus grade with a subtle primary border, no chip selected.
- [ ] Long-press the tick FAB → same QuickTickBar (no separate sheet).
- [ ] Tap the red **Attempt** button → tick is saved with `status: 'attempt'`. Verify in logbook.
- [ ] Default tries (1) → Save button label reads **Flash**; bump to 2 → flips to **Send**.
- [ ] Type a comment, save, confirm it persists on the tick.
- [ ] Open the tick UI from the persistent queue bar → `LogAscentSheet` opens as a real bottom sheet with handle + backdrop; pan-down dismisses; same Attempt + Save layout inside.

author: geophyai
body:
## Summary

Adds image-method free-surface support to **ElasticVRR** (`elastic_vr2d`),
matching the convention already used by `elastic2d`. Previously the eager path
only re-zeroed the surface stresses (incomplete) and the CUDA path had no
free-surface handling at all.

This is the standard stress-image (method-of-images) free surface for a
first-order momentum–stress scheme — three coupled pieces:

1. **Mirror extension** of fields across the surface row whenever a z-derivative
   stencil reaches above it (`extend_top_free_surface` / `elastic_top_fs_value_2d`).
2. **Per-field parity** — `σzz`, `σxz`, `vz` odd; `vx` even — which encodes the
   traction-free condition into the mirror.
3. **Surface-row projection** `σzz = σxz = 0` each step (`zero_top_row`).

## Changes

- **eager** (`elastic_vrr.py`): image-method z-derivatives for the four
  surface-adjacent z-derivs.
- **CUDA forward** (`elastic_vr2d/kernels.cuh`): `elastic_top_fs_sgradient_z_2d`
  + surface-row zeroing; top PML row released when `free_surface`.
- **CUDA backward** (`kernels.cuh` + `backward.cu`): adjoint image-method
  z-derivatives (`elastic_top_fs_adjoint_sgradient_z_2d`) + an adjoint
  surface-zeroing kernel, wired into all four modes (full / boundary-saving /
  chunk- and recursive-checkpoint).

## Validation

- eager-vs-c forward: rel-L2 **1.3e-6** (free surface on & off)
- gradient consistency vs eager autograd with `free_surface=True`, all 6 model
  params: **cos = 1.0000**, rel-L2 ~1e-6 across full / bs / ckpt-chunk /
  ckpt-recursive
- +4 parametrized free-surface gradient-consistency tests; the existing
  `free_surface=False` suite is unchanged (no regression)

Refs #20

author: cajasmota
body:
Closes #3724 (child of epic #3625).

Extends the Redis key/channel/stream topology template established for Python (#3668) to **C#, PHP, Ruby, and Rust**. Each new `custom_<lang>_redis` extractor pulls the literal key/channel/stream a Redis op touches and emits a `SCOPE.Datastore` keyspace target node (`Datastore:redis:<label>`, deduped per file) plus an access edge — mirroring `internal/custom/python/redis.go` so the data-access graph is cross-language consistent and traversable.

## Langs now emitting Redis key-topology
| Lang | Client | Edges | Keys asserted in tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C#** | StackExchange.Redis | READS_FROM / WRITES_TO / PUBLISHES_TO / SUBSCRIBES_TO | `session:abc`, `user:42`, `user:*` (concat), `session:*` (interp), channel `events`, stream `orders` |
| **PHP** | predis / phpredis | same | `session:abc`, `cfg:flags`, `user:42`, `user:*` (`.`-concat + `"$id"` interp), channel `events`, stream `orders` |
| **Ruby** | redis-rb | same | `session:abc`, `user:42`, `user:*` (`+`-concat + `"#{id}"` interp), `user:#{id}` (single-quote literal), channel `events`, stream `orders` |
| **Rust** | redis-rs | same | `session:abc`, `cfg:flags` (turbofish), `user:42`, channel `events`, stream `orders`, plus `cmd("GET"/"SET"/"PUBLISH").arg(...)` builder |

## Edge direction
- read verbs (get/hget/lrange/xread/…) → `READS_FROM`
- write verbs (set/hset/xadd/del/…) → `WRITES_TO`
- `publish` → `PUBLISHES_TO`, `subscribe`/`psubscribe` → `SUBSCRIBES_TO`

## Honest-partial
Fully-dynamic keys (`db.StringGet(k)`, `$redis->get($k)`, `con.get(format!(...))`) emit the op site flagged `dynamic=true` with **no** fabricated keyspace node or access edge. Each language has a value-asserting negative test for this.

## Records
Re-stamps `lang.{csharp,php,ruby,rust}.driver.redis` `query_attribution` cells `missing → full`, citing the new extractors (reverses the #3635 downgrades). `coverage validate` exits 0 (only pre-existing unrelated warnings); `coverage fmt --check` reports canonical.

## Quality gates
- `go test ./internal/custom/{csharp,php,ruby,rust}/... ./internal/types/ ./tools/coverage/` — green
- `gofmt -l` empty, `go vet` clean on all four packages
- Wiring confirmed: `custom_{csharp,php,ruby,rust}_` prefixes are mapped in `internal/extractors/custom_dispatch.go`; registry-key registration via `init()` auto-dispatches.

author: omarb97
body:
## What

Bounds the `/tmp/dflash_floor.log` recovery diagnostic in `qwen35_backend.cpp`. Replaces the two raw `std::fopen(..., "a")` append sites with an `open_dflash_floor_log()` helper that opens `O_CREAT|O_APPEND|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW`, verifies the fd is a regular file (`S_ISREG`), and truncates once the file passes a 1 MiB cap.

## Why

The production `dflash` lane now runs the stall recovery (`env: DFLASH_MIN_TOKENS=64`, `DFLASH_STALL_TOOL_PREFIX=1`), so the floor-log evidence file is written on every floor/inject event. Without a cap a long-running server could grow it unbounded. This ports the hardening already reviewed on the upstream recovery PR (#315, head `3a06dd4`) into the fork deploy branch so the deployed binary matches it.

## Behavior / safety

- Default lane unaffected: the log is only written when `DFLASH_MIN_TOKENS>0`.
- `O_NOFOLLOW` + `S_ISREG` refuse a symlinked/non-regular `/tmp/dflash_floor.log`; truncation only runs when `O_NOFOLLOW` is available (else it skips logging rather than risk a redirected target).

## Verification

author: theaboutbox
body:
## Problem

The orchestrator exposes two operator-facing env vars that both point at the same orchestrator URL:

- `ORCHESTRATOR_URL` — consumed by the runner's step-reporter (`POST /api/step-report`)
- `RUNNER_CALLBACK_BASE_URL` — used for the runner-result callback (`POST /runner/result`) and run-token minting

They were never meaningfully different. Operators had to set both to the same value, and setting only one left runs silently half-wired (a class of "machine completes but is marked failed" bug).

## Change

Drop `ORCHESTRATOR_URL` from the operator-facing config — the `AppConfig` field, the env read, and the `.env.example` entry. Both dispatch paths now source the runner's `ORCHESTRATOR_URL` env from `RUNNER_CALLBACK_BASE_URL`:

- **fly-machines**: `machineConfig.orchestratorUrl` ← `config.runnerCallbackBaseUrl`
- **local-docker**: the `localOrchestratorUrl` fallback chain uses `runnerCallbackBaseUrl` instead of the removed field

## Runner contract is unchanged

The session still receives an `ORCHESTRATOR_URL` env var (set by `fly-machines.ts` / `local-docker.ts` and read by `run-autonomous.ts`). Only the *operator-facing source* is consolidated — one fewer env var to configure, with no way to half-wire a run.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — 1126 passed (81 files)

author: koriym
body:
## 問題

公開サイトの `https://www.app-state-diagram.com/llms-full.txt` が **404** になっていました。

## 根本原因

master への push ごとに **2つのデプロイパイプラインが並走**しています:

| パイプライン | 内容 | `llms-full.txt` |
|---|---|---|
| **Deploy Jekyll site to Pages**（独自 `jekyll.yml`） | `bin/generate_llms_full.php` を実行してから `_site` をデプロイ | ✅ 生成して含む |
| **pages build and deployment**（GitHub標準のブランチビルド / `dynamic`） | master のソースから直接 Jekyll ビルド | ❌ スクリプト未実行で含まない |

PR #52（`7e338fe`）で `llms-full.txt` を Git 管理から外し「ビルド時生成」に切り替えた際、配信が独自 Actions ワークフロー一本である前提でした。しかし実際には GitHub 標準のブランチビルドも生き残っており、両者が同じ `github-pages` 環境へ競合デプロイします。`llms-full.txt` は `.gitignore` で未追跡のため、**ブランチビルド側の成果物には含まれず**、そのデプロイが勝つと 404 になります。

## 修正

どちらのパイプラインが配信しても確実にファイルが存在するよう、**`llms-full.txt` を Git 管理に戻しました**:

- `.gitignore` から `llms-full.txt` を除外
- 生成済み `llms-full.txt`（`llms.txt` + 英語マニュアル22ファイル, 約152KB）をコミット

CI の生成ステップ（`jekyll.yml`）はそのまま残してあり、Actions 経路ではビルドのたびに最新化されます。

## 推奨（恒久対策・任意）

リポジトリ設定の **Settings → Pages → Source を「GitHub Actions」** に変更すると、ブランチ標準ビルドが停止し独自ワークフロー一本になります。その場合は生成物を追跡せずビルド時生成のみに戻すことも可能です（PR #52 の本来の意図に沿う形）。これはコードでは変更できないため、必要であればリポジトリ設定で対応してください。

author: whamp
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5986.

This removes mipmap generation from the WebGL glyph atlas upload path and explicitly sets non-mipmapped linear filters for atlas pages:

```ts
gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D, gl.TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, gl.LINEAR);
gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D, gl.TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, gl.LINEAR);
```

The goal is to avoid glyph atlas corruption seen in downstream Linux + Wayland WebGL terminals while preserving the WebGL renderer.

## Context

Two downstream applications have hit the same failure class: dense terminal text can turn into black cell blocks, smears, or corrupted glyphs on Linux + Wayland GPU stacks when the WebGL addon is active.

- xterm.js issue: https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5986
- Orca downstream issue: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/1579
- Orca downstream fix: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/1743
- Hermes Agent downstream issue: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/37203
- Hermes Agent downstream workaround PR: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/37205

In the Orca case, Electron/ANGLE logged `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` while allocating mipmaps for generation. Removing `gl.generateMipmap(gl.TEXTURE_2D)` and using explicit non-mipmapped filters resolved the corruption there. The Hermes downstream workaround applies the same change to its installed `@xterm/addon-webgl` package.

I have not reduced this to a standalone xterm.js demo repro; it appears GPU/driver/backend-specific. This PR is intentionally narrow so the exact WebGL state change can be reviewed directly.

## Testing

Ran in a clean `/tmp/xterm.js-pr` checkout to avoid parent-directory `node_modules` pollution:

- `npm ci`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint-changes`
- `npm run setup`
- `npm run test-unit` — 2367 passing
- Started the demo with `PORT=3310 npm start`
- Built the demo client with `npm run esbuild-demo-client`
- Loaded `http://127.0.0.1:3310/` in Chromium and opened the `webgl` panel; confirmed the page loaded and a WebGL2 canvas was present
- Verified the built demo bundle contains `TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER` / `TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER` and no `generateMipmap`

## Notes

The repository contribution guide asks for tests when changes are easy to test or likely to regress. I did not add a new automated test because this failure is GPU/driver-specific and the existing unit test surface does not directly exercise browser WebGL texture state. The focused build, lint, unit test suite, and demo smoke test are included above.

author: lunchbox951
body:
## Why
Stage 1 of the `co` v1 self-host build: land **L0 Foundations** — the persistence substrate every later
layer stands on — by promoting the reviewed `dev` integration branch to `main`.

## What changed
**L0 (roadmap layer; operator-locked spec):** new `packages/core/src/{store,replay,registry,config}/`
- **Store** over Node's built-in `node:sqlite` (zero runtime dependency) behind a narrow **synchronous
  `Store` interface**; append-only **global-`seq` event log = source of truth** + projection tables in the
  same db file (append + projection commit in one transaction). Node floor raised to **24** (node:sqlite
  unflagged), `.nvmrc` + CI updated, no `ExperimentalWarning`.
- **Projections + replay**: drop-and-replay rebuildable cache; per-event `v` + **payload upcaster
  registry**; deterministic replay (all time from the persisted `ts`, never wall-clock).
- **Project registry** (in the global store): absolute path → **opaque, path-independent id** → data
  dir; **headless relink** after a move preserves the id + full event history (append-only index update).
- **Config cascade**: `effective = global ⊕ project-overrides`, resolved from program-data **only**; a
  reusable **pristine-repo guard harness** wraps every public op (nothing is written into the target repo).

This promotion also catches `main` up with prior **reviewed** `dev` work not yet promoted (vitest 4 bump,
dev-tooling/Actions updates, the `dev`→`main` CI promotion policy).

## Verification
- `pnpm lint / typecheck / build` green; **73 tests** across 13 files; zero `ExperimentalWarning`.
- All six layer criteria met (**AC-L0-1..6**); every change reached `dev` through a gated **PASS** review.
- Advances v1 acceptance criteria **ST-1** (everything is an event), **ST-2** (recoverable from its own
  record), **WT-3** (pristine repo — orchestration state in program-data); foundation for **SH-2**, **SH-4**.

## Conventions
TypeScript monorepo (pnpm workspaces, ESM/NodeNext `.js` specifiers), strict TS with `assertNever`,
logic in `@co/core` with thin `cli`/`mcp` adapters, Conventional Commits + DCO sign-off. Promotion is
gated (`co pr-merge`), per the `dev`→`main` policy.
