body:
## 做了什么
带仓库的本地任务卡在工具授权（permission prompt）时，卡片指示灯转黄，提示「等待你授权」；工具执行 / 用户回复 / 回合结束后自动转回绿色。

## 怎么实现的
走 **Claude Code hooks**（比读屏更稳）。派发时往 worktree 的 `.claude/settings.local.json` 注入 hook，由 session 自己上报状态：

| 事件 | 上报 | 灯色 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Notification(permission_prompt)` | `POST /hook/wait` | 🟡 黄 |
| `PostToolUse` / `UserPromptSubmit` / `Stop` | `POST /hook/clear` | 🟢 绿 |

意图编码在 URL 里，服务端不必解析版本相关的 hook payload。

## 变更
- `server/hooks.ts`：生成 `settings.local.json`，hook 命令带 `-m 2` 超时且恒 `|| true`，永不拖慢/失败 session
- `server/hooks.test.ts`：单测 3 例（matcher / wait+clear url / 永不失败）
- `POST /api/tasks/:id/hook/:state` 收上报，`taskWaiting`(Map) 内存记账；`GET /api/tasks` 输出 `waiting` 字段；archive / cleanup / delete 时清理
- 仅**本地机器仓库任务**注入（hook curl `localhost:PORT`，只在本机可达；远端任务不亮灯、不报错，即 v1 范围）
- 注入文件写入 `.git/info/exclude`，**不污染 `git status`**（隔离仓库验证：写入后 `git status --porcelain` 为空）
- 前端：`alive+waiting` → `.sdot.waiting` 琥珀黄灯；i18n 补 zh/en

- `node --test` 11/11 绿（hooks 3 + schema 3 + local 5）
- 源码 `tsc --noEmit` 零报错（仅既有 `.test.ts` 的 `.ts`-import 约定告警，tsx 运行时不受影响）

author: nixidexiangjiao
body:
## Description

The env-based retrieval path (`RETRIEVE_DRIVER=milvus`) previously passed a
hard-coded `nil` IndexConfig into the Milvus repository, so collections were
always created/loaded with the Milvus server defaults (shard=1, replica=1).
Shard and replica counts could only be customized through the DB-store
(`vector_stores`) path, which is not wired into the knowledge-base creation UI.

This PR lets operators tune those two values directly from environment
variables on the env path:

- `MILVUS_SHARDS_NUM` — number of shards per collection (`CreateCollection`), range 1–64
- `MILVUS_REPLICA_NUMBER` — in-memory replica count (`LoadCollection`), range 1–10

Behavior:
- New `IndexConfigFromEnv()` parses both variables, validates their range, and
  returns `nil` when neither is set to a valid value — preserving the previous
  default behavior (full backward compatibility).
- Invalid / out-of-range / non-numeric values are logged and ignored rather than
  failing startup.
- `container.go` now passes `IndexConfigFromEnv()` instead of `nil` on the
  Milvus env path.
- `scripts/dev.sh` no longer unconditionally overrides `MILVUS_ADDRESS`; it now
  honors a value from `.env` (`${MILVUS_ADDRESS:-localhost:19530}`) so external
  Milvus clusters can be reached in local dev.
- `.env.example` documents the two new variables.

Note (Milvus semantics): `MILVUS_SHARDS_NUM` only applies when a collection is
first created — Milvus does not allow changing shard count on an existing
collection. `MILVUS_REPLICA_NUMBER` is applied on load.

## Type of Change
- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change
- [ ] 📚 Documentation update
- [ ] 🎨 Refactor
- [ ] ⚡ Performance improvement
- [ ] 🧪 Test
- [x] 🔧 Configuration / Build / CI

## Related Issue
N/A

## Testing
- `go build ./...` passes.
- `go test ./internal/application/repository/retriever/milvus/` — 9/9 pass.

author: gavinmcfall
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2094. PR #2094 exposed licence-gate :8000 at Cilium LB IP 10.99.8.216 so workers could POST `/distributed/job_complete` back to master — but the existing NetworkPolicy `lighthouse-only-from-envoy` only allows port 8000 ingress from Envoy Gateway pods. Worker LAN traffic to 10.99.8.216:8000 was **denied at the NetworkPolicy layer** even though the LB allocated correctly.

**Smoking gun (after #2094 deployed):** `curl http://10.99.8.216:8000/distributed/system_info` from VengeancePC hangs forever (no SYN-ACK because NetworkPolicy drops at pod ingress).

## Change

Add a new ingress rule allowing worker LAN subnet `10.90.101.0/24` on port 8000, mirroring the existing pattern for port 9090 (model-serve).

## Security posture

With this change there are TWO authorized sources to licence-gate :8000:

1. **Envoy Gateway** — OIDC-verified family/browser identities (unchanged)
2. **Worker LAN subnet** — brand-bearer-token-validated worker callbacks (new)

The decode-not-verify JWT pattern still relies on Envoy for family identities — worker LAN ingress carries `LIGHTHOUSE_DR_TOKEN` Bearer which the proxy validates via `crypto/subtle` constant-time compare. Two distinct auth modes, two distinct ingress paths.

Verified worker IPs are in this subnet (vengeance: 10.90.101.86, vixen: 10.90.101.79).

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge → Flux reconciles → NetworkPolicy updated
- [ ] From VengeancePC: `curl http://10.99.8.216:8000/distributed/system_info` returns `{"status": "success", ...}`
- [ ] Re-run smoke; render dispatches; callback succeeds; file at `/app/output/dopamine-racing/workshop-sdxl_*.png`

author: mcbeebe
body:
## Summary

**This is the cutover commit.** Merging triggers the workflow that orphan-force-pushes the standalone airlock to `mcbeebe.github.io/Broken-Arrow-Training/`. From that moment, any visit to a legacy URL collects the user's `ba_*` localStorage, transfers it to `attune.coach` via a postMessage popup, unregisters the legacy service worker, clears caches, and forwards the user to attune.coach preserving `?view=` and `#athleteId`.

### What this PR does

- **`deploy.yml`**: removes the `build-and-deploy` job (the legacy Vite app deploy) and replaces it with `cutover-airlock`, which copies `scripts/airlock/{index.html,404.html}` and publishes to `gh-pages` with `force_orphan: true` so the old app's history is gone.
- **`scripts/airlock/index.html`**: tightened the popup-blocked fallback. The previous "your data will move when you sign in" message was misleading. Now the fallback offers a real "Try again" button (the user click counts as a gesture and unblocks the popup on retry) plus a "Download backup" button that produces the same JSON payload the `MigrationReceive` component already accepts via file upload.

### Witchel 3-rule check

1. **Massive market** — every existing user who ever visits the old URL goes through this; nothing else affects them more.
2. **Visceral solve** — they hit an old bookmark, see "Bringing your training history with you…" for two seconds, land on attune.coach with everything intact. The friction this removes is "I'm going to lose my history" anxiety.
3. **Customer language** — UI says "training history" not "localStorage payload", "Download backup" not "JSON export", "Continue without my data" not "abort migration".

### Verification after merge

1. Wait ~2 min for the workflow to publish.
2. Open `https://mcbeebe.github.io/Broken-Arrow-Training/` in a browser with seeded `ba_*` localStorage. Should: brief "Bringing your training history…" screen, popup opens to `attune.coach/?__migrate=1`, popup closes, you land on `https://attune.coach/` with localStorage populated.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a browser-based interactive documentation app that renders a fake terminal using xterm.js as the display surface and Blazor WebAssembly for command processing. No backend, no OS access, no WebSocket, no node-pty — everything runs client-side as static files deployable to GitHub Pages.

### Fake shell engine (`Terminal/`)
- `FakeShell` — processes raw keyboard input, dispatches commands, handles backspace/Ctrl+C
- `ITerminalCommand` / `ITerminalOutput` — clean interfaces for testability
- Commands: `help`, `clear`, `components`, `about`, `demo <component>`
- `demo` subcommands render ANSI previews: `button`, `table`, `tree`, `box`, `chart`, `spinner`, `calendar`, `text`

### xterm.js integration
- TypeScript module (`wwwroot/terminal/terminal.ts`) bundled with Vite into a single ES module
- Exposes `initTerminal`, `write`, `writeln`, `clear`, `focus`, `fit`
- Keyboard input forwarded to .NET via `DotNetObjectReference.invokeMethodAsync("OnTerminalData", data)`
- FitAddon + WebLinksAddon, ResizeObserver for auto-fit
- CSS from npm, no CDN dependency
- `XtermInterop.cs` wraps the JS module as `ITerminalOutput`

### Blazor WASM app (`docs/TermBlade.Docs.Wasm/`)
- Standalone Blazor WASM (SDK `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BlazorWebAssembly`), references `TermBlade.Core`
- `/terminal` page wires up xterm.js ↔ FakeShell
- Dark theme (Tokyo Night palette), `Cascadia Code` / `Fira Code` font stack

### GitHub Pages workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-docs-wasm.yml`)
- `npm ci` → `vite build` → `dotnet publish` → `upload-pages-artifact`
- Rewrites `<base href>` for repo subpath, adds `.nojekyll` + `404.html` for SPA routing
- Triggers on push to `main` (docs or core changes) + `workflow_dispatch`

### What's NOT changed
- TermBlade.Core — zero modifications, no new xterm.js dependency
- All 184 existing tests pass, format check clean

author: cachenat
body:
Introduces `core/remote_control.py` — a lightweight REST API server
(stdlib only, no new dependencies) that runs in a background daemon
thread alongside the GUI when started with `--remote-control [PORT]`.

Endpoints (all require X-API-Key header except /health):
  GET  /api/v1/health        – liveness probe
  GET  /api/v1/status        – interface, scan state, network counts
  GET  /api/v1/networks      – discovered WEP/WPA access points
  GET  /api/v1/database      – cracked-key database entries
  POST /api/v1/scan/start    – start airodump-ng {"interface":"wlan0mon"}
  POST /api/v1/scan/stop     – stop airodump-ng

A random API key is generated per session and printed to stdout on
startup. `execute.py` gains a `--remote-control [PORT]` flag (default
port 8765) that wires the server to the live monitor interface.

## 📝 변경 사항
`development` 브랜치에 변경이 머지될 때마다 GitHub Actions가 자동으로 빌드하여
GitHub Pages(`gh-pages` 브랜치)에 배포하는 **미리보기 인프라**를 추가합니다.
별도 서버 없이 누구나 다음 URL에서 최신 UI 상태를 바로 확인할 수 있습니다.

의존성 추가도 없습니다 (`package.json` 변경 없음).

| # | 커밋 | 영역 | 핵심 변경 |
|---|------|------|-----------|
| 1 | `feat: development push 시 gh-pages 자동 배포 워크플로우 추가` | CI/CD | `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` 신규 |
| 2 | `feat: Vite base와 React Router basename을 BASE_URL 기준으로 분리` | 빌드·라우터 | `DEPLOY_TARGET=gh-pages`일 때만 `base: '/sejong_market_front/'` 적용 |
| 3 | `feat: GitHub Pages SPA 새로고침 및 딥링크 404 폴백 추가` | SPA 호환 | `public/404.html` + `index.html` 인라인 스크립트 (rafgraph/spa-github-pages 방식) |
| 4 | `fix: mock 상품 이미지 절대경로에 BASE_URL prefix 적용` | mock 데이터 | `productConstants.js`의 `/products/*.png` → `asset('products/...')` |
| 5 | `docs: GitHub Pages 미리보기 안내 및 gh-pages 브랜치 규정 추가` | 문서 | README 미리보기 섹션, CONTRIBUTING 6장 금지사항 #7 + 7장 신설 |
### 동작 흐름
누군가 feature/* → development 머지 ↓ GitHub Actions 트리거 (deploy-pages.yml) ↓ npm ci → DEPLOY_TARGET=gh-pages npm run build ↓ peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4 가 dist/ 를 gh-pages 브랜치에 force-push ↓ GitHub Pages 1~2분 안에 갱신

로컬에서 `DEPLOY_TARGET=gh-pages npm run build` 로 GH Pages 모드 빌드를 검증했습니다.

body:
Two related Home/recurring fixes from the same feedback thread.

## 1. Remove the "Upcoming bills" card
The always-on list dominated the Home screen and wasn't wanted. Removed it; the actionable **due-today card** (Paid / Skip / Snooze) stays.

## 2. "Every N days" bills are now due on their start day
A custom-interval bill computed its first due date as **start + interval**, so a Jio recharge set to *"every 80 days"* starting today was first due in **80 days** — it never showed on Home with Paid/Skip when added, even though the user had just paid it.

Now the **first occurrence (no payment/skip yet) is the start date itself**, so a freshly-added "every N days" bill shows as **due today** and can be confirmed. Tapping **Paid** anchors the next due to that payment + interval (e.g. +80 days), and it reminds again then.

- `getRecurringDueDate`, `isRecurringDueToday`, and `billReminders` updated to match.
- This only changes **custom / every-N-days** bills; monthly and yearly are untouched.

- `npm run lint` — 0 errors / 14 warnings (baseline)
- `npm run typecheck` — clean

## After deploying
Your existing Jio recharge (every 80 days, started today) will show on Home as **due today** with Paid/Skip. Tap **Paid** to confirm today's recharge — it'll then remind you again in ~80 days.

The demo now speaks all five World Cup languages Granite supports (EN/ES/FR/PT/DE). Five-language toggle, per-language captions + aria-labels, and the `aria-live` region's `lang` attribute flips so the screen reader picks the right voice.

**Granite robustness:** greedy decoding occasionally echoed the prompt scaffolding on non-English runs (caught on Portuguese). The retry loop now rejects prompt-leak markers and falls back to a per-language deterministic floor (EN/ES/FR/PT/DE), so the demo never shows leaked prompt — or English for a non-English request.

Shows VARSITY's lead over the live TV picture: the **~20s over-the-air broadcast offset** (Phenix / Stats Perform real-time latency study) **minus VARSITY's own live-measured trigger→verdict latency**. ## Verified (live, Playwright + watsonx)
- 5 language buttons render; EN streams; switching to FR re-explains in French (`lang` flips `en`→`fr`).
- PT/FR/DE come back **in-language with no prompt leak** across repeated runs.

body:
## What this does

When the nightly "Backup Formance to Supabase" job failed, the run log showed only:

```
Backup script failed. See backup-error.log.
Error: Process completed with exit code 1
```

…and nothing about *why*. The script's error output was redirected into `backup-error.log` and only uploaded as an artifact, which has to be downloaded separately to read. On a phone (or anywhere) you just saw "failed, no reason."

This prints the captured error output straight to the job log on failure (with a `::error::` annotation), in both the backup and restore workflows, while still uploading the artifact. The real reason now appears inline in the run.

## Context — the backup itself is now working

The actual cause of the repeated failures was a missing / too-old `pg_dump` on the runner, fixed in #271 (install the PostgreSQL 17 client). I dispatched this branch's backup workflow against the live secrets to confirm: it succeeded — `pg_dump` ran, the dump uploaded to Supabase, and the script's upload verification passed (run 26804884979, all steps green, the failure-log upload step skipped because there was no failure).

This PR is the follow-up so that if a backup ever fails again, the reason is visible immediately instead of hidden.

author: forestdragon-wesnoth
body:
## Summary

One PR, three coupled feature changes plus a test-harness fix that was overdue.

### 1. Statuses rework: `Set[str]` → `Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]`

Per the "what X does is stored in X" rule, each status carries its own data dict. `!ent status` gained `set`/`del`/`info` subcommands (dotted paths). `_parse_scalar` coerces literal `true`/`false` to bool (case-sensitive; `yes`/`no` stay strings). Save/load preserves the dict shape and bool types.

### 2. `skip_turn_statuses` rule **removed** → per-status `skips_turn` field

The engine recognizes one convention on status data: `skips_turn: true` skips the bearer's turn. No global name-list rule; each status declares its own behavior.

### 3. Status auto-tick — GM-configurable, no hardcoded fields

`status_tick_when` (enum `never`/`turn_start`/`turn_end`/`round_start`/`round_end`) + `status_tick_formula` (runs once per `(entity, status)` with `self`/`this`/`status_name` bound). No hardcoded `remaining` — the GM's formula decides what to decrement and when to clear.

### 4. Constrained `for` loops in formulas

`for x in <call>:` / `for (a, b) in <call>:` where `<call>` is one of `entities_within`, `group_members`, `cells_in_burst`, `cells_in_line`, `cells_in_cone`. Bounded by `formula_loop_limit` (default 10000) via a transformer-injected `__loop_tick()`.

### Supporting infrastructure

- New formula functions: `group_members(name)` + the seven `status_*` accessors (mirror `tile_*`).
- Bare `self`/`this`/`current` identifiers now bind to string ids (or None unbound), so `status_set(self, status_name, ...)` reads cleanly.

## NEW: committed scenario runner (`run_scenarios.py`)

There was no committed harness — verification used throwaway inline scripts that only caught 💥 crashes. And `test_sequences.txt` writes multi-line formulas as the two-char escape `\n` (to keep each command on one physical line for the line-oriented parser), which **nothing un-escaped** — so shlex saw a literal backslash-n, the formula failed to parse, and the eval/passive silently errored. The real bot never hits this (Discord/CLI carry real newlines), so **~35 scenarios** (every if/elif body, every multi-line passive) were silently not running what their prose described.

The runner:
- takes command lines only **above** the `Expected:` marker (so prose lines starting with `!` aren't mistaken for commands — a perennial false-positive)
- converts `\n`/`\t` to real characters **before** shlex, reproducing what the command layer receives
- flags **💥** (uncaught exceptions) and **"Syntax error"** (formula parse failures — the sandbox's *intentional* rejections never look like a Python "Syntax error")
- CLI: run all / specific numbers / `--list` / `-v`; nonzero exit on failure

**Full run: 245 scenarios, 0 flagged failures.**

## Scenario fixes surfaced by actually running them

- **#174**: `!eval random_int("not", "int")` — shlex strips the inner quotes from an unquoted eval → `random_int(not, int)` → Python keyword `not` → "Syntax error", never testing the intended path. Wrapped in outer quotes; now correctly yields "lo must be int".
- **#10**: if/elif/revive evals never ran before. Now they do — but `!ent add hero Hero 30` auto-fills `max_hp=30`, so the `hp ≤ max_hp` clamp pinned branches setting hp above 30. Prose was written as if unclamped. Set `max_hp=100` up front; corrected prose (elif→50, revive→100).
- **#121**: retitled "Disallowed: loops" → "Loops are constrained" — `for` over a loopable builtin is now legal; only `while` is fully disallowed and `for` over a non-loopable iterable is rejected.
- **#11 / #221**: prose (and #221's bad-body command) updated so the for-loop rejection cases describe the new "iterable must be a loopable builtin call" reason.

## Test scenarios

- **#40 / #237** narration updated for dict-of-dicts; **#240 REPLACED** (was `skip_turn_statuses` rule; now per-status `skips_turn`).
- **#241–248** added: status set/del/info; remove vs clear; `status_*` functions; round_end auto-tick decay (full trace verified); `skips_turn`+tick together (stunned wears off); for-loop AOE damage; iterable validation + loop limit; `group_members` + tuple-unpack loops.

## Note on the pre-existing `\n` issue

The harness fix means the multi-line scenarios execute for the first time. I verified #10 thoroughly and spot-checked the passive DOT/duration scenarios (#57 poison decay 25→21→18, #60/#76 passives now register and fire). They were silently inert before. If any of the remaining multi-line scenarios have stale prose values (like #10's clamp case), the runner will keep running them clean — they just need prose touch-ups as noticed; I fixed the clear cases.

author: johnramberger
body:
## Problem

Signing in to a source with **"Login with Google"** (e.g. Cale, which auths via Patreon) ended on a **blank white screen**.

Cause: the account chooser opens in a `window.open` popup. The login WebView didn't enable multiple-window support and had no `onCreateWindow` handler, so the popup window was created by the engine but never attached to the view tree — nothing rendered, and there was no opener context to complete the sign-in.

## Fix

- Enable `setSupportMultipleWindows(true)` + `javaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically`.
- Handle `WebChromeClient.onCreateWindow`: build a child WebView, hand it to the `WebViewTransport`, and **overlay it** on top of the main WebView. Keeping it as a real child window preserves `window.opener` / `postMessage`, which is what lets the provider finish the OAuth handshake.
- `window.close()` (via `onCloseWindow`) and the system back button dismiss the popup.
- Login-success detection also runs on the popup, so a redirect that lands there still finishes the flow.
- Debug-only (`BuildConfig.DEBUG`) logging of page lifecycle + load errors for future diagnosis.

## Verified

Built and run on emulator (Pixel 9 Pro XL, API 35). Drove the Cale → Login with Google flow: the popup now renders instead of a white screen and the WebView reaches the signed-in `patreon.com/home`, completing login. Logcat (`SourceLogin` tag) confirms page lifecycle with no popup-related errors.

author: cyprien-bussy
body:
## Summary

memhook v0.2: adds the three deferred v0.1 non-goals — an **OpenAI provider**, a
local **Ollama provider**, and an optional **YAML config file** — behind a
clean, provider-agnostic abstraction. Fully backward-compatible: an existing
env-only Anthropic setup behaves exactly as before, and `api.anthropic.com`
stays the only default outbound call.

## Changes

- **Provider-agnostic interface** — `apiKey` is now optional and the
  Anthropic-only `betaHeaders` / `cacheControlTtl` moved off the shared
  `SelectionRequest` into `AnthropicProviderOptions`, so OpenAI/Ollama adapters
  never see Anthropic-isms.
- **`src/providers/http.ts`** — one shared `fetch` transport (AbortController
  timeout + single retry) so the fail-soft network path is audited in one place.
- **`OpenAIProvider`** — Chat Completions, `Authorization: Bearer`, catalog as
  the leading system message (engages OpenAI auto prompt-caching), usage mapped
  to the normalised shape. Default `gpt-4o-mini`.
- **`OllamaProvider`** — native `/api/chat`, no API key, `stream:false`, 30s
  default timeout for cold model loads. Default `llama3.1`.
- **`createProvider` factory** — selects the adapter from `provider.type` with
  compile-time `never` exhaustiveness.
- **YAML config** — opt-in (`$MEMHOOK_CONFIG` or `~/.config/memhook/config.yaml`),
  precedence `env > yaml > default`. YAML I/O is isolated in `configFile.ts`
  (never throws), and every consumed field is type-narrowed at the reader
  boundary so a malformed/wrong-typed file can never crash the hook.
- **Cache key** now includes provider identity (`type:model`) so switching
  provider/model never serves a stale selection.
- **`yaml`** is the first runtime dependency (zero sub-dependencies).
- Version centralised in `src/version.ts` (was duplicated in `config.ts` + `bin/`).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes

💡 What: Replaced direct `Math.sqrt()` calls in the canvas animation node interactions with fast bounding box checks and squared distance comparisons.
🎯 Why: In O(N^2) loops (like node connections) and O(N) loops (mouse interaction), `Math.sqrt()` is called for every pair, causing a massive performance bottleneck. The vast majority of nodes are too far apart to interact.
📊 Impact: Exponential reduction in expensive mathematical calculations, significantly improving rendering frame rate, battery life, and overall responsiveness of the NeuralBackground canvas.
🔬 Measurement: Can be verified by running performance profiling in browser dev tools on the canvas frame rate before and after this change.

author: ruvnet
body:
## Nightly Research: MinCut-Guided Agent Working Memory Compaction

Adds `crates/ruvector-mincut-memory` — a graph-cut guided agent memory compaction
primitive that answers the question every long-running AI agent faces:
**when memory is full, what should be forgotten?**

### Includes

1. Working Rust PoC: `crates/ruvector-mincut-memory` (18 tests, 0 failures)
2. ADR: `docs/adr/ADR-196-mincut-memory-compaction.md`
3. Research document: `docs/research/nightly/2026-06-02-mincut-memory-compaction/README.md`
4. Public gist source: `docs/research/nightly/2026-06-02-mincut-memory-compaction/gist.md`
5. Real benchmark results (two dataset sizes, all strategies PASS)

### Three strategies, one trait

```rust
pub trait Compactor {
    fn compact(&self, store: &mut MemoryStore, target_size: usize) -> CompactionResult;
}
```

| Strategy | Eviction criterion | Graph insight |
|---|---|---|
| AgeEvict | Oldest by timestamp | None (baseline) |
| CoherenceEvict | Lowest mean edge weight | Local neighbourhood |
| **MinCutEvict** | **Lowest weighted degree** | **Global cut boundary** |

### Real benchmark results

Hardware: x86-64 Linux 6.18 · Intel Celeron N4020 · rustc 1.94.1

**N=500, D=32, 50% compaction:**

| Strategy | Recall_b | Recall_a | Mean µs | Edges_a | Accept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AgeEvict | 1.000 | 1.000 | 6 340 | 1 955 | PASS |
| CoherenceEvict | 1.000 | 0.980 | 6 807 | 3 114 | PASS |
| **MinCutEvict** | **1.000** | **1.000** | **6 562** | **3 629** | **PASS** |

**N=1000, D=64, 50% compaction:**

| Strategy | Recall_b | Recall_a | Mean µs | Edges_a | Accept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AgeEvict | 1.000 | 1.000 | 51 859 | 759 | PASS |
| CoherenceEvict | 1.000 | 1.000 | 53 392 | 1 420 | PASS |
| **MinCutEvict** | **1.000** | **1.000** | **53 056** | **2 026** | **PASS** |

MinCutEvict retains **2.67x more graph edges** than AgeEvict at N=1,000.

### Ecosystem connections

- `ruvector-mincut` — theoretical basis
- `ruvector-graph` — graph storage integration path
- `mcp-gate` — MCP `memory_compact` tool (next step)
- `rvAgent/rvagent-mcp` — agent integration
- `ruvector-verified` — witness log per compaction (next step)
- ruFlo — scheduled compaction workflow (next step)

### Run it

```bash
git checkout research/nightly/2026-06-02-mincut-memory-compaction
cargo build --release -p ruvector-mincut-memory
cargo test -p ruvector-mincut-memory
cargo run --release -p ruvector-mincut-memory
```

body:
## Summary

Every `SqlConnection` in the codebase was created with `New` and closed with an explicit `.Close()` — any exception (or `Response.Redirect`'s `ThreadAbortException`) between Open/Close leaked the connection. Errors from DB operations propagated as unhandled yellow-screen exceptions instead of user-facing messages.

### Changes

**`Login.aspx.vb`**
- Wrap `SqlConnection`/`SqlCommand` in `Using` blocks so connections are always disposed.
- `Response.Redirect("Dashboard.aspx", False)` — avoids `ThreadAbortException` that skipped `con.Close()`.
- Guard against missing `"DBCS"` connection string.
- `Try/Catch SqlException` → shows `"A database error occurred…"` on `lblMsg` + `Trace.TraceError`.

**`Employees.aspx.vb`**
- Extract shared `ConnectionString` property with null-safe access on `ConfigurationManager.ConnectionStrings("DBCS")`.
- `Session("role").ToString()` → null-guarded: `If role Is Nothing OrElse …` — prevents `NullReferenceException` when session expires.
- `ViewState("Count")` → `If(ViewState("Count") IsNot Nothing, CInt(…), 0)` — safe fallback.
- `btnSave_Click`, `LoadEmployees`, `gvEmployees_RowUpdating`, `gvEmployees_RowDeleting`: all wrapped in `Using` + `Try/Catch` with specific `SqlException` / `InvalidCastException` handlers and user-facing `lblMsg` feedback.
- Auth redirect uses `endResponse:=False`.

author: popstas
body:
## Summary

Overhauls progress reporting so the desktop GUI bar and remote streaming reflect real pipeline work instead of jumping or stalling. Each pipeline stage now maps onto stable GUI percentage bands, the bar is kept monotonic so an encoder GPU→CPU fallback can't make it regress, and audio processing reports genuine progress instead of a synthetic timer.

## Changes

- **Real audio-processing progress** — `audio.py`/`pipeline.py` emit actual progress during phase-vocoder processing; the synthetic audio timer stops once real updates arrive.
- **Stable GUI bands** — `gui/progress.py` defines `STAGE_PROGRESS_RANGES` and `map_stage_progress()` to map each remote stage onto fixed percentage bands (Uploading 0–5%, Extracting audio 5–20%, Audio processing 20–35%, Generating final 35–100%).
- **Monotonic bar** — `_set_progress_monotonic()` clamps each value against `_progress_floor` so the bar never moves backwards; `_reset_progress_baseline()` re-bases the floor per file in a batch.
- **Remote upload progress** — `gui/remote.py` and `service_client.py` expose and normalize upload progress; the server logs received upload filename and size.
- **Log-only milestones** — parse `Task: NN%` milestones from logs as a progress channel.

author: drian320
body:
## 背景
画面が静止しているときも、ほぼ目標ビットレートを消費し続けていた。原因は全 HEVC エンコーダバックエンドが **CBR(固定ビットレート)** で動いており、CBR はフレームがほぼ変化しなくても目標レートを維持するためパディング/画質向上でビットを使い切るため。

## 変更
全バックエンドを **Capped VBR** へ切り替え。VBR は目標レートを狙うが**パディングしない**ため、静止時は出力がゼロ方向に下がり、ピークは既存の max ビットレートでキャップされる。ビットレート値は据え置き、**RCモードのみ変更**。

| バックエンド | 変更 |
|---|---|
| ネイティブNVENC (`config.rs`/`encoder.rs`) | `NV_ENC_PARAMS_RC_CBR` → `_VBR` |
| media-win FFmpeg 8bit / Main10 | dict `rc=cbr` → `vbr` |
| `prdt-media-ffmpeg` nvenc 8bit / Main10 | dict `rc=cbr` → `vbr`(+テスト更新) |
| Media Foundation | `eAVEncCommonRateControlMode` CBR(0) → PeakConstrainedVBR(1)。既存 Mean + Max(+20%) を VBR 上限として流用 |

vaapi(`rc_mode=CBR`, Linux)は対象外で据え置き。

## CIガード
MF のレート制御は `mf/encoder.rs` 全体バイト同一性凍結 `[1,603]` の内側にあるため、`check-8bit-helpers-byte-identity.py` の凍結範囲を `[1,359]` + `[401,603]` に分割し、`configure_rate_control` の RCブロック(master 行360-400)をレビュー済み例外として除外(`renegotiate_output_type` 前例に倣う)。ファイルは603行のまま。

## 検証
- ✅ `python3 scripts/check-8bit-helpers-byte-identity.py` PASS(分割後の範囲で通過)
- ✅ `cargo fmt --all` クリーン
- ⚠️ media-ffmpeg nvenc テストは dev container の ffmpeg バージョン不一致(8 vs 固定6/7)でローカル実行不可 → **本PRのCIで検証**
- ⚠️ media-win(NVENC/MF/FFmpeg)は Windows専用でローカルビルド不可 → **CI windows-latest で検証**

## ⚠️ レビュー時の注意 / マージ前確認事項
1. **MF の CBR→PeakConstrainedVBR が最もリスクが高い**。ハードウェアMFT依存で、元コメントは「明示RCモードを置かないと品質モードでIDRが~9倍暴発」と警告していた。mode 1 は MaxBitRate でキャップされるため暴発しない想定だが、**実Windows機での帯域・画質確認を推奨**。
2. **アイドルはゼロにはならない**:GOP=60(毎秒IDR)は本PRでは未変更のため、静止時も毎秒1枚のキーフレーム分は残る。さらに下げる場合は無限GOP化 / カーソルのみスキップが追加レバー。
3. NVENC は `averageBitRate == maxBitRate == 設定値`。ドライバによっては VBR でも CBR寄りになり得る。アイドルをさらに攻める場合は averageBitRate を max より下げるのが次の調整ノブ。

author: peterponyu
body:
## What

Replaces the fixed **random Gaussian projection** "encoder" with a **genuinely trained** factor model — graph-regularized NMF (GNMF) implemented in **pure numpy** (no torch, no scipy at runtime).

`src/factorgraph_st/model/learned.py`:
- `fit_gnmf(X, edges, n_factors, *, lam, n_iter, tol, seed)` minimizes
  `||X - H @ W.T||_F² + lam·Tr(Hᵀ L H)` over `H, W ≥ 0` via the standard GNMF multiplicative updates, where `L = D − A` is the **unnormalized Laplacian** of the spatial kNN graph. Adjacency is applied as a scatter-add, so the n×n matrix is never materialized.
- `fit_transform_gnmf(...)` packages the fit into the existing `FactorGraphOutputs` contract (column-partition split into `Z_shared`/`Z_private`, loadings re-gauged via the shared decoder helper).

**Why this fixes the gap (Refs #181, #199):**
- **Spatial coherence is LEARNED** via the graph Laplacian regularizer — coordinates are *never* baked into the feature matrix.
- **Domains are clustered on the factor scores `H` alone** (not `[H | coords]`), so `morans_i_domain` is no longer high by construction.
- **Deterministic**: same seed → bitwise-identical `H`, `W`.

## Opt-in wiring (defaults preserved)

`scripts/run_real_factorgraph.py` gains `--model {projection,gnmf}`, **defaulting to `projection`**. The existing projection run + all its tests are **byte-for-byte unchanged** (every new branch is gated behind `--model gnmf`). On the `gnmf` path: `interpretability.model_is_learned=true`, domains clustered on `H` alone, the Moran's permutation null is still emitted for honesty, and the objective trace + `lam` are recorded.

## Learning tests (tiny-synthetic, numpy-only CI — no real training)

`tests/test_learned.py` (fails-to-exist on `origin/main` → `ImportError`; passes with this fix):
- **determinism** — same seed → identical fit.
- **objective decreases monotonically** — non-increasing trace; `obj[-1] < obj[0]`.
- **beats projection on factor recovery** — GNMF `matched_factor_correlation` > projection on planted nonnegative spatial factors.
- **beats projection on domain ARI** — GNMF domain ARI > projection.
- **contract** — outputs satisfy `validate_outputs`.

Measured on the planted-spatial instance (12×12 grid, 3 elongated-stripe domains):

| metric | GNMF (`lam=1`) | random projection |
|---|---|---|
| matched_factor_correlation | **0.9999** | 0.6928 |
| domain ARI vs planted | **1.0000** | 0.5493 |
| objective | 1795.3 → 6.8 (monotone ↓) | — |

## Scope / follow-up

This lands the **trained model + opt-in wiring + synthetic learning tests**. The **real-DLPFC convergence run, the beats-projection validation on real data, and flipping the default to `gnmf`** are the documented follow-up (a separate compute tier) — hence `Refs` rather than `Closes` #181.

body:
## Skill Improvement ($50-150 Bounty)

### Skill Modified
**Skill name:** `segmentation`
**Skill path:** `skills/network/segmentation/`

### What Was Wrong
The skill had good conceptual coverage for zone mapping and trust boundary analysis, but it did not require effective path evidence. Reviewers could mark a boundary pass/fail from a route, policy, or diagram alone without recording whether traffic actually traverses a policy enforcement point, whether policy is enforced, whether flow/test evidence exists, or why a boundary is not evaluable.

### What This PR Fixes
This PR adds:

- An effective segmentation path matrix for source zone, destination zone, route path, enforcement point, policy source, default action, observed/tested traffic, confidence, and Not Evaluable reason.
- Evidence confidence levels for combined source-of-truth, partial configuration, test/flow-only, narrative-only, and missing evidence.
- Not Evaluable reason codes for missing route exports, missing policy exports, unknown PEP traversal, unknown CNI/mesh enforcement, stale or absent segmentation test results, missing PCI dependency mapping, and incomplete cloud service endpoint policy.
- Output-format updates and pitfalls that force reviewers to separate routable paths, effective allowed flows, and policy bypasses.

### Evidence

**Before (skill misses this / false positive on this):**
```text
Trust Boundary Matrix:
Source Zone: User
Dest Zone: Data
Enforcement: Firewall
Status: Restricted

The report does not require proof that the route actually crosses the firewall,
that Kubernetes NetworkPolicy is enforced by the CNI, or that test results are
fresh enough to validate the boundary.
```

**After (now correctly handled):**
```text
Effective Segmentation Path Matrix:
Source Zone: User
Dest Zone: Data
Route Path: user subnet -> transit gateway -> firewall -> data subnet
PEP Traversed: firewall policy FW-220
Policy Source: exported firewall config + route table IaC
Observed/Test Evidence: nmap test 2026-06-01, blocked tcp/5432
Confidence: High
Not Evaluable Reason: none
```

- [ ] Added benign test cases (`tests/benign/`)

body:
## Summary

Benchmark-only changes to make **ReTrace-Bench** coherent and AAAI/ACL-ready as an *independent* benchmark paper. No ReTrace-Learn training touched; no new domains/failure-modes/splits.

**1. Oracle gold-replay decision (the blocking bug).** `retrace_oracle_engine` in `scripts/run_retrace_bench_baseline.py` constructed its decision from a hard-coded `failure_mode -> decision` map, which is wrong for `test_800_templateheldout_en` where each mode admits several decisions (`DECISIONS_BY_MODE`). Since the oracle is a gold-replay reference (it already reads `hidden_gold` for answer/evidence/diagnosis), it now also replays the gold decision:

```python
decision = gold.get("expected_decision")  # was: {policy_violation: refuse..., ...}.get(primary_failure_mode, "use_current_memory")
# fall back to use_current_memory + stderr warning only if absent (present for the canonical split)
```

Result on `data/retrace_bench/test_800_templateheldout_en/scenarios.jsonl` (oracle row):

| metric | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| decision accuracy | 0.294 | **1.000** |
| decision macro-F1 | 0.232 | **1.000** |
| non-answer accuracy | 0.132 | **1.000** |
| evidence F1 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| diagnosis | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| memory state | 0.968 | 0.968 |

`memory_state` stays `0.968` (unchanged by this fix): the minimal oracle proposer only emits `SUPERSEDES`/`UNCERTAIN` edges, so `deleted`/`restored`/`blocked` and condition-`unresolved` states on 90/800 scenarios remain `current`. Documented precisely in `baseline_results_test_800_templateheldout_en.md`.

**2. Regenerated** `docs/retrace_bench/baseline_results_test_800_templateheldout_en.md` with the fixed oracle row and explicit `sanity / memory-baseline / oracle` grouping; oracle relabeled a **gold-replay consistency reference**, not a deployable method.

**3. Headline metrics.** `scorers_general.py` gains `HEADLINE_METRICS` (`decision_macro_f1`, `non_answer_decision_accuracy`, `memory_state_accuracy`, `evidence_f1`, `failure_diagnosis_accuracy`, `stale_reuse_rate`) and `AUXILIARY_METRICS` (incl. `black_box_decision_accuracy`). `aggregate_metrics` now additionally returns grouped `headline_metrics` / `auxiliary_metrics` / `all_metrics` / `per_decision_*` views; the flat `metrics` key is **preserved** for backward compatibility (`run_retrace_bench_ablation.py:load_metrics`, tests). The `# Primary metrics.` comment on `black_box_decision_accuracy` is replaced to mark it a per-example raw/auxiliary signal.

**4. Centralized decision label space.** `general_taxonomy.py` now defines `DECISIONS` (alongside existing `NON_ANSWER_DECISIONS`). `scorers_general.py` imports them (`ALL_DECISIONS = set(DECISIONS)` kept as alias) and `generate_retrace_templateheldout_test.py` imports `DECISIONS` instead of redefining it.

**5–7. Benchmark-paper framing & split clarity.** `benchmark_paper.md` reframed as an independent, method-neutral benchmark; the aggressive "None of these directly evaluate..." paragraph replaced with the safer "complementary / isolates / operational evaluation target" framing and named related work (LongMemEval, MemBench, LoCoMo, + optional MemoryAgentBench/EvoMemBench). author: zrbecker
body:
## What

Replaces the `Application` seam's `commit -> Result<()>` with `commit -> Result<CommitResult>`:

```rust
pub struct ValidatorUpdate { pub node_id: NodeId, pub weight: u64 } // ABCI {pub_key, power}; weight 0 removes
pub struct CommitResult { pub validator_updates: Vec<ValidatorUpdate>, pub app_data: Option<Bytes> }
```

This is the **#225 M2** interface addition — the channel by which an application that owns membership (a staking module) drives the validator set, mirroring ABCI's `ResponseFinalizeBlock.validator_updates`. First concrete piece of milestone **Validator economics** (#3).

## Scope (seam only — no consumer yet)

- The integration layer **receives** `validator_updates` but does not consume them. Both production call sites (`commit_block`, the #635 EL-catchup replay) use `if let Err(e) = …`, so they ignore the `Ok` payload unchanged. Applying updates at a view boundary via the reconfig path (#140/#462) is the follow-up, **#652**.
- All three `Application` impls return `CommitResult::default()`:
  - **reth EL** — drives no membership changes (Ethereum keeps the validator set in the *consensus* layer, not the EL).
  - **counter app** (`MempoolBlockBuilder`) — drives none.
  - `RecordingApp` (test).
- `app_data` is carried as an opaque ABCI-style escape hatch; its **commitment** story (new header field vs. fold into the commands commitment) is deliberately left unsettled and is a follow-up.

## Why this shape

`ValidatorUpdate` is keyed by `NodeId` + `weight` (0 = remove) so #652 can translate a batch directly into the existing `ReconfigCommand` add/remove/weight-change path. Endpoint resolution for *added* validators is out of scope here (endpoint-advertisement concern, #546/#547).

## Behaviour

Provably inert: every impl returns the default, so there is no observable behaviour change (hence no DigitalOcean A/B — there is nothing to differentiate at runtime). Covered by tests instead.

## Tests / gates

- New unit tests lock the public shape (`commit_result_default_reports_nothing`, `commit_result_carries_validator_updates`); extended a reth commit test to assert the EL returns an empty `CommitResult`.
- `cargo fmt` · `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` · `cargo test` · Docs gate · `cargo deny` all green. (One unrelated, pre-existing proptest flake `proptest_weighted_byzantine_committee_…` — a timing-sensitive randomized BFT sim under a 1.5s phase cap; passes in isolation.)

Part of #225 (M2). Closes #651.

author: transitrix
body:
## What

PR1 of the **Activity Card** renderer (Studio track of epic vkgeorgia/strategy#97, task #134) — the `@transitrix/diagrams` half. The extension preview + wiring + example land in PR2.

The Activity Card is the **first multi-document Studio notation**. The card YAML holds only `id` / `project` (an Activity ID) / `description` / `milestones[]`; everything painted on the card is pulled **by reference** at view time from sibling `*.activities.*` and `*.fgca.*` documents in the same view directory.

## Contents

- **`types.ts`** — raw card doc model + assembled view-model (`ResolvedActivityCard`) + pure layout geometry.
- **`validate.ts`** — document-local structural validation only: `HDR-001/002` (header), `AC-001..006` (card + milestone shape, id grammars, date format), and the document-local half of `PC-001` (project field present + well-formed).
- **`resolver.ts`** — the novel piece. Filesystem-free, directory-scoped (exact-dir) cross-document resolver. Resolves the project Activity, child activities (`parent` = project id), and expands the project's `goals[]` / `delivers_changes[]` into the Factors→Goals→Changes chain against sibling FGCA docs. Emits the cross-document rules:
  - `PC-001` (project does not resolve), `PC-002` (`activity_type` ≠ `Project`), `PC-003` (milestone changes ⊄ project changes), `PC-004` warning (milestone date outside `[valid_from, valid_to]`)
  - `LIFECYCLE-001..003` scoped to the resolved **project Activity** (initiation = `valid_from`).
- **`layout.ts`** — single-page card geometry (title · dates band · milestone timeline · F→G→C columns + edges · child-activity rows). Applies the spec **§5.1 ArchiMate-class convention** (`ACTIVITY` → "Work Package", `MILESTONE` → "Implementation Event") renderer-side, derived from TYPE — no `archimate_class` data field.

## Design decisions

- **Resolution scope = single view directory, exact-dir (non-recursive).** The extension (PR2) globs the card's own directory and hands parsed siblings in.
- **String-ID canonical FGCA.** The card expands the project's canonical `GOAL-…` / `CHANGE-…` references, so the resolver reads the canonical string-ID FGCA form directly rather than reusing `parseCanonicalFGCA` (which collapses IDs to the internal numeric model).
- **LIFECYCLE scoped to the project only.** Child activities / FGCA elements are not lifecycle-checked — today's Studio docs may legitimately omit those fields.
- Resolver narrows every sibling defensively → a malformed sibling degrades to an error/warning, never a crash.

## Tests

27 new unit tests (`validate` / `resolver` / `layout`). Full diagrams suite green (**503 passed**); `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Out of scope (PR2)

`extension/src/activity-card-preview.ts`, preview-router / command / activation-event / language wiring in `extension/package.json`, the worked example under `examples/`, and the hand-test of the success signal.

body:
**Stacked on #47.** The two remaining flow bugs you flagged.

1. **Cutters no longer dive into a live drive.** A committed basket-cutter on the **drive side** (in the lane the handler is attacking) clears out to the weak-side corner instead of cutting into the congestion and dragging his man to the ball. A **weak-side** cutter keeps going — he's the dunker/dump-off target (a real rim finish, so the driving rim-floor still passes).

2. **Bring-up flows into the offense** instead of a separate hard-coded stage. The transition now settles to the half-court as soon as the PG has the ball in the **frontcourt** (past a shorter min beat: `BRINGUP_MIN_T` 3.4→1.8) rather than dribbling all the way to the top and *then* flipping the offense on. The handler brings it the rest of the way and initiates through his own half-court decisions — continuous. The PnR call is range-capped (`SCREEN_MAX_HANDLER_DIST`) so he doesn't call a screen from 35 ft out.

## Verification
Screens still set/used ~5/game; **driving rim-floor**, transition-spacing, and positioning tests all pass; sim realistic + balanced. Goldens re-baselined; full suite 22/165/3-skip; typecheck clean.

**To eyeball:** the bring-up should feel like one motion into the set now; and on a drive, the strong-side cutter clears while the weak-side man stays for the dump-off. (I can't see the exact bring-up "glitch" you described, so a visual confirm would help.)

author: okaz-code
body: ## Summary This adds three new BGFX post-processing chains that bring D3D-HLSL-style CRT rendering to **vector games**, which previously had no equivalent of the raster HLSL/CRT pipeline: - **Vector (Star Wars)** — beam **overload** (focus bloom-out on bright beams) and **monitor glow** (whole-tube glow when the beam is driven off-screen), on top of the full CRT post chain. - **Vector (Color)** — color vector CRT (Tempest, etc.) with shadow mask. - **Vector (Monochrome)** — monochrome phosphor CRT (Asteroids, Battlezone, Lunar Lander, Vectrex, etc.) with a tunable phosphor color. Vector lines are rasterized into a supersampled FBO by a new analytic-AA line shader, then run through phosphor persistence, multi-level bloom (with HLSL-style overdrive cross-talk), optional shadow mask, and an asymmetric pincushion distortion. Where possible the existing `hlsl/*` effects are reused; the vector-specific stages are new `sw_*` effects. Selecting a chain for a vector game now lists only vector-compatible chains (filtered by a `"screen_type": "vector"` tag), so the raster `default` chain is no longer offered for vector hardware. ## Screenshots **Star Wars — beam overload (bright beams bloom/defocus)** **Star Wars — monitor glow (tube glows as beams are driven off-screen)** ## What's included New BGFX assets: - 3 chains: `bgfx/chains/vector-{starwars,color,monochrome}.json` - 9 effects: `bgfx/effects/sw_*.json` - 9 shaders: `src/osd/modules/render/bgfx/shaders/fs_sw_*.sc`, with precompiled binaries for dx9 / dx11 / glsl / essl / metal / spirv under `bgfx/shaders/*/`. Core engine changes: - `vector.{h,cpp}` — per-frame, per-beam **overload pipeline** shared by all vector games (sigmoid → threshold split into display intensity + overload amount → beam width expansion), **monitor-glow accumulation** of off-screen overloaded beam energy, intensity-driven **point-vector dot sizing**, and an optional generation- counter-based **vector CRT flicker**. All effect parameters come from chain sliders, with ini-derived fallbacks when a chain exposes no matching slider. - `avgdvg.{h,cpp}` — Star Wars carries a raw beam score (VCTR × STAT intensity) so the overload split can be computed from the original beam current; the default clip window is made symmetric so overscan can reveal off-screen beams. - `drawbgfx.{h,cpp}` — renders `PRIMFLAG_VECTOR` lines into a supersampled FBO via the new line effect, feeds the result into the chain, pushes the per-frame vector options, and injects the monitor-glow amount as a uniform. - `chainmanager.{h,cpp}` — detect vector games and filter the chain selection list by `screen_type`; build the 8-level bloom mip targets. - `render.{h,cpp}` — `render_container::add_line` gains an `overload` parameter threaded through to the primitive. - Small supporting changes in `targetreader.cpp` (per-target format, RGBA16F for the float bloom accumulator), `view.h`, `chainentry.*`, `targetmanager.cpp`. ## Behaviour on non-BGFX renderers is unchanged A single `s_bgfx_active` flag (set only when the BGFX renderer initializes) gates the new path. On every other renderer, `vector_device::screen_update` and the Star Wars beam path fall back to the **stock** intensity/`beam_width` behaviour, so non-BGFX output is byte-for-byte identical to stock. ## Testing - Full `make clean` rebuild plus shader rebuild; verified in-game. - Star Wars (overload + monitor glow), Tempest (color + shadow mask), Asteroids / Battlezone / Lunar Lander (monochrome) on the BGFX renderer. - Non-BGFX renderers confirmed identical to stock vector output. ## Known issue On Windows, OS/driver post-processing that targets DXGI flip swapchains — notably **NVIDIA RTX Dynamic Vibrance** and Auto HDR — can blow out the SDR image (the UI blows out too, so it is not a shader issue). OpenGL is unaffected. This is external to MAME; disabling that per-app driver filter restores correct output. ## Notes - All comments are in English; new files carry BSD-3-Clause headers. - Comment/asset additions only for the most recent commit — no functional change there. The pipeline itself is opt-in via chain selection and has no effect unless a `sw_*` / vector chain is chosen.

author: fenio
body:
The Webhook notification channel today sends `{subject, body, source, timestamp}` strings to a configured URL and gives up on the first failed POST. That's enough for \"fire a Discord message when something breaks\" but it doesn't compose with Home Assistant / n8n / monitoring receivers that want typed dispatch, and one transient 503 silently loses the event.

Three additions, all backward-compatible.

## Structured payload

Today:
```json
{ \"subject\": \"[NASty CRITICAL] disk failing\", \"body\": \"…\", \"source\": \"nasty\", \"timestamp\": \"…\" }
```

After this PR:
```json
{
  \"subject\": \"[NASty CRITICAL] disk failing\",
  \"body\": \"Disk /dev/sda SMART health check FAILED\",
  \"source\": \"nasty\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-06-02T…\",
  \"event_type\": \"alert.fired\",
  \"event_id\": \"alert-smart-health-/dev/sda-0\",
  \"nasty_version\": \"0.0.10\",
  \"nasty_hostname\": \"nasty\",
  \"data\": {
    \"rule_id\": \"smart-health\",
    \"rule_name\": \"SMART health failure\",
    \"severity\": \"critical\",
    \"metric\": \"smart_health\",
    \"message\": \"Disk /dev/sda SMART health check FAILED\",
    \"source\": \"/dev/sda\",
    \"current_value\": 0.0,
    \"threshold\": 1.0
  }
}
```

The legacy fields stay so consumers that regex on `subject` keep working. New consumers route on `event_type` and pull typed values out of `data` (which is the full `ActiveAlert` serialized via serde — every field the WebUI shows).

## HMAC-SHA256 signing

Optional \`secret: Option<String>\` field on the Webhook channel. When set:

- Every POST carries `X-NASty-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body
- Receivers verify by recomputing — proves the request really came from NASty
- Cross-checked against Python's stdlib in a unit test so a future crate-bump can't silently break wire compat:
  ```python
  hmac.new(b\"secret\", b\"hello\", hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
  == \"88aab3ede8d3adf94d26ab90d3bafd4a2083070c3bcce9c014ee04a443847c0b\"
  ```
- Optional — old configs without a secret still work, just unsigned

## Retry on transient failure

- Three attempts with 5s + 30s backoff (total wall-clock cap ~35s)
- 5xx and network errors retried; 4xx not (won't fix itself)
- Event id is stable across attempts so receivers can dedupe on it

## Plumbing

- New `Event<'a>` struct carries the structured fields alongside the legacy subject/body
- New `send_event()` is the structured entry; existing `send(subject, body)` thin-wraps it for the SMTP/Telegram/etc. channels that have no use for typed data
- Alert dispatch site (`main.rs`) now passes the `ActiveAlert` as typed `data`

## WebUI

- Optional \"Signing Secret\" input next to the Webhook URL
- Form description updated to mention structured fields + HMAC verification recipe

## Tests (5 new in nasty-system)

- HMAC stable across runs, varies with key, varies with body
- HMAC matches Python reference for fixture vector
- Webhook payload carries both legacy + structured fields

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --no-deps --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `npm run check` in webui
- [ ] Manual: configure a webhook with a secret pointing at https://webhook.site, fire a test alert, verify both the payload shape and that the X-NASty-Signature header validates

author: e-r-butch
body:
## Problem

On macOS Apple Silicon machines (8GB MacBook Air tested), the hindsight embedded daemon consumes 7-8GB of IOAccelerator (GPU) memory immediately on startup. This happens even though the default embedding model is bge-small-en-v1.5 (~130MB on disk).

## Root Cause

PyTorch detects the MPS backend and lets SentenceTransformer auto-select it. The MPS backend pre-allocates 4GB+ of GPU pageable memory for the model, regardless of actual model size. On Apple Silicon with unified memory, this eats directly into system RAM, causing:

- **7.3GB IOAccelerator "Pageable allocation"** (measured via `ioreg -w0 -l`)
- **3.4GB swap** usage (nearly full on 8GB machines)
- System-wide memory pressure, WindowServer starvation, black screen in severe cases

The `embeddings_local_force_cpu` and `reranker_local_force_cpu` config options exist but default to `False`. The generated `~/.hindsight/profiles/hermes.env` file never includes `HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_LOCAL_FORCE_CPU=true` unless the user manually adds it.

## This Has Bitten Us 3 Times

We first hit this on June 1, set the env vars, fixed it. Then it came back the next day. Turned out the env file gets regenerated from scratch by `_build_embedded_profile_env()` every time the daemon restarts — and the env was being rewritten without FORCE_CPU. We kept patching the env file manually but never committed the source fix. A `git pull` would blow away the uncommitted change and the next daemon restart would regenerate a bad env.

Refs: #7135, #8972

## Fix

In `_build_embedded_profile_env()`, detect macOS ARM64 via `platform.system() + platform.machine()` and default both `HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_LOCAL_FORCE_CPU` and `HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_LOCAL_FORCE_CPU` to `true` — unless the user explicitly set them to `false` in their config. This matches how `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER` and other settings are already handled: reasonable platform-appropriate defaults, overridable by config.

## Before / After

```
# Before (MPS):
$ sudo footprint <pid>
IOAccelerator: 4.1 GB
Total dirty:   5.2 GB
Swap:          3.4 GB

# After (CPU forced):
$ sudo footprint <pid>
Total dirty:   657 MB
Swap:          1.4 GB
```

The footprint tool shows no IOAccelerator entries after the fix. The model (bge-small) runs at its actual memory size (~130MB + Python overhead).

No performance impact in practice — recall latency is still under 10 seconds, and on 8GB machines the system can actually do other work without swap thrashing.

author: oreofeolurin
body:
Follow-up to #7. That PR fixed the stream/kv **apply loops**; this closes the rest of the same wrap-boundary class and hardens durability around it.

## Background

`UAL.read` (and therefore `RaftLog.getEntry`) is zero-copy and returns `null` for an entry whose payload **wraps the hot-ring byte boundary** — it can't express two non-adjacent byte runs as one slice. That `null` is fine where a caller can safely fall through (warm/cold fallback, existence probes), but any path that must observe **every** entry was silently dropping the wrapped one.

## Wrap-safety fixes

- **UAL**: documented `read`'s three distinct null cases; added **`readRangeCopy`** (arena-packed, reconstructs wrapped payloads, stops at the first gap so batches stay contiguous); deprecated the zero-copy `readRange` for correctness-sensitive callers.
- **`RaftLog.getRange`** → `readRangeCopy` (+ caller-provided payload arena).
- **`replication.buildAppendRequest`** threads a payload arena → gap-free AppendEntries batches.
- **`coordinator.applyCommitted`** → `getEntryCopy` (was dropping committed `raft_config` commands from the metadata state machine).
- **`persistEntry` + KV handler broadcast paths** → `getEntryCopy` (was dropping wrapped entries from peer replication → follower divergence — this is the live cluster replication path).
- **`partition.isInHot`** → `contains()` (zero-copy `read` falsely reported a wrapped live entry as evicted); **`partition.readTiered`** hot path → `readCopy` (also fixes a warm branch that was a no-op stub).
- **`stream.getPayloadAndTier`** deliberately *stays* on the zero-copy `read`: the warm store always backs it, so null-fallthrough is correct (now documented, to stop a future "fix" from forcing a needless copy).

## Durability hardening

Persist failures were swallowed with `catch {}`, presenting disk faults as silent data loss:

- **shard**: `persist_failures` counter; surface sync-flush / async-flush / append-buffering errors via `log.err` instead of acking writes that aren't on disk.
- **`SegmentWriter.writeToFile`**: `fsync` the data **before** the atomic rename, so `sync` durability actually delivers its fdatasync-before-ack guarantee.

## Tests

- UAL wrap regressions: `read` returns null on a wrap while `readCopy`/`readRangeCopy` recover it; `readRangeCopy` returns a gap-free batch across a wrap.
- e2e 3-node **"leader retains all stream records across a hot-ring wrap"** (4 KB ring): asserts **leader 50/50**.
- `test-unit`, `test-integration`, full `test-e2e` all green.

## Out of scope (separate, pre-existing)

The same cluster test prints a **diagnostic**: follower stream reads return ~half the records (leader 50/50, follower **25/50**) — and this happens even with a default, non-wrapping ring, so it is **not** the wrap bug (a wrap drop is 1–2 records, not half). It's a separate follower-side stream replication/read gap, left as a diagnostic (not asserted) and tracked separately so this regression stays meaningful and green.

author: probablyrobot
body:
## Problem

`search_fulltext` (both the temporal-store path in `engines/skeleton/backends/pgvector.py` and the relational coordinator path in `storage/backends/pgvector.py`) built its tsquery with **`plainto_tsquery`**, which **ANDs every content word** of the query.

A natural-language question - e.g. *"from which deity was Augustus said to descend"* - almost never has all of its content words present in a single chunk, so the `content_tsv @@ tsquery` match returns **nothing**. In practice the BM25/lexical channel returned **0 chunks on essentially every query** (logs: `BM25 channel returned 0 chunks`). The lexical channel was effectively dead, leaving retrieval vector-only.

Verified on a live DB: that question matched **0** chunks in `khora_chunks` with `plainto_tsquery`.

## Fix

Tokenize the query (alphanumeric terms) and **OR** them via `to_tsquery`, ranking with **`ts_rank_cd`** (cover density) so chunks where more query terms co-occur - and closer together - rank highest. This restores lexical recall without the AND cliff, while the density ranking keeps the right passage near the top.

Same question now matches **302** chunks (then ranked, and downstream reranked to top-k).

Applied to both full-text paths (temporal store is tried first; coordinator is the fallback).

## Impact

Found while benchmarking khora on GraphRAG-Bench, where exact-name fact lookups (proper-noun answers) were the weakest bucket and the lexical channel that should serve them was returning nothing. This revives the BM25 channel that fusion already weights (`bm25_weight`).

## Test plan
- [x] Live DB: `to_tsquery` OR form returns 302 chunks vs `plainto_tsquery` AND form's 0, for a representative fact question on `khora_chunks`.
- [x] ruff + ty pre-commit hooks pass.
- [ ] Benchmark medium run to confirm `BM25 returned 0 chunks` warnings drop and retrieval-side metrics on fact lookups improve.

## Summary

Adds **15 new recon executors** (8 → 23) and **6 new playbooks** across two roadmap phases, all wired into both the CLI runner and the MCP server. - Playbooks: `vulnerability-assessment`, `owasp-top10-recon`, `cloud-security-assessment`

**Docs**: `_templates.md` reorganized into 6 stage-segmented sections with full per-executor option docs; `all-tools-selftest` exercises all 23 executors; README/executors/playbooks/roadmap/CHANGELOG synced; version 0.3.0 → 0.5.0.

## Test Coverage

This project has no automated test framework (network-dependent recon executors by design). Verification is via the live diagnostic self-test and per-executor smoke tests:
- **`all-tools-selftest` passes 23/23** against a live HTTPS host (every executor exercised once).

Adversarial review run on both phases (Claude subagent; Codex unavailable in this environment). Findings fixed:
- **SSRF/host-override** via unvalidated `scheme`/`path` in shared `buildUrl` — scheme whitelisted, path guarded.
- **`ip.intel`**: validate Team Cymru ASN is numeric before interpolating into a follow-up DNS query.
- **`tls.deep`**: probe timers cleared so a completed scan doesn't hold the event loop; legacy-cipher probes no longer crash on OpenSSL 3.
- **Multi-request executors** (`fuzz_paths`/`methods`/`bucket_finder`): per-request timeout decoupled from the runner step budget; `http.methods` probes concurrently; `CONNECT` excluded (hangs Node's client); `fuzz_paths` buildUrl moved inside the per-path try so a bad wordlist entry can't abort the scan.
- All HTTP GETs cap response body size (`maxContentLength`).

## Notes

author: rbowater
body:
## Summary

Fixes a case-sensitivity bug in the repo-list/batch processing path that causes **mixed-case repositories to be duplicated many times** in the output CSV when a batch retries.

## Root cause

In `processRepositoriesFromFile` (the path used by `--batch-size`/`--batch-index` and `--repo-list`), the "already processed" guard compared the **raw-case** repo name taken from the list:

```ts
for (const { owner, repo } of repoList) {
  if (processedState.processedRepos.includes(repo)) { // repo is original case
    continue;
  }
```

But processed names are stored **lowercased** — `mapToRepoStatsResult` sets `Repo_Name: repo.name.toLowerCase()`, and `handleRepoProcessingSuccess` records that lowercased value into `processedState.processedRepos`.

So for any repository whose name contains an uppercase letter, `includes(repo)` is **always false**, and the repo is never recognised as already processed.

This is normally harmless on a clean first pass, but it breaks resume-on-retry. When an API error occurs (e.g. a `500`), `withRetry` re-invokes the operation, which **restarts the batch from the top of the repo list** and relies entirely on this guard to skip work already done:

- All-lowercase repos → raw name == stored name → correctly skipped → written once.
- Mixed-case repos → never matched → re-analysed and **re-appended to the CSV on every retry pass**.

A batch that hit ~24 retries therefore wrote each mixed-case repo ~24–25 times.

## Evidence

From a real run of one org (5,019 unique repos), grouping duplicate rows by copy-count and by whether the repo's GitHub name contains an uppercase letter:

| copies | mixed-case | all-lowercase |
|------:|----------:|-------------:|
| 1 | 135 | 4276 |
| 2 | 22 | 542 |
| 3 | 9 | 0 |
| 13 | 2 | 0 |
| 23 | 14 | 0 |
| 24 | 17 | 0 |
| 25 | 2 | 0 |

**Every repository duplicated 3× or more is mixed-case; no all-lowercase repo was duplicated more than twice.** Examples: `acresDeploy×25`, `analytics-db-HESIPerformanceLogs×24`. The small ×2 residue is case-independent (write-then-crash before the state record, plus batch-slice boundary overlap) and is not addressed here.

## Fix

Normalise the name to lower case before the membership check:

```ts
if (processedState.processedRepos.includes(repo.toLowerCase())) {
```

The cursor-based (non-batch) path already compares the lowercased `result.Repo_Name` on both sides, so it was unaffected and is unchanged.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `vitest run __tests__/main.test.ts` → 42/42 pass.
- Diff is a single guard line plus an explanatory comment.

## Notes

- I deliberately kept the diff minimal. `npm run build` runs `prettier --write .`, which reformats several unrelated files on this branch (it is behind upstream and not prettier-clean); I excluded all of that to keep the change reviewable. `prettier --check src/main.ts` already warned on this file before my change, so no new formatting regression is introduced.
- A focused regression test would require exporting `processRepositoriesFromFile` (currently module-private) or extracting the skip decision into a small helper — happy to follow up with that if you'd like it in this PR.

<!---
The core Triton is a small number of people, and we receive many PRs (thank
you!).  To help us review your code more quickly, **if you are a new
contributor (less than 3 PRs merged) we ask that you complete the following
tasks and include the filled-out checklist in your PR description.**

Complete the following tasks before sending your PR, and replace `[ ]` with
`[x]` to indicate you have done them.
-->

# New contributor declaration
- [ ] I am not making a trivial change, such as fixing a typo in a comment.

- [ ] I have written a PR description following these
  [rules](https://cbea.ms/git-commit/#why-not-how).

- [ ] I have run `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`.

- Select one of the following.
  - [ ] I have added tests.
    - `/test` for `lit` tests
    - `/unittest` for C++ tests
    - `/python/test` for end-to-end tests
  - [ ] This PR does not need a test because `FILL THIS IN`.

- Select one of the following.
  - [ ] I have not added any `lit` tests.
  - [ ] The `lit` tests I have added follow these [best practices](https://mlir.llvm.org/getting_started/TestingGuide/#filecheck-best-practices),
    including the "tests should be minimal" section. (Usually running Python code
    and using the instructions it generates is not minimal.)

# compilation pipeline optimization.

- **Compilation Pipeline Optimization**: Extracted `torch_npu`-related workspace/sync lock/async launch capabilities from the launcher into a standalone `npu_utils.so`, transforming the launcher into a lightweight bridge layer that reduces compile-time heavy dependencies.

## Performance Gains

### Overview

| Scenario         | Metric                                                 | Old Architecture | New Architecture | Absolute Change | Relative Change |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ---------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| First Compile    | `total_compile + npu_utils_build_so + launcher_build`  | 16.266s          | 9.121s           | -7.145s         | -43.93%         |
| Second Compile   | `total_compile + launcher_build`                       | 3.503s           | 2.621s           | -0.882s         | -25.19%         |

### First Compile `softmax` Phase Breakdown

| Phase                      | Old Arch(s) | New Arch(s) | Change(s)  | Notes                                        |
| -------------------------- | ----------: | ----------: | ---------: | -------------------------------------------- |
| `total_compile`            |       2.415 |       2.406 |     -0.009 | Triton kernel core compilation nearly unchanged  |
| `npu_utils_build_so`       |       0.809 |       6.168 |     +5.359 | `torch_npu` dependency cost centralized in `npu_utils.so` build |
| `launcher_build`           |      13.042 |       0.548 |    -12.495 | Launcher build cost reduced significantly    |

Launcher detail:

| Sub-phase                    | Old Arch(s) | New Arch(s) | Change(s)   |
| ---------------------------- | ----------: | ----------: | ---------: |
| `launcher_precompile_header` |      11.615 |       0.000 |    -11.615 |
| `launcher_build_stub`        |      13.040 |       0.546 |    -12.494 |
| `launcher_load_module`       |       0.002 |       0.001 |     -0.001 |

### Second Compile `test_sum` Phase Breakdown

| Phase             | Old Arch(s) | New Arch(s) | Change(s) | Notes                                |
| ----------------- | ----------: | ----------: | --------: | ------------------------------------ |
| `total_compile`   |       2.048 |       2.072 |    +0.024 | Triton kernel core compilation nearly unchanged   |
| `launcher_build`  |       1.456 |       0.549 |    -0.907 | Launcher build continues to benefit  |

Launcher detail:

| Sub-phase                    | Old Arch(s) | New Arch(s) | Change(s) |
| ---------------------------- | ----------: | ----------: | --------: |
| `launcher_precompile_header` |       0.000 |       0.000 |     0.000 |
| `launcher_build_stub`        |       1.453 |       0.548 |    -0.905 |
| `launcher_load_module`       |       0.002 |       0.001 |    -0.001 |

On second compile, `npu_utils.so` has already been cached, so there is no additional `npu_utils_build_so` overhead.

### Performance Analysis

- First compile gain driver: removed `launcher_precompile_header` (11.615s → 0s), launcher build dropped from 13.04s to 0.55s
- Second compile gain driver: launcher build consistently shortened to ~0.55s (1.453s → 0.548s)
- Cost: `npu_utils_build_so` first build increased from 0.809s to 6.168s, but the launcher-side gain is larger, resulting in significant overall compile time improvement
- `Kernel compile` core (`stage_npubin`) is essentially unchanged, confirming the optimization did not impact the core compilation flow

## Core Changes

### npu\_utils.so Extraction

Centralized `torch_npu`-related capabilities into `npu_utils.cpp`:

1. **Added `USE_TORCH_NPU` conditional compilation block**: centralized management of `ATen/ATen.h`, `torch_npu/csrc/core/npu/NPUWorkspaceAllocator.h`, `torch_npu/csrc/framework/OpCommand.h`, and other dependencies
2. **Added three `extern "C"` exported interfaces**:
   - `triton_allocate_workspace`: workspace allocation
   - `triton_allocate_sync_block_lock`: sync block lock allocation
   - `triton_async_launch`: taskqueue async launch
3. **Added tensor lifetime retention mechanism (opaque handle + RAII guard)**: prevents raw pointers returned from being invalidated during launch, while also solving the ever-growing global `retained_tensors` vector memory leak risk

### Launcher Lightweighting

The launcher no longer directly depends on `torch_npu`, instead loading `npu_utils.so` at runtime via `dlopen/dlsym`:

- No longer includes `precompiled.h`, replaced with a lightweight header
- No longer directly constructs `at_npu::native::OpCommand`, instead forwards through `npu_utils.so`
- No longer carries `torch_npu` heavy dependencies at compile time

### retained_tensors Memory Leak Fix (Opaque Handle + RAII Guard)

#### Background

After decoupling the launcher, the underlying `at::Tensor` objects for workspace and sync block lock changed from temporary launcher-side objects to internally allocated objects within `npu_utils.so`. The previous implementation used a global `retained_tensors` vector inside `npu_utils.cpp` to hold all allocated tensors. While this approach avoided dangling pointers, the vector only grew without shrinking, causing continuous accumulation of unused workspace/sync lock tensors during long training runs or frequent compilation.

#### Solution

Replace the process-level global `retained_tensors` container with per-allocation releasable opaque handles, with the launcher side using `std::shared_ptr` custom deleters to achieve RAII automatic release. RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) binds resource lifetime to object lifetime: `shared_ptr` holds the handle upon construction (resource acquisition), and when leaving scope, it automatically destructs and invokes the deleter to release the underlying tensor, guaranteeing no resource leaks regardless of normal return or exception exit.

**New struct in `npu_utils.cpp`:**

```cpp
struct RetainedTensorHandle {
  explicit RetainedTensorHandle(at::Tensor tensor) : tensor(std::move(tensor)) {}
  at::Tensor tensor;
};
```

**Allocation interfaces changed from returning only a device pointer to also returning a handle:**

```cpp
extern "C" void* triton_allocate_workspace(uint64_t size, void **handle);
extern "C" void* triton_allocate_sync_block_lock(uint64_t size, void* stream, void **handle);
extern "C" void triton_release_retained_tensor(void *handle);
```

The `handle` points to a `RetainedTensorHandle`, which holds the actual `at::Tensor`. The launcher still passes the returned `void*` device pointer to

## Summary
Enhanced the database migration system to provide detailed reporting when migrations fail. The system now tracks migration state throughout the process and outputs a comprehensive report to console.error when an error occurs.

## Key Changes
- **New `MigrationReport` interface**: Tracks skipped, undone, and applied migrations, plus the current migration being processed when an error occurs
- **Report formatting**: Added `formatReport()` function to generate human-readable error messages with migration details
- **Migration tracking**: Updated the `migrate()` function to populate the report as migrations are processed
- **Error logging**: Console error output now includes:
  - Target database name
  - Migration that failed (with filepath)
  - List of migrations skipped (already applied)
  - List of migrations undone during this run
  - List of migrations successfully applied before the failure
- **Database name resolution**: Attempts to query the current database name for inclusion in the report
- **Test coverage**: Added test case verifying the report is logged to console.error on migration failure, including validation of database name, failed migration, and applied migrations in the output

## Implementation Details
- The `fmtMigration()` helper formats migration IDs with zero-padding (e.g., "001-initial") for consistent display
- Report state is maintained throughout the migration process and cleared after each operation completes
- Database name resolution failures are silently handled with a debug message to avoid blocking migrations
- The report is only output when an error occurs; successful migrations don't produce console output

body:
## Problem

The Claude backend hardcodes `base_url` to `https://api.anthropic.com`, making it impossible to route requests through Anthropic-compatible API gateways or proxies.

This breaks usage behind:
- Corporate API gateways (our use case — a centralized gateway that routes to Bedrock)
- LiteLLM / other proxy servers
- Self-hosted Anthropic-compatible endpoints

## Fix

Read `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from the environment and pass it to the `anthropic.Anthropic()` constructor. Falls back to `https://api.anthropic.com` when unset — fully backwards-compatible.

This matches the convention used by the [official Anthropic Python SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python#usage) itself, which respects this env var.

## Changes

`graphify/llm.py`: Two call sites patched:
1. `_call_claude()` — used for semantic extraction
2. `_call_llm()` claude backend — used for query/cluster

## Testing

Verified with a corporate API gateway (Anthropic Messages API compatible, JWT auth):
```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=$JWT_TOKEN
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://gateway.example.com
graphify . --update --backend claude --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
# → Successfully extracts via gateway
```

Without the env var set, behavior is identical to before (hits api.anthropic.com).

  - the workflow built docs via `cd docs && mkdocs build`, which changed the shell working directory before writing `build/reports/pages/index.html`

- **Workflow adjustment**
  - run MkDocs from the repository root with an explicit config path:
    ```yaml
    - run: mkdocs build -f docs/mkdocs.yml
    ```
  - this keeps all generated Pages content under the existing artifact root: `build/reports/pages`

- **Docs config update**
  - update MkDocs Material locale from `no` to `nb` in `docs/mkdocs.yml`
  - preserves Norwegian localization while matching supported theme assets

- **Resulting behavior**
  - ADR docs continue to publish to `build/reports/pages/adr`
  - the generated Pages index remains written to `build/reports/pages/index.html`
  - the reusable build workflow now prepares the Pages artifact without tripping over MkDocs locale or path handling
