author: erseco
body:
## Summary

A multi-agent audit swept every subsystem (service worker, PHP worker, runtime/bootstrap, crash recovery, blueprint engine + PHP code generation, shell/remote, shared utils, PHP patches, build scripts) and surfaced **17 confirmed findings** (15 distinct bugs after dedup), each cross-examined by an adversarial skeptic panel. This PR fixes **all of them**, plus **3 blockers** and 2 extra injection/SSRF hardenings that an adversarial review of the *fixes themselves* caught.

**Verification:** `npm run build:worker` clean · `make lint` exit 0 · **`make test` → 422 pass / 0 fail** (≈115 new regression tests) · all blocker fixes re-verified closed with no new bypass.

> `dist/` and `sw.bundle.js` are gitignored (CI rebuilds them), so only source + tests are committed.

## Critical — code execution / SSRF / XSS

| Bug | Fix |
|-----|-----|
| **ZIP-slip → arbitrary PHP exec** in plugin/theme install & `unzip` step | Central `sanitizeArchivePath()` in `lib/moodle-loader.js` (rejects `..`/absolute entries) + per-handler containment checks in `filesystem.js` & `moodle-plugins.js` |
| **PHP code injection** via unescaped `pluginName` in plugin install | Validate `pluginName` in `resolvePluginDir()` **before** any extraction (chokepoint); `escapePhp()` now escapes backslashes; `customField` keys validated as PHP identifiers |
| **Open proxy / SSRF** in `github-proxy-worker.js` | Host-aware allowlist; reject private/loopback/link-local + IPv4-mapped-IPv6 + cloud-metadata DNS; **re-validate every redirect hop** (`redirect:"manual"`, cap 5) so an allowlisted host can't 302 into an internal address |
| **Reflected XSS** in `sw.js` HTML attribute rewriter | Re-encode rewritten attribute values (`escapeHtml`) so decoded URLs can't break out of the attribute |

## High / Medium — data-loss & correctness

- **CLI install failure silently marked `installed:true`** → gate on per-stage success markers; throw before writing the marker on failure (`bootstrap.js`)
- **SQLite ALTER emulation dropped columns / threw `ddsequenceerror`** on upgrades → preserve live columns and re-add `PRIMARY KEY` (incl. composite) (`patches/.../sqlite_sql_generator.php`)
- **`data-url` resources with media-type params** (e.g. `charset`) rejected → fixed regex in `resources.js` + `parser.js`
- **`escapePhp` corrupted multi-line text** (literal `\n`) → only escape `\` and `'` for single-quoted context
- **Manifest HEAD-failure booted the wrong branch** → only fall back on a definitive 404 and verify channel match before extracting
- **Provisioning check could abort boot** in the saved-state branch → wrapped in try/catch to fall back to fresh install
- **Crash snapshot pinned in heap** when restart refused → hydrate only after reset succeeds; clear otherwise and on reconfigure (`php-worker.js`)
- **Scoped static cache leaked assets across runtimes** → namespace cache key by scope+runtime (`sw.js`)
- **Dead `readyNavigated` guard caused double frame navigation** → navigate once using the resolved path (`remote/main.js` + `php-worker.js`)
- **`set -e` aborted snapshot script before logging the installer error** → guard so the install log is always dumped on failure

## Methodology

`find → adversarially verify → fix → adversarially review → fix blockers → re-verify`, run as parallel agent workflows over disjoint file groups. The fix-review pass caught 3 real blockers (late validation order, redirect-follow SSRF bypass, missing PK on table rebuild) that the initial fixes missed.

## Known minor follow-ups (non-blocking)

- Composite-PK column *order* is not preserved across SQLite ALTER emulation (uniqueness is unaffected; no current Moodle core table relies on it).
- `omeka.org` proxy path scope left unrestricted (out of scope; tightening risks breaking Omeka usage).
- The riskiest untested paths (CLI-install marker gating, SQLite upgrade emulation) warrant an e2e upgrade check; flagged for a follow-up.

author: sbaker617
body:
## What's this?

Fixes DRE-12252 — the `GH_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT was leaking into Docker image metadata because Dockerfiles used `ENV GH_ACCESS_TOKEN` which persists in the image config JSON (visible via `docker inspect`).

This PR replaces the PAT-based auth entirely with a read-only SSH deploy key scoped to `slackhq/vitess-addons`.

## What changed

- **7 Dockerfiles**: Replaced `ARG GH_ACCESS_TOKEN` + HTTPS rewrite with `ARG VITESS_ADDONS_DEPLOY_KEY` + SSH key setup
- **docker-bake.hcl, build.sh, build-bootstrap action**: Renamed variable/input
- **~100 CI workflow files** (templates + generated + manual): Switched from inline secret interpolation to `env:` block pattern for multi-line SSH key handling
- **build.env, docker/test/run.sh, test/vtop_example.sh, test/ci_workflow_gen.go**: Updated references

## How it works

Instead of rewriting HTTPS URLs with an embedded token:
```
git config url.https://$TOKEN@github.com/.insteadOf https://github.com/
```

We now write the deploy key to `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and rewrite to SSH:
```
git config --global url.git@github.com:.insteadOf https://github.com/
```

The key is never persisted in image metadata — it's only available during the build via `ARG` (not `ENV`).

## Required setup

The repo secret `VITESS_ADDONS_DEPLOY_KEY` must contain the private key for the deploy key added to `slackhq/vitess-addons`. Once confirmed working, the old `GH_ACCESS_TOKEN` secret can be removed.

body:
## What & why
Round-trip testing (import a book from DCS → export back → byte-diff) surfaced two export-path defects, found while validating import↔export fidelity for OBA, RUT, and HOS.

### 1. TQ rows reordered on export (data bug)
`tn_rows`/`twl_rows` carry a `sort_order` column (migrations 0003/0004) and export `ORDER BY chapter, verse, sort_order`; `tq_rows` never got it and exported `ORDER BY chapter, verse, id`, so any verse with more than one question was re-sorted alphabetically by id, discarding authored order (RUT 1:1, 4:4, 4:6, 4:17). Pure reordering — no content change — but it churns the nightly export and reorders published questions.

**Fix:** add `sort_order` to `tq_rows` (migration `0025`), seed it on import (`bookImport`), leave it NULL on reimport / AI-insert (NULLS-LAST, matching tn/twl), and order the tq export + editor read by it.

### 2. ULT/UST collide in the R2 backup (latent)
Both render to `NN-BOOK.usfm`; the R2 key `exports/<instance>/<book>/<filename>` omitted the resource, so UST overwrote ULT in the R2 backup within one export instance (harmless on DCS — separate repos — but the backup lost the ULT copy). **Fix:** key is now `exports/<instance>/<book>/<resource>/<filename>`.

## Verification
Full round trip on an isolated local stack (no DCS writes):
- RUT `tq` and HOS `tq` (100 rows) now round-trip **byte-identical** (RUT tq was reordered before the fix).
- ULT/UST land at distinct R2 keys.
- OBA/RUT/HOS otherwise byte-identical except benign usfm-js whitespace normalization in USFM (marker/verse line breaks, double→single space — zero content change, confirmed identical after whitespace strip).
- `npm run typecheck` passes both workspaces.

## Deploy note
Not deployed yet (per request). After merge, prod needs `wrangler d1 migrations apply bible_editor --remote --env production` for migration `0025`.

body:
## Summary

Adds the ability to **physically feed a selected feeder** through the PPBFC AS feeder controller over serial, following the *PPBFC AS Feeder Test Tool* protocol.

- **▶ Perform feed** toolbar button (selection-based): opens the configured serial port, sends the feed sequence for the selected feeder, then closes the port. `N` and advance come from the feeder itself — `N` = slot number (`bank*100+port`), `F` = its tape advance (mm).
- Sequence mirrors the test tool's Activate + Single Advance:
  ```
  M610 S1 · M611 S0 · M611 N<n> S1 · M600 N<n> F<mm> X1 · M611 N<n> S0
  ```
- **⚙ Settings** dialog: sets the serial port (editable dropdown of detected ports) and baud (default `19200`), persisted to `settings.json` in the per-user config folder.
- Serial I/O runs on a worker thread; the main thread polls the result via `after()` so all Tk updates stay on the main thread.
- `pyserial` is imported lazily — the app still runs stdlib-only without it; the feed button reports a clear message if it's missing. Clear errors too when no port is set, the feeder has no tape advance, or the slot can't be read from the name.
- The "feeder will physically advance" confirmation shows **once per session** (after the first confirmed feed, later feeds run immediately).

## Testing

- `py_compile` passes.
- Feed command building and `settings.json` round-trip verified.
- **Real serial write path over a PTY** — both directly and end-to-end through the GUI (worker → poll → done): the port received exactly the 5 g-code lines for `N300/F4`; status/flag/button reset correctly.

### Surfaces élargies (full-width)

| Surface | Avant | Layout interne |
|---|---|---|
| `/admin/members` | `max-w-4xl` | liste → `grid xl:grid-cols-2` + `[&>li]:h-full` |
| `/admin/reports` | `max-w-4xl` | listes/semaine → `grid lg:grid-cols-2 2xl:grid-cols-3` + `h-full` |

### Gardées en colonne-lecture (stratégie §23 par-surface, jamais 100 %)

`/admin/members/[id]` (détail + onglets texte : rapports, notes), `/admin/reports/[id]` (rapport long), `/admin/members/[id]/training/[…]` (1 backtest), `/admin/invite` (formulaire), `…/trades/[tradeId]` (détail trade).

author: jennydove
body:
## Summary
- Markdown encoded hierarchy purely via heading level (Outcome=H2, Opportunity=H3, Solution=H4, Experiment=H5), so same-type nesting (e.g. a sub-opportunity under another opportunity) couldn't be represented — both ended up at H3 and the parent link was discarded by the serializer. Dragging opp B onto opp A updated the in-memory tree, but autosave wrote markdown that flattened them back to siblings, and the next 10s poll reverted the UI.
- Adds an optional `{^parentId}` token in the heading line after `{#cardId}`. The serializer emits it only when the tree's actual parent doesn't match what heading-level inference would reconstruct, so trees that already fit the natural OST hierarchy serialize identically to today.
- Parser is now two-pass: collect all cards (with explicit refs + inferred parents), then resolve. The explicit ref wins when it points to a known card; falls back to inferred parent for forward refs / dangling references.

## Example
Sub-opportunity nesting:
```
## [Outcome] Goal {#out1}

### [Opportunity] A {#a}

### [Opportunity] A1 {#a1} {^a}     ← parent override; visually H3 but child of A

#### [Solution] S {#s}

### [Opportunity] A2 {#a2} {^a}     ← also a sub-opportunity of A
```

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 359 unit tests pass, 5 new in `sameTypeNesting.test.ts` covering serialize-emits-marker, no-marker-for-natural-hierarchy, sibling preservation, mixed hierarchy, and unknown-ref fallback
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` — 60/60 pass
- [x] Existing `markdownRoundTrip.test.ts` (30 tests) still passes — backward compat verified
- [ ] Manual: drag an opportunity onto another opportunity in the canvas; the move should now persist across the 10s poll

## Notes
- Backward compatible: existing trees in cloud have no `{^...}` markers and serialize/parse identically.
- CLI and share-links use the same shared serializer/parser, so they get this automatically.
- The token order in a heading is now: `### [Type] Title {#id} {^parent} @status` (parent ref between ID and status).

author: guillempuche
body:
## What

Hardens the research MCP tool surface against the input-validation, data-integrity, and error-handling bugs found while testing the live production deployment.

## Changes

- **Input validation** at the MCP parameter boundary: UUID-checked ids, `schema_name` restricted to the closed registry set, non-empty + length-capped query, and clamped pagination (finite-int, `[1,100]`). Malformed or oversized inputs are now rejected cleanly instead of reaching SQL (raw `SqlError` leak) or creating runs that only fail at phase 0.
- **Orphan-link prevention**: `attach` verifies the subject (company/contact) and the run exist under the org before writing a `research_links` row. Enforced in the service, so the MCP and HTTP callers both benefit.
- **Honest cancel**: `cancel` reports `not_found` / `already_terminal` instead of always returning `cancelled`.
- **Error redaction**: a transient `SqlError` collapses to a generic defect, so the Postgres driver error (statement, connection details) — and our own source path — no longer reach clients.

A small follow-up `ai:` commit registers the production batuda MCP server (env-var keyed) and unpins the Claude Code model.

## Verification

`check-types`, unit tests, and `build` all pass. New BDD coverage: validation schemas, pagination clamp, cancel/attach outcome logic, and the redaction security property. DB round-trips for attach/cancel remain `it.todo`, matching the repo's integration-test convention.

## Deferred

- **F1** intermittent 500 — originates in the shared `OrgMiddleware` (auth/org resolution), not research code; belongs with the crash-resilience backlog.
- **F9** Cloudflare WAF user-agent blocking — infrastructure/rule review, not code.

author: zostay
body:
## Summary

Adds `/zed:maintenance <tag>` — a system-wide maintenance harness (e.g. weekly Dependabot sweeps) that discovers every project defining a `maintenance-<tag>` skill, runs each in a subagent, and streams progress to a local observability database that a lightweight web app renders live.

## What's included

**Skill** — `skills/maintenance/SKILL.md`, invoked as `/zed:maintenance <tag> [--now] [--fast] [--headless]`.
- Default: methodical **serial** subagents. `--fast`: parallel subagents. `--now`: explicitly selects the serial path.
- Honest about batch: Claude Code has no user-facing batch primitive for orchestrating subagents from a skill, so no fake batch API is claimed.

**Scripts** (`scripts/`)
- `maintenance-common.sh` — shared data-dir/path resolution + SQL escaping
- `maintenance-config.sh` — manages `config.json` (`searchRoots` + `blocklist`, default `~/projects`)
- `maintenance-discover.sh` — finds `maintenance-<tag>` skills under configured roots, applies blocklist, emits JSONL
- `maintenance-db.sh` — observability writer CLI (runs/jobs/events lifecycle)
- `maintenance-monitor.sh` — start/stop/status/url the web app, single-instance via pidfile
- `schema.sql` — SQLite schema

**Database** — SQLite (the ultralight choice) in **WAL mode with `busy_timeout`**, so `--fast` parallel subagent writes are corruption-safe (concurrent readers + serialized writers). Tables: `runs`, `jobs`, `events`.

**Observability web app** (`app/`) — Python 3 **standard library only** (no pip/npm/build):
- `server.py` — threading HTTP server, read-only SQLite, JSON API + SSE live stream, auto port-probe from 7373
- `static/*` — vanilla-JS UI: runs sidebar with red/green health pills, stage stepper, per-project job cards (green/red/amber/grey), counts header, live SSE updates with polling fallback, rendered Markdown summaries

**Docs** — README `maintenance` section, CHANGELOG `0.2.0` entry, `plugin.json` bumped to `0.2.0`, `__pycache__` ignored.

## Verification

Built via a multi-agent workflow against a shared design contract, then verified end-to-end in an isolated data dir: config → discovery → full DB lifecycle → live server API. The verify pass caught and fixed 3 real bugs (a SQL single-quote escaping bug used on every DB string write, and two integer/float comparison bugs in the monitor's poll loops). A conformance review confirmed the independently-built pieces interoperate; remaining findings are minor and benign.

## Notes

- Optional hardening not applied: `maintenance-db.sh` splices numeric `--run`/`--job` IDs into SQL without a numeric guard. String values are fully escaped (verified non-exploitable), and these IDs only come from the script's own integer output, so it's not exploitable in the documented flow — a `[[ =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]` guard would harden it further.

author: sdh07
body:
## What & why

cogni-knowledge had three planned contradiction surfaces, decomposed from #335 by #431:

- **(a)** `wiki-contradictor` at `knowledge-finalize` Step 10.6 — synthesis vs its cited source/distilled/question pages (shipped, v0.1.15).
- **(b)** `source-contradictor` at `knowledge-ingest` Step 4.6 — new source claims vs peer claims (shipped, v0.1.61).
- **(c)** synthesis-vs-prior-syntheses — **this PR (#444)**, the last deferred half.

The gap: (a) never compared a just-deposited synthesis against the **earlier syntheses on the same base**. Synthesis pages carry no claim block, so they were out of scope for the cheap claim-vs-claim surface (a)/(b) share. This PR locks the surface as **assertive-sentence-vs-assertive-sentence comparison**, reusing `wiki-contradictor`'s existing sentence discipline. No schema change; pure observability.

## How

A **second comparison pass (Pass B)** inside the *same* `wiki-contradictor` agent — no new agent, no new dispatch. Off the same sentence-split of the new synthesis body it already does for Pass A:

- **Pass A** (unchanged): new synthesis sentences × cited-page claims → findings with `clm`/`dcl`/`acl` `conflicting_claim_id`.
- **Pass B** (new): the same sentences × each prior synthesis's assertive sentences → findings with `conflicting_claim_id: null` and a synthesis-slug `conflicting_page`.

Findings merge into one `findings[]`; the `unknown` cap of 3 spans both passes.

### Key decisions
- **No schema change** — the finding shape already allowed a null `conflicting_claim_id`; `compared_against` gains additive `prior_syntheses[]` + `prior_synthesis_count`.
- **Scores ALL prior syntheses (capped, most-recent-first, `PRIOR_SYNTHESIS_MAX=20`), no similarity/theme pre-rank** — there is no theme index on syntheses; the conservative assertive-sentence discipline is the relevance filter (unrelated syntheses produce no findings).
- **Empty-`CITED_SOURCE_SLUGS` contract relaxed** — a 2nd+ synthesis with no claim-bearing cited peers now runs Pass B alone (skip only when BOTH lists are empty).
- **New `--no-prior-syntheses` flag** suppresses Pass B only; `--no-contradictor` still kills both.
- **Step 11 split** — `<n_cited> vs cited evidence` + `<n_prior> vs prior syntheses`, partitioned on `conflicting_claim_id` null-ness, plus an independent `prior-synthesis comparison truncated at 20/<N>` cap line.
- **De-collisioned the overloaded "(c)" label** — `wiki-contradictor` had used "approach (c) territory" for *cross-language scoring*; relabelled to "a separate, unshipped extension" since (c) now means this surface.

## Files
- `agents/wiki-contradictor.md` — Pass B + `PRIOR_SYNTHESIS_SLUGS` input, empty-CITED relaxation, label de-collision.
- `skills/knowledge-finalize/SKILL.md` — Step 10.6 enumeration + threading + widened skip + `--no-prior-syntheses`; Step 11 split.
- `tests/test_contradictor_contract.sh`, `tests/test_finalize_contract.sh` — strengthened/extended.
- `references/inverted-pipeline.md`, `references/differentiation-thesis.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — flip the deferred note to shipped, reconcile lettering.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — `0.1.61 → 0.1.62`.

## Verification
- All 43 cogni-knowledge contract test suites pass (incl. the two ingest-side regressions `test_source_contradictor_contract.sh` + `test_contradiction_ingest_store.sh`).
- Breadcrumb guard: 0 new violations (agent/SKILL files stay `#NNN`-free).
- Manual/local bake-in (the LLM scoring can't run in bash CI): on a base with ≥2 finalized syntheses on overlapping themes, confirm `contradictor-vN.json` has a populated `compared_against.prior_syntheses[]` and any Pass B findings carry `conflicting_claim_id: null`; `--no-prior-syntheses` suppresses Pass B while Pass A still appears; the first synthesis in a base (empty prior CSV) still runs Pass A.

Closes #444. With approach (b) already shipped, this lets #431 close.

author: alexeykuznetsov-dd
body:
# What Does This Do

POC to investigate if we can improve readability of tests by using syntax sugar from modern Java while still compiling
test classes to Java 8 bytecode using https://frgaal.org.

Only **ONE** test updated to show how it will be.

# Motivation

Many tests contain payload-heavy setup code, string concatenation for JSON/XML, simple dispatch switches, and casts that are harder to read than the behavior being tested. This POC explores using Frgaal for test sources only, so tests can use selected modern Java syntax while keeping the bytecode target compatible with Java 8.

| Feature                        | Java | Java 8 safe? | Worth using in tests?                                                      |
|--------------------------------|-----:|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Text blocks                    |   15 | Yes          | Yes, high value for JSON, SQL, XML, HTML payloads.                         |
| Switch expressions / `case ->` |   14 | Yes          | Yes, useful for compact mappings/assertion setup.                          |
| `instanceof` pattern variables |   16 | Yes          | Yes, removes noisy casts.                                                  |
| Local `var`                    |   10 | Yes          | Yes, but restrained. Good when RHS is obvious; avoid hiding fixture types. |

# Additional Notes

This is intentionally very limited: it is literally syntax sugar for test readability. Advanced modern Java features are
not part of this POC and should not be treated as generally available, especially features with runtime semantics such
as records, sealed classes, record patterns, preview features, module imports, or compact source files.

author: shayc
body:
Two minimal, additive import-integrity fixes from the design review.

## #1 — Identity: stop deriving `setId` from the filename
`setId` is now a random id ([random-id.ts](src/shared/utils/random-id.ts)) instead of the lowercased filename. Two distinct boards that share a filename can no longer **silently overwrite** each other — a re-import lands as its own visible, deletable set. Display names are disambiguated against existing sets (`"Core"` → `"Core (2)"`) so copies stay tellable apart.

**Tradeoff (intentional):** re-importing the *same* board now creates a duplicate rather than updating in place. A duplicate is visible and recoverable; the old clobber was invisible and permanent. A future conflict dialog ("Update existing / Keep both") composes cleanly on top of opaque identity.

## #2 — Atomicity: write the `boardSet` record last
`listBoardSets` reads **only** the `boardSets` store, so writing that record last makes it a commit marker: a failure mid-import leaves nothing visible instead of a board whose pictograms never landed. Adds an explicit `boardCount` to `UpsertBoardSetInput` (the count can't be back-filled from a set that doesn't exist yet).

## Tests
- Updated the two existing tests to capture the random `setId`.
- **New:** re-import → distinct set + disambiguated name.
- **New:** a failed import leaves the library and stores unchanged (no half-written set, no orphans).

**Scope note:** the failure test exercises the realistic failure (corrupt/unparseable file, which fails before any write). Pinning the exact write *ordering* would require injecting a fault into a storage internal, which the repo's testing rules (no mocking internals/native APIs) disallow — so the ordering is enforced by code + the success-path assertions rather than a fault-injection test.

## Deferred (additive, by design)
- Compensating delete + startup orphan-GC sweep for write-stage failures.
- Per-file import notifications.
- Conflict dialog for the duplicate case.

Verification: `npm run lint` clean · `npm test` 322 passed (38 files, real Chromium) · `npm run build` green.

### Motivation
- Make the Sea Breeze pages feel more premium, compact and usable on desktop while preserving responsive behavior and image quality. 
- Reduce visual noise (overly dominant vacancy CTA, framed gallery images) and focus hierarchy on listings and projects.
- Move filtering/search controls to a single horizontal row on desktop to save vertical space and improve discoverability.
- Fix listing detail gallery letterboxing/frames so photos always fill their container.

### Description
- Reduced hero heights across breakpoints by ~15-20% to produce a more compact desktop hero (`--hero-height-desktop`, `--hero-height-tablet`, `--hero-height-mobile`).
- Increased header logo sizing by ~10-15% while preserving aspect ratio and responsive breakpoints via updated `.site-logo` styles.
- Replaced the bright red vacancy CTA styling with a calmer slate/gray-blue gradient and adjusted hover/badge colors for a secondary, premium appearance (`button.vacancy-cta`, `.vacancy-badge`).

author: slotterbackw
body:
## Summary
Upgrades `@candidhealth/react-vitals` from `1.0.0-alpha.10` to `1.0.0-alpha.11`.

`alpha.10` had a packaging bug: its `exports` map listed `"development": "./index.ts"` first, but `index.ts` was not shipped in the published tarball (`files: ["dist", "theme.css"]`). Since conditional exports resolve by key order, Vite's dev server picked the missing source file and failed with *"Failed to resolve entry for package @candidhealth/react-vitals"*. (The production build was unaffected because it uses the `import`/`production` condition.)

`alpha.11` removes the `development` condition, so the dev server resolves cleanly to `dist/index.mjs` — no Vite config workaround needed.

## Changes
- `package.json`: bump `@candidhealth/react-vitals` to `1.0.0-alpha.11`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: updated accordingly

## Testing
- `pnpm dev` starts with no resolution errors; app serves at http://localhost:5173/ (200)

author: copilot
body:
When `EmbeddingService` builds providers internally (default path), repeated requests can leave Ollama `httpx.AsyncClient` instances open until GC. This change ensures provider-owned resources are explicitly closed at the end of each embedding generation call.

- **Lifecycle ownership and cleanup**
  - Track whether providers are service-owned (`providers is None`).
  - Wrap `generate_embeddings_for_document()` in `try/finally` and always run provider cleanup in `finally`.

- **Provider-agnostic close behavior**
  - Add `_aclose_owned_providers()` to close only owned providers.
  - If a provider exposes `aclose()`, invoke it and await only when the result is awaitable (supports async cleanup without forcing a stricter provider interface).

- **Focused regression coverage**
  - Add a close-tracking provider test to verify owned providers receive `aclose()` after generation.

```python
try:
    ...
    return EmbeddingGenerationResult(...)
finally:
    await self._aclose_owned_providers()
```

author: harsh-bh
body:
## Summary
Replaces network-dependent `getUser()` calls with local JWT verification via `getClaims()` across auth layer and middleware, reducing latency on every request. Adds React `cache()` wrapper to deduplicate verification within a single request. Introduces a loading skeleton for admin routes to improve perceived performance during data fetching.

## Key Changes
- **Auth optimization:** Replaced `supabase.auth.getUser()` with `supabase.auth.getClaims()` in `src/lib/session.ts` and `middleware.ts`
  - `getClaims()` verifies JWT locally using cached JWKS (no network round-trip) when asymmetric signing keys are enabled
  - Falls back to remote check for legacy symmetric keys, so never slower than `getUser()`
  - Still refreshes expired sessions automatically
  
- **Request deduplication:** Wrapped `getCurrentUser()` and `isAuthenticated()` with React `cache()` so multiple calls in the same request share a single verification instead of repeating it

- **Type simplification:** Created `SessionUser` type to match JWT claims structure (`id`, `email`, `user_metadata`) instead of importing full Supabase `User` type

- **Loading state:** Added `src/app/(admin)/loading.tsx` as a Suspense fallback for all admin routes
  - Shows skeleton UI instantly while page data loads
  - Enables Next.js prefetch of loading state for better perceived performance
  - Matches neobrutalism design system (border-2, rounded-base, shadow-shadow)

- **Minor cleanup:** Changed `let response` to `const response` in middleware (immutable reference)

## Implementation Details
- JWT claims extraction: `claims.sub` → user ID, `claims.email` → email, `claims.user_metadata` → metadata object
- Loading skeleton replicates typical admin table layout (header + 6 rows with 4 columns each)
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing middleware auth flow

### Motivation

### Motivation

- Ensure the CSV preview reflects manual edits held in `manual/support-worker-review.md` so users see the current manual action state after a rerun.
- Keep excluded/selected rows visible in the human-facing review artifacts even when the JSON pipeline excludes them.
- Mirror the `service-admin` pattern for reading/applying `action:` edits so conventions and tokens (e.g. `FORCE_EXCLUDE`, `1`) are consistent across pipelines.

### Description

- Parse explicit `action:` blocks from `manual/support-worker-review.md` into both a mapping by `job_id` and a set of preview rows via `_markdown_review_action_by_job_id` and new `_markdown_review_action_rows` helper.  This captures `action: exclude` / `action: select` as previewable rows. 
- Overlay Markdown actions onto the generated CSV preview by adding `_manual_review_csv_rows` and changing `write_manual_review_csv` to accept `markdown_actions`, applying `FORCE_EXCLUDE` for `exclude` and `1` for `select` by `job_id`.
- Keep actioned rows visible in the compact CSV preview by adding `_manual_review_preview_rows` and feeding those rows (including preserved action rows) to the CSV writer; regenerate the CSV preview on every run (but continue to treat the Markdown file as the editable source of truth). 
- Regenerate compact Markdown output while preserving explicit `action:` edits and wire preserved action rows into the Markdown writer so actioned rows remain visible in the compact review even if the JSON output excludes them; update CLI messaging to reflect CSV refresh semantics.

### Testing

author: jmayeur
body:
## Problem

`envdata` rows were purged immediately after aggregation (24 h cutoff).
If the daily AQI scoring cron job on `aqi-impact` failed or ran late,
the raw minute-level readings for that window were already gone and
unrecoverable — only the hourly averages (which understate peak AQI)
remained.

## Changes

### 1 — Aggregation checkpoint (`agg_meta` table)

A new `agg_meta` key/value table stores the Unix timestamp of the last
successful aggregation run (`last_agg_checkpoint`).

- Created with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` — completely self-bootstrapping, no migration needed.
- On the first run the checkpoint is `0`, so behaviour is identical to before.
- `readUnprocessedData(newerThan, olderThan)` replaces `readOldData(olderThan)` and adds a `time > checkpoint` lower bound so each 10-minute tick only processes rows it hasn't seen before.
- The checkpoint is written **only after both** `updateFinalAggs` and `updateHourPeaks` succeed. A partial failure leaves the checkpoint unmoved; the next tick retries automatically.

### 2 — 30-day purge window

`purgeOldData()` is now called with a 30-day cutoff instead of 24 h.
Minute-level data accumulates for ~30 days (~43 k rows, trivial for SQLite),
giving a wide safety window for any replayed or late-running scoring jobs.
The two operations are now decoupled: aggregation and purge run
independently, so a purge always happens even when there is nothing new
to aggregate.

### Other cleanup

- Flattened the nested promise chain in `main()` into a linear `.then()` chain — easier to follow and ensures `close()` is always called on both success and error paths.
- Removed `console.log('success', ...)` noise from `updateFinalAggs` / `updateHourPeaks`; meaningful progress is now logged from `main()`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy to Pi; confirm `agg_meta` table is created automatically on first run
- [ ] Verify log output shows `Aggregation window: <checkpoint> → <cutoff>` and `Checkpoint advanced to …`
- [ ] Confirm `envdata` rows older than 30 days are removed and rows newer than 30 days are retained
- [ ] Simulate an aggregation failure (e.g., kill mid-run); confirm checkpoint does not advance and the next tick re-processes the same window

author: haggyroth
body:
## Summary

Phase E (final phase) from REVIEW.md. Six targeted improvements — no architecture changes, all independently safe.

| ID | Change | File |
|---|---|---|
| SEC-9 | Exec temp files → `os.tmpdir()` | `codeTools.ts` |
| BUG-5 | Allow spaces in `save_file` filenames | `fileTools.ts` |
| CON-3 | Remove `gh_push` (duplicate of `git_push`) | `githubTools.ts` |
| BUG-8 | Linux clipboard: try `wl-paste/wl-copy` → `xclip` → `xsel` | `miscTools.ts` |
| BUG-9 | `read_document` — remove DOMMatrix polyfill, fix API call | `miscTools.ts` |
| PERF-1 | Memory DB connection cache + single migration | `memoryTools.ts` |

### Details

**SEC-9** — `run_javascript` and `run_python` wrote temp scripts into the workspace (`cwd`), so `temp_script_*.ts/py` appeared in `list_directory` output and could be matched by `delete_files_by_pattern`. Moved to `os.tmpdir()` with a namespaced prefix.

**BUG-5** — `save_file` rejected filenames with spaces (`/[ \*\?<>|"]/`). `my report.md` was a validation error. Removed the space from the disallowed set.

**CON-3** — `gh_push` shelled out to `git push origin` and had no set-upstream support, no force flag, and no remote/branch selection. `git_push` (PR #4) does all of this. Removed with a comment pointing to the replacement.

**BUG-8** — On Linux, clipboard only tried `xclip`, which fails on Wayland and many distros. New `tryClipboardCmds()` helper tries candidates in order and returns a clear install hint if all fail:
- Read: `wl-paste` → `xclip` → `xsel`
- Write: `wl-copy` → `xclip` → `xsel`

**BUG-9** — The PDF branch used a non-standard `new PDFParse({ data: buffer })` constructor, monkey-patched `global.DOMMatrix` as a side effect, and mixed `require()` for PDF with `await import()` for DOCX. Replaced with the standard `pdf-parse(buffer)` call, removed the polyfill, and documented the require-vs-import rationale consistently.

**PERF-1** — Every memory tool call opened a fresh `better-sqlite3` connection (synchronous file open + schema check) and re-ran `migrateLegacyFile()` (async `readFile` of `memory.md`). Replaced `openDb()` with `getDb()` backed by a `Map<dbPath, {db, migrationDone}>`. First call opens + migrates; all subsequent calls return the cached handle with no I/O.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test`: 163 pass / 0 fail / 12 skipped (unchanged)
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean
- [ ] Smoke: `run_python` — `os.tmpdir()` shows no `temp_script_*.py` in workspace
- [ ] Smoke: `save_file` with `file_name: "my report.md"` succeeds
- [ ] Smoke: `git_push` still works; `gh_push` is gone from tool list
- [ ] Smoke: `read_clipboard`/`write_clipboard` work on Wayland (wl-paste/wl-copy)
- [ ] Smoke: `read_document` on a PDF returns text without DOMMatrix errors
- [ ] Smoke: multiple `save_memory` calls in a session are faster (single DB open)

body:
## What
Silences the benign **`KubeMemoryOvercommit`** alert (and its sibling `KubeCPUOvercommit`) by stripping them from the `kubernetes-resources` PrometheusRule group on the omv cluster.

## Why
On this asymmetric 2-node cluster (omv 8 GiB vs omv-ha ~1 GiB), the HA branch of the overcommit expression is **permanently true** — if omv is lost, omv-ha can't hold the rescheduled requests. There's no actionable fix without more hardware, so it's pure Slack noise. `k8s/cluster-protection/apply-prometheus-rule-tuning.sh` already documents this and strips it — but that script runs over **SSH**, which a cloud session can't use.

## How
Adds the strip to the **kubectl-based** `scripts/prometheus-tune.sh`, which runs via the existing `prometheus-tune.yml` workflow (Tailscale + `KUBECONFIG_B64`, posts results to issue #382). Merging this to `main` touches `scripts/prometheus-tune.sh`, which **triggers that workflow** to apply it live.

- Discovers the owning PrometheusRule by **alert presence** (no hardcoded chart object name).
- Removes only the two overcommit alerts; keeps the rest of every group.
- **Idempotent** — re-stripping a missing alert is a no-op.

## Verified (offline)
- `bash -n scripts/prometheus-tune.sh` clean.
- jq discovery + patch filters validated against a mock PrometheusRule: only the right object is selected, both overcommit alerts removed, other alerts + recording rules preserved.

> Note: like the rest of the tuning, this is reversed by a `helm upgrade` of kube-prometheus-stack; the durable fix is the chart's `defaultRules` values. Stripping matches the existing operational pattern.

author: rotium
body:
The previous guard was `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang"` only. The
  arm64 CI runs an **older Clang** that doesn't know that warning, and passing
  an unknown `-Wno-error=deprecated-literal-operator` is *itself* an error there
  under `-Werror` (`-Wunknown-warning-option`):

      error: unknown warning option '-Werror=deprecated-literal-operator'; did
      you mean '-Werror=deprecated-copy-dtor'? [-Werror,-Wunknown-warning-option]

  `-Wdeprecated-literal-operator` was introduced in **Clang 17** — which is also
  the only range where the flutter_secure_storage json actually fails — so add a
  `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_VERSION VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL 17` condition. Older Clang
  and GCC never receive the flag.

body:
## Summary
- add a typed `MetadataInput.metadata_template_key` field for metadata source routing
- enforce one canonical SDK request key: `metadata_template_key`
- add contract and endpoint regression coverage proving non-canonical keys do not populate the field
- refresh the generated SDK capability manifest

## Why this is needed
APITree widgets generated from app contracts can define multiple metadata sources. Native apps with more than one metadata source need a routing key to decide which tree to return from `/workflows/v1/metadata`.

The SDK contract should expose one consistent way to do this, not absorb every platform or app-specific spelling. Heracles owns the native/platform normalization layer and now maps incoming `metadataTemplateKey` into the SDK-canonical `metadata_template_key` before calling app handlers.

This keeps the SDK boundary typed and strict: apps read `input.metadata_template_key`; callers that send `metadataTemplateKey` or `type` directly to the SDK do not populate this field. That avoids making legacy/proxy payload names part of the SDK contract.

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The scraper was vulnerable to a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) bypass. While the initial URL was validated against internal IP ranges using `is_safe_url`, `requests.get()` follows HTTP redirects by default. An attacker could provide a safe external URL that redirects to a malicious internal IP (e.g., `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254`), bypassing the pre-request validation.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could scan internal networks, access private metadata services, or interact with unauthenticated internal APIs by leveraging the scraper as an open proxy.
🔧 Fix: Set `allow_redirects=False` in the `requests.get()` call to prevent automatic following of redirects. The test mock `side_effect` was updated to accept `**kwargs` to accommodate this new argument.
✅ Verification: Ensure the test suite passes, and the codebase is linted. The diffs confirm that `requests.get` now explicitly disables redirects.

<!--
Write a short description of the changes included in this pull request,
also include relevant motivation and context. Have in mind the following

The `runway-ota-rc.yml` caller workflow was missing the `actions: read`
permission required by the `slack-rc-notification.yml` reusable
workflow.

GitHub Actions enforces that a reusable workflow cannot use permissions
that the calling workflow has not already granted.
`slack-rc-notification.yml` declares `actions: read` (needed by
`actions/download-artifact@v4` to download the Android Play Store check
report), but `runway-ota-rc.yml` only granted `contents: read`,
`pull-requests: read`, and `id-token: write`. This caused the workflow
validation step to fail with:

requesting 'actions: read', but is only allowed 'actions: none'.

The fix adds `actions: read` to the `permissions` block in
`runway-ota-rc.yml`.

body: Live smoke test of the merged Postiz pipeline (#856) surfaced two real bugs and a missing safety mode. All three fixed in this PR. ## What the smoke test caught Running locally with all keys present: - X thread + 1 X trend post drafted to Postiz successfully (2/5) - 3 IG drafts ALL failed at upload with `400 Unsupported file type` - Root cause when traced: `https://pitchrank.io/api/infographic/movers?platform=instagram` returns `200` with `Content-Type: image/png` but `Content-Length: 0` (empty body). All three infographic routes do. ## Root cause Step 14 of the merged Postiz migration switched the wordmark from text to an SVG logo via ``. Satori (the @vercel/og renderer) does not support SVG inside `` — it returns an empty buffer instead of an error. The endpoints look healthy (200 OK, correct Content-Type) but render nothing. ## Three fixes 1. **PNG logo asset** — `frontend/public/logos/logo-primary.png` (copied from the brand's existing 800w PNG). 2. **LOGO_URL points to PNG, not SVG** — `frontend/app/api/infographic/_shared/assets.ts`. Inline comment explains why so a future contributor doesn't flip it back. 3. **Filename extension inference in Postiz upload** — `_upload_to_postiz` in `scripts/marketing_pipeline.py` now derives `.png`/`.jpg`/etc from the Content-Type header. Postiz validates by file extension; the URL-derived filename `movers` (no extension) was a second, latent reason the upload would fail. ## Bonus: `--postiz-only` CLI flag Lets you run the full live pipeline against Postiz without firing the Beehiiv newsletter or committing a blog post. Use for ad-hoc smoke tests: ```bash python scripts/marketing_pipeline.py --postiz-only ``` ## Test plan - [x] 37 unit tests still pass. - [x] Live `--postiz-only` run drafts 2/5 to Postiz today (X thread + trend) and 0/3 IG due to the empty-image bug. - [ ] After this PR merges and Vercel deploys, re-run `python scripts/marketing_pipeline.py --postiz-only` (or `gh workflow run marketing-pipeline.yml -f dry_run=false`) and confirm 5/5 drafts including IG with valid `uploads.postiz.com` paths. Worth noting: the empty-image regression has been live since PR #856 merged, but no IG drafts were attempted yet because the marketing pipeline workflow is currently `workflow_dispatch`-only. No production traffic was affected.

## Summary

Closes #208 / [SKY-446](/SKY/issues/SKY-446)

One-line fix in `electron-main/src/vault.test.ts`: canonicalise `dstDir` via `fs.realpathSync.native()` before building the rename spy's expected path in the atomic-write crash test.

**Why:** On macOS `os.tmpdir()` returns `/var/...` but `realSafePath()` resolves the path through `realpathSync.native` to `/private/var/...`. Normalising `dstDir` through `realpathSync.native` before constructing `dstFull` makes the spy intercept correctly on both Linux and macOS.

**Change:** `const dstFull = path.join(fs.realpathSync.native(dstDir), 'crash.md');`

> **Note:** This is a clean rebase of PR #243 onto current `main`. PR #243 was based on top of unmerged branch `feat(SKY-156)`, causing merge conflicts. This PR isolates only the one-line SKY-446 fix.

author: banse
body:
## packet
Schema: `spark-compete-hotfix-v1` · Event: `spark-compete-first-event` · Submission: public_repo_pr

## team
**The Dudes** — His Dudeness, El Duderino, Duder. LLM device holder: His Dudeness (github `banse`). GitHub accounts: `banse`.

## pr_author
`banse`

## repo
`vibeforge1111/spark-telegram-bot`

## actual_behavior
`shouldAnswerAuthoritativeRuntimeStatus` (`src/index.ts:1194`) decides whether a message is a live runtime-status question. Several of its checks use `.*` that spans the **entire** message, e.g.:
```js
/\b(?:is|are)\s+(?:spawner|telegram|spark|systems?|stack)\b.*\b(?:healthy|running|online|up|live|supervised)\b/
/\b(?:spawner|telegram)\b.*\b(?:healthy|running|supervised|stopped|offline|online|up|down)\b/
/\b(?:raw|debug|details?|full|exact)\b.*\b(?:live|health|status|state)\b/
```
The gating `runtimeTruthSignals(text).live` is itself satisfied by any text mentioning "spark/telegram/spawner" plus a "status/state/running" word. So a long pasted document — e.g. the Spark Compete brief (which mentions "Spark", "Telegram", "Spawner UI", "running", "status", "state") — trips both the gate and the `.*`-spanning patterns. The result: when an operator pastes the brief and asks for help, `handleTextMessage` (`index.ts:6031`) short-circuits to the authoritative live-status report ("Spark is healthy right now / Live loop / Telegram: polling / …") instead of answering the request. (Telegram also splits the long paste into multiple messages, each routed independently.)

## expected_behavior
The authoritative runtime-status answer should only be returned for a genuine, concise status question (e.g. "are the spawner and telegram systems running?"), not for a long pasted document that merely mentions these words in passing.

## repro_steps
1. Paste a long document mentioning Spark/Telegram/Spawner and a status/running word in passing — e.g. the public Spark Compete brief — prefixed with a normal request like "Can you help me test to find bugs? Here's the brief: …".
2. Observe the reply is the live status report ("Spark is healthy right now …"), unrelated to the request.
3. Deterministic: `node node_modules/ts-node/dist/bin.js tests/runtimeStatusBoundary.test.ts` — the new test asserts `shouldAnswerAuthoritativeRuntimeStatus(brief) === false`; fails before the fix, passes after.

## before_after_proof
**SMOKE / redacted conversation excerpt** (user → bot intent, observed): user pastes "Can you help me test to find bugs? Here's the brief: … Spark … Telegram … Spawner UI … status: live … the systems are running." **BEFORE:** bot replies with the live status report ("Spark is healthy right now / Live loop / Telegram: polling / Mission Control: ready / …"), unrelated to the request. **AFTER (this PR):** that paste no longer routes to the status report and is handled as a normal request. **DETERMINISTIC TEST** `tests/runtimeStatusBoundary.test.ts`: BEFORE the fix the long-pasted-brief case fails with `AssertionError` (`shouldAnswerAuthoritativeRuntimeStatus(brief)` returns `true`); AFTER, both cases pass — the brief returns `false`, while genuine concise questions ("are the spawner and telegram systems running?", "what is the current live state?", "show me the raw live status") still return `true`. Related suites green: conversationIntent 80, runtimeFreshness 4, runtimeSyncCompatibility 1, accessPolicy 16, naturalRouteDecision 28 — 0 failures.

## tests_or_smoke
`node node_modules/ts-node/dist/bin.js tests/runtimeStatusBoundary.test.ts` (2 tests; the pasted-brief case fails pre-fix, passes post-fix). Plus the live smoke above. No new failures across the related suites.

## duplicate_notes
No open PR/issue addresses `shouldAnswerAuthoritativeRuntimeStatus` / the runtime-status over-match on long input. The "over-broad intent predicate misroutes X" theme has several open PRs, but each targets a **different** predicate by root cause — #421 (memory-doctor pattern), #367 (routeFirewall false positives), #377 (memory/voice state checks), #426 (market-chart prompts → Memory Doctor), #447 (no-execution replies). None touch the runtime-status predicate. This is also a distinct root cause from the sibling browser-proof boundary fix (different function, different lane). Re-checked open spark-telegram-bot PRs immediately before submission.

## risk_notes
Low risk. The change adds a single length bound at the top of `shouldAnswerAuthoritativeRuntimeStatus`; it can only make the predicate return `true` **less** often, so it cannot newly suppress a legitimate non-status reply (over-narrowing degrades gracefully to normal chat). The gating `runtimeTruthSignals().live` and the individual patterns are unchanged, so genuine concise status questions still match (covered by the test). No secrets/installer/CI/dependency surface touched.

## review_claim
Impact: medium (core conversational routing returns an unrelated system status report to a normal message). Evidence: failing_test, passing_test, smoke_test, redacted_conversation_excerpt. Requested review state: `pr_review`. Scope: `shouldAnswerAuthoritativeRuntimeStatus` only; other routing predicates are unchanged and out of scope for this PR.

## Summary

W5.3 follow-up. Applies the same `*.accessibility.test.tsx` scaffold landed in #106 (ARIA Labels and Roles / Keyboard Navigation / Focus Management / Screen Reader Support) to three more component archetypes:

### What ships

- **Drawer** — slide-in overlay focus management. aria-modal carried unconditionally across every position variant (left/right/top/bottom), auto-generated `aria-labelledby` ↔ heading id wiring when `title` prop is used, the dev-only "missing accessible name" `console.warn` fires when none of the three naming paths (`title` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`) is provided, `closeOnEscape={false}` opt-out works, close button is keyboard-activatable, overlay is `aria-hidden` so AT walks straight to the dialog.
- **Tabs** — keyboard arrow nav + roving tabindex. `tablist` / `tab` / `tabpanel` role wiring, `aria-orientation` reflects local prop override + context, panel ↔ tab `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` deterministic pairing, `aria-selected` mutual exclusivity, ArrowLeft/Right wrap-around at boundaries, disabled tabs skipped by arrow nav, roving tabindex (active=0, others=-1), external Tab from outside lands on the **active** tab not the first one.
- **Accordion** — disclosure pattern (WAI-ARIA APG). Each header is a `button` with `aria-expanded` tracking state, `aria-controls` ↔ panel id pairing, panel `aria-hidden` flips with open state, Enter **and** Space both toggle, disabled items not activatable even when forcibly focused, chevron icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`), panel ids unique across items.

### Pattern scope

Now **7/62** component dirs (Header pre-existing + Modal/Pagination/Breadcrumb from #106 + these 3). Same scaffold shape across all of them — future a11y suites can lift the section structure verbatim.

### Numbers

- **+29 tests** (9 Drawer + 11 Tabs + 9 Accordion). Suite total: 988 → 1017.
- Zero new dependencies.
- No production code touched.

## Test plan

Tabs and Accordion suites emit React `act()` warnings on a couple of automatic-mode focus transitions / state updates. ## Summary

Ports the WinForms `ImageUtilSkillSystemsAnimeCreator` **EXPORT** path to a cross-platform Core seam (`SkillSystemsAnimeExportCore`, read-only) and wires the SkillConfig views' `AnimationExport_Click`. Exports a skill animation → `.txt` script + per-frame PNGs + optional GIF. **Import is a separate deferred follow-up** (out of scope). Closes #910.

Skill animations use the 5-pointer "anime config" format (NOT standard battle-anime), so this is a fresh Core port reusing the merged TSA-composite + GIF infrastructure.

## What changed
- **New Core `SkillSystemsAnimeExportCore.cs`** (read-only):
  - `SkipCode(rom, animeAddr)` → `(configAddr, isDefender)`: FE8J (`is_multibyte`) returns the address directly; FE8U memcmps the 0x150 program-code prefix vs `config/patch2/FE8U/skill/skillanimtemplate*.dmp` (via `CoreState.BaseDirectory`) → `addr + dmp.Length` + D-flag.

author: benmsanderson
body:
## Summary

Performance work on the upwelling-diffusion thermal model. **All changes are bit-identical** — output of the full SSP245 1750–2100 run matches `main` byte-for-byte across all seven output files, and the full test suite (113 tests) passes.

Three commits, each one logical step:

1. **Solve via LAPACK `?gtsv` instead of `solve_banded`** — the per-substep tridiagonal solve (~8400/run) went through `scipy.linalg.solve_banded`, which spends most of its time on input validation and banded-format bookkeeping. Bind the LAPACK tridiagonal solver once and call it directly. Single largest win.
2. **Precompute run-constant parts of `coeff`** — the geometry-only (`dz`/`rakapa`/`dt`) divisions in the a/b/c coefficient arrays are hoisted out of the per-substep loop; only the `wcfac`/`gam_fro_fac` terms are recomputed per call.
3. **Hoist deep-layer diffusion factors out of the `energy_budget` loop** — `beto*dt/(c1*dz)` (and the `fnso`-scaled southern variant) is run-constant but was rebuilt as an array division on every substep.

## Measured impact (SSP245 → 2100, `_run` wall-clock, 5 runs)

| Step | `_run` mean | Δ |
|---|---|---|
| before this PR | 0.889s | — |
| LAPACK gtsv | 0.616s | −0.218s |
| precompute coeff | 0.547s | −0.069s |
| hoist deep-layer factors | 0.520s | −0.027s |

(Numbers measured in the full speedup chain; the gtsv swap alone is ~15% of total run time.)

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest` full suite — 113 passed
- [x] Bit-identical output vs `main` (all 7 SSP245 output files, byte-compared)
- [ ] Reviewer sanity check on the `?gtsv` diagonal mapping (sub=`a[:-1]`, main=`b`, super=`c[1:]`)

author: jjfantini
body:
Phase 2 — the provider seam the indexing engine calls, landing with **zero new external dependencies** and full offline test coverage.

## What
- **Provider** interface (`Complete`/`Name`) + typed `RetryableError`/`IsRetryable` (transient vs permanent) and `ErrCircuitOpen`.
- **Resilience** (`ResilientProvider`): hand-rolled circuit breaker with an **injectable clock** + bounded exponential-backoff retry with an **injectable wait** — so timing is deterministically testable. Rate limiting via a `Limiter` interface that `*x/time/rate.Limiter` satisfies (caller injects; no dep here).
- **Cache**: prompt-hash `CacheKey` (sha256 of model+messages+temp); `MemoryCache`/`FileCache`; read-through `CachingProvider`. This is both the 'don't burn retries / cheap re-runs' lever and the deterministic **cassette seam**.
- **Structured output**: `ExtractJSON` (```json fences + trailing-comma tolerance → **typed error**, never silent `{}`); generic `CompleteJSON` **validate-then-retry** that re-prompts with the error (works at temperature 0; **preserves `thinking` CoT fields**, no constrained decoding).
- **MockProvider** (scripted + recording) — the test/cassette base.
- **Tokens**: `TokenCounter` (offline `HeuristicCounter`) + `GroupPages` (port of `page_list_to_group_text`: token-bounded, overlapping, physical-index tagged).

## Verification
`go test -race ./internal/llm` green: retry-after-transient, permanent-not-retried, exhaust, breaker-opens-and-fails-fast, breaker-recovers-after-cooldown, backoff caps, cache hit + persistence, JSON extraction, validate-then-retry, page chunking.

## Deferred (follow-up)
Concrete OpenAI/Anthropic adapters + a tiktoken-backed `TokenCounter` (need the SDKs + live keys to exercise) land in a focused PR so this stays green/tight. The engine (P4) builds and tests against `MockProvider` meanwhile.

author: svandragt
body:
Follow-up to #310: make the browser (Playwright) suite block merges too — without adding a second required status check.

## Why not just require the `playwright` check?

The old `playwright.yml` was path-filtered at the workflow trigger (`src/**`, `e2e/**`, …). A required check from a `paths:`-filtered workflow **hangs as "pending" forever** on PRs that don't trigger it — which would permanently block every docs-only PR. So instead it's folded into the existing single `ci` gate.

## How

- A **`changes`** job (`dorny/paths-filter`) detects e2e-relevant edits (`src/**`, `e2e/**`, `playwright.config.ts`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`).
- The **`playwright`** job runs only when those change; otherwise it's *skipped*, keeping docs-only PRs fast.
- The **`ci`** gate now also `needs: playwright` and fails on a real failure/cancellation, while treating `skipped` as a pass.
- The CI workflow itself always runs, so the required `ci` context is always reported.
- Removes the now-redundant `playwright.yml`.

Net: a Playwright failure on a PR touching `src/**` turns `ci` red and blocks the merge; a docs-only PR skips Playwright and still passes. **No ruleset change needed** — `ci` stays the only required check.

Docs: `.github/rulesets/README.md` updated to reflect that Playwright is now gated via `ci` rather than advisory.

author: doesdev
body:
## Stage S6b — enrich the per-target project-mode scaffolders + fix Go `core.error`

Fills each per-target `Scaffolder` body (`bock-codegen/src/scaffold.rs`) with the **full project-mode scaffolding** (spec §20.6.2), honoring the parsed `[targets.<T>]` (deep) / `[targets.<T>.scaffolding]` (shallow) config with target-appropriate defaults, and fixes the pre-existing Go `core.error` field/method collision (Q-go-error-message). Project-mode only — `--source-only` stays bare.

### Per-target scaffolding emitted

| Target | Manifest | Test framework (default) | Formatter | Linter (opt-in) | Pkg-mgr hint (README) |
|--------|----------|--------------------------|-----------|-----------------|------------------------|
| JS | `package.json` (name/version/`type:module`/test script + framework devDep) | Vitest (or Jest) | Prettier `.prettierrc.json` unless `none` | `eslint.config.js` | npm/pnpm/yarn |
| TS | `package.json` + `tsconfig.json` (NodeNext, strict) + `typescript` devDep | Vitest (or Jest) | Prettier | `eslint.config.js` | npm/pnpm/yarn |
| Python | `pyproject.toml` (metadata + pytest/unittest + Black/Ruff format) | pytest (or unittest) | Black (or Ruff/none) | ruff/pylint config | pip/Poetry/uv |
| Rust | `Cargo.toml` (`[package]`+`[[bin]]`, tokio only when concurrency runtime present) | cargo test (universal) | rustfmt (universal, no config) | `clippy.toml` | (cargo only) |
| Go | `go.mod` (module path from `[targets.go] module` or name slug) | `go test` (universal) | gofmt (universal, no config) | `.golangci.yml` | (go mod only) |

Each target also emits a **README first-contact** (run + test instructions honoring the package-manager hint). Shallow linter configs are **opt-in** — emitted only when `[targets.<T>.scaffolding].linter` is set. Unset deep fields take the §20.6.2 defaults.

**Tests:** thorough new unit tests in `scaffold.rs` assert manifest/config/README content per target, per default-vs-explicit selection, and that shallow configs appear only when set (41 scaffold tests).

### TS run-plan change (required by the tsconfig)

`bock-build/src/toolchain.rs`: TS run plan `tsc main.ts` → **`tsc -p .`**. With a scaffolded `tsconfig.json` always present in project mode, the single-file invocation fails TS5112 (*"tsconfig.json is present but will not be loaded if files are specified on commandline"*). Building by project honors the config and compiles the whole per-module `.ts` tree. Per-file build-time validation is unaffected (it runs from the project root, where no tsconfig exists). Run-plan unit test updated.

### Go `core.error` fix (Q-go-error-message)

`core.error` declares `record SimpleError { message }` **and** `fn message(self)`. The Go backend emitted both as `Message` on the struct → `go build` rejects "type SimpleError has both field and method named Message", so `.message()` never compiled on Go. New `go_method_name` disambiguates a public method whose PascalCased name collides with a record field to `<Name>Method`, applied **uniformly** at the trait interface, the receiver method, and every call site (field stays `Message`). Verified end-to-end: `go run .` on a `core.error` program prints the message.

Locked by:
- a `go.rs` unit test (`method_colliding_with_field_is_disambiguated`),
- new `conformance/exec/exec_core_error.bock` (executes `.message()` cross-target on **rust + go**).

### Docs
- `docs/src/reference/tooling.md`: new **Project-Mode Scaffolding** section (per-target file list + config table) + the `tsc -p .` note + updated per-target output descriptions.
- `docs/src/reference/project-schema.md`: replaced the stale "scaffolding bodies still being filled in" note with the now-implemented per-target output. mdBook builds clean.

### Deferred to S7 (NOT in this PR)
The transpiled `@test` **files** (Vitest/Jest/pytest/`cargo test`/`go test` test code) and the formatter-clean `--check` release gate. S6b only sets up manifests/configs that *reference* the framework.

### FOUND — pre-existing js/ts/python `core.error` collision
The same field/method-name collision is a pre-existing bug on **js/ts/python**, surfaced while adding the cross-target fixture:
- **TS** — `tsc` "Duplicate identifier 'message'" (hard compile error).
- **JS** — the instance field set in the constructor shadows the prototype method, so `e.message` is the string and `e.message()` is "not a function".
- **Python** — the `@dataclass` field overwrites the method; `e.message()` calls the string.

Fixed for **Go** here. The js/ts/python equivalents are structural shadowing (not just a name clash) and need their own per-backend disambiguation — a separate follow-up. The exec fixture restricts to `rust, go` so conformance stays 0-failed. Recommend the orchestrator queue this as `FOUND: core.error .message() collision on js/ts/python`.

cargo test --workspace                                     # 0 (incl. conformance exec test: 2 passed, 0 failed)
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features   # 0

author: dmerrick
body:
## Context

The dashcam `PersistentVolume` is **host-specific** (NAS server IP + export path), so the committed `dist/` shipped it with `<NFS server address>` / `<export path>` placeholders. That broke a clean GitOps create: on a fresh stage rebuild, Argo would create the PV *with placeholders* and the mount would fail. The kustomize-era workaround was `kubectl apply`-ing a gitignored `dashcam-nfs.local.yaml` by hand — exactly the open TODO ("dashcam PV NFS placeholder breaks a clean GitOps create").

This surfaced live during the stage Argo cutover.

## Approach

Treat the PV as what it actually is — **per-cluster bootstrap infrastructure** (like the NFS server itself), not app config — and keep it out of Argo's reconcile loop entirely. These coords aren't a secret (LAN IP + NAS path), so no ESO/SM; the right mechanism is synth-time injection, which cdk8s already supports via `$NFS_SERVER`/`$NFS_PATH`.

- Split `emit_dashcam_volume` → `emit_dashcam_pvc` (Argo-managed, stays in `DataChart`) + `emit_dashcam_pv` (new `DashcamPVChart` → `dist/<env>-dashcam-pv.k8s.yaml`).
- Neither `ApplicationSet` globs that file (they match `<env>-{apps,data}.k8s.yaml`), so the PV is **out of Argo by construction**. Dropped the now-dead `ignoreDifferences`.
- New `task k8s:<env>:dashcam-pv` synths *just* the PV with real coords from the gitignored `cdk8s/dashcam-nfs.local.env` and applies it. `main.py` now honors `CDK8S_OUTDIR`, so it renders to a throwaway dir — the committed golden never gets real coords. (`cp dashcam-nfs.local.env.example …` to set up.)
- The PVC stays Argo-managed and binds to the PV by name.

Also drops a latent bug: the PV previously carried `namespace: stage-1` (PVs are cluster-scoped); the dedicated chart emits it without one.

## Verification

- Golden gate green (`task cdk8s:check`); unit tests updated + split (PVC-is-Argo-managed-without-PV, PV-is-own-cluster-scoped-unit).
- Confirmed the task mechanics: temp-dir synth produces real coords while `dist/` keeps placeholders.

Resolves the dashcam-PV-placeholder TODO.

author: jakechampion
body:
Implements the **bounds-checked** policy you chose for out-of-bounds array indexing (the fork flagged in #1807). Out-of-range `xs[i]` / `xs[i] = v` previously diverged three ways:

| `xs[5]` on a len-3 array | interp | x86-64 | arm64 | wasm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | error | **returns 0** | **returns 0** | trap |

The natives silently read/wrote past the end and returned garbage. Now every backend **aborts** instead.

## What changed

Every `__arr_idx*` / `__slice_idx*` helper on **x86-64 and arm64** now compares the index against the array's length prefix (`[base-4]`) or the slice header's length (`[slice+4]`) before computing the element address — a single unsigned compare that catches both a negative index and `index >= len` — and aborts with **exit code 134** on failure. That's the same trap the string-slice helper already used, and what wasm's `unreachable` produces under wasmtime, so all backends now agree on the observable contract:

| | interp | x86-64 | arm64 | wasm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| out of bounds | error, exit ≠0 | exit 134 | exit 134 | exit 134 |
| in range | value | value | value | value |

Covers reads, writes, and every element stride (1/2/4/8/16). In-range accesses are unchanged.

## Tests / docs

- `internal/e2e/array_bounds_test.go` — out-of-range reads / writes / negative indices / slice indexing all abort on every codegen backend; in-range indexing across widths, loops, and slices still agrees.
- `docs/ARRAY-BOUNDS.md` documents the contract (the array counterpart to `docs/INTEGER-SEMANTICS.md` / `docs/FLOAT-SEMANTICS.md`).

Full suite green.

This closes the out-of-bounds divergence the cross-area differential sweep (#1807) surfaced.

author: nawidhashimi786-ui
body:
# Week 9 Security Audit

## IAM Audit

### Before Changes

| Role |
|--------|
| roles/artifactregistry.writer |
| roles/compute.networkAdmin |
| roles/iam.serviceAccountUser |
| roles/run.admin |
| roles/storage.admin |
| roles/viewer |

### After Changes

| Role |
|--------|
| roles/artifactregistry.writer |
| roles/compute.networkAdmin |
| roles/iam.serviceAccountUser |
| roles/run.developer |
| roles/viewer |

## Reflection

### Q1: Why is roles/run.admin inappropriate for a CI/CD pipeline service account?

roles/run.admin is too broad for a CI/CD pipeline because it allows the service account to delete Cloud Run services, change IAM permissions, and make other administrative changes. A deployment pipeline only needs enough access to deploy and update services, so roles/run.developer follows the principle of least privilege.

### Q2: What is the security difference between storing a secret in GitHub Secrets vs. Google Secret Manager?

GitHub Secrets stores secrets inside GitHub and can be accessed by workflows. Google Secret Manager stores secrets in Google Cloud and provides centralized access control, audit logging, and better security management. This reduces the risk of exposing sensitive information.

### Q3: A coworker says "I will clean up IAM permissions after the project launches. For now I need everything to work fast." What is the risk of this approach?

Waiting until after launch to reduce permissions can leave the environment over-permissioned and vulnerable to misuse or compromise. If an account is breached, an attacker may gain unnecessary access. Applying least privilege from the beginning improves security.

author: benmsanderson
body:
## Summary

One logical idea applied across the run loop: in the hot per-year path we were repeatedly doing pandas `DataFrame`/`Series` scalar lookups (`df[col][yr]`), which carry significant per-access overhead. Cache the relevant columns as numpy arrays once and index them positionally. **All changes are bit-identical** — full SSP245 1750–2100 output matches `main` byte-for-byte; full suite (113 tests) passes.

Three commits:

1. **Cache `df_gas` column lookups in the concentrations/emissions hot path** — precompute per-gas scalar parameters (alpha, tau, beta, natural-emission terms, etc.) into arrays/dicts instead of re-reading DataFrame cells each year.
2. **Use numpy emission arrays in the hot path + prebuild aerosol reference map** — emissions and reference-species lookups served from contiguous numpy arrays indexed by `yr - yr0`.
3. **Cache solar/volcanic/LUC forcing as numpy arrays in the driver loop** — `ciceroscm.py` `_run` and `add_year_data_to_output` read cached arrays instead of `.iloc` into the source DataFrames (DataFrames retained for the `rf_run` path).

## Measured impact (SSP245 → 2100, `_run` wall-clock, 5 runs)

| Step | `_run` mean | Δ |
|---|---|---|
| before this PR | 1.450s | — |
| cache df_gas lookups | 1.340s* | — |
| numpy emission arrays | 1.016s | −0.211s |
| cache forcing arrays | 0.889s | −0.127s |

(\*measured in the full speedup chain after an unrelated thermal commit; the three changes here account for ~0.45s / ~31% of baseline run time.)

- [x] `pytest` full suite — 113 passed
- [x] Bit-identical output vs `main` (all 7 SSP245 output files, byte-compared)
- [ ] Reviewer check that the cached arrays stay aligned with `years[0]` for non-default `nystart`/`nyend`

body:
Adds the first periodic deterministic integer wave basis.

Release claim:
- BOGVM can synthesize periodic wave-like byte fields from compact integer parameters.
- DECLARE_BASIS triangle_u8 declares a fixed integer triangle oscillator.
- LOAD_COEFFICIENTS stores start byte and length.
- SYNTHESIZE reconstructs bytes using byte[i] = (start + offsets[i mod 8]) mod 256.
- VERIFY_HASH gates reconstructed data.
- ACCEPT_DATA only accepts after hash verification.
- Bad hash paths emit blocked receipts.

- python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -q

author: quanticsoul4772
body:
## Why

The convergence signal (#75) handed callers a `converged` bool computed from two hand-picked cutoffs (0.9 best-value, 0.2 UCB1 gap) with no way to see or override them. An agent could over-trust an opaque verdict driven by magic numbers. The retrospective flagged these thresholds as silently load-bearing.

## What

Make the heuristic **transparent rather than authoritative**:
- Return the cutoffs that produced the verdict — `dominance_gap_threshold` and `high_value_threshold` — so a caller now has `top_gap`, `best_value`, **and** the thresholds, and can recompute the verdict or apply its own tolerance.
- Each `reason` cites the value against its threshold (e.g. *"top candidate leads the runner-up by 0.53 UCB1 (>= 0.20 threshold)"*) instead of issuing a bare *"commit"*.
- Re-document `converged` as an advisory default, not a directive.

The bool's value is unchanged; this reframes it as one signal alongside the raw evidence already returned, so the hand-picked numbers aren't silently load-bearing.

## Tests
- New unit test asserts the thresholds are surfaced, cited in the reason, and that the raw evidence (`top_gap`/`best_value`) needed to override the bool is present.
- Existing convergence unit + wiremock assertions (reason substrings) unchanged.

## Validation
- `cargo fmt --check` ✓ · `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` ✓
- `cargo test` — 2609 unit + 143 integration + 21 doctests, 0 failed ✓
- `cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 95` ✓

## How it was chosen

`reasoning_decision` ranked this #1 of the five retrospective follow-ups. (Noted for the record: that same run ranked grounded rewards last and scored a threshold tweak above the one architectural change — the effort-bias the retro's `reasoning_detect` pass flagged. This PR follows the tool's pick; the larger items — de-risking the verification false-positives, and grounded rewards — remain the higher-ceiling work.)

💡 What: Replaced `Promise.all` with `c.env.DB.batch()` in the `GET /api/tasks/history` endpoint in `src/routes/tasks.ts`.

🎯 Why: In Cloudflare D1, using `Promise.all` for parallel database queries results in per-query HTTP network overhead. Grouping queries with `db.batch()` sends them in a single HTTP request, significantly reducing overall network latency.

📊 Impact: Eliminates one HTTP roundtrip to the database per request to the tasks history endpoint, improving response time and reducing network overhead for this route.

💡 **What**: Added composite database indexes `idx_logs_client_issues_composite` and `idx_memory_quarantine_composite` on `(client_id, tenant, project_id, status)` for the `logs_client_issues` and `memory_quarantine` tables.

author: captheavenger
body:
## Fix the 6 duplicate tutorial shots

Workflow produced 16 multi-shots but **6 were byte-identical** (md5 confirmed). Per-feature banners would show the same image twice or display the wrong feature.

### Two root causes

**1. Four profile-sub-tab hashes weren't routed.**
`metabinder`, `custombinder`, `testinggroups`, `wishlist`, `collection` weren't in `HASH_ALIASES` at all → `applyHash()` bailed → page landed on whichever profile sub-tab was default (Collection). All four screenshots ended up showing the same empty Collection view.

Fixed by adding aliases to both `HASH_ALIASES` (token → `'profile'`) and `PROFILE_SUBTAB_FOR_HASH` (token → sub-tab id) for: `metabinder`, `meta-binder`, `custombinder`, `custom-binder`, `testinggroups`, `testing-groups`, `wishlist`, `collection`. Same routing path the Telegram bot deep-links use, so future bot commands can land on these sub-tabs too.

**2. Meta Call shots taken before predictor finished.**
`1-field.png` and `2-recs.png` were taken with a 0 ms wait after hash navigation, so `MetaCall.init()` hadn't loaded data — both shots captured the empty loading state.

Fixed by:
- 3500 ms wait after hash navigation to let the predictor pipeline complete (CSV loads + P 4.6/5.6/5.7 + panel render)
- `2-recs.png` now waits for `.mc-rec-panel` selector BEFORE scrolling, then `scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })` − 20 px so the panel title is the focal point

### Re-trigger
Once this lands, run **Tutorial Screenshots** workflow again. The 6 duplicates should diverge:
- `meta-call/1-field.png` ≠ `meta-call/2-recs.png` (different scroll position, same dashboard)

author: dnikolaev-amd
body:
Opaque types live in a global registry for the whole process. The registered name is the class's fully qualified name: 
`name = f"{cls.__module__}.{cls.__qualname__}"`

`test_opaque_obj` defines a nested `MyInput`, so every invocation registers the same name as `test_export.TestExport.test_opaque_obj.<locals>.MyInput`. 

Test generators reuse that body under different method names. The second run fails with:
`Type '...MyInput' is already registered as an opaque type`

Unregister the opaque type using `self.addCleanup` lambda so each test run cleans up the registries before the next variant runs.
Cleanup restores _OPAQUE_TYPES_BY_NAME, not _OPAQUE_TYPES same as test_opaque_obj_v2

Fixes https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/170302 
Fixes https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/170449

Bootstraps this repo's agent context (Mode B of the import workflow) by vendoring a coherent module set from [agentic_optimization_research](https://github.com/ChrisKornaros/agentic_optimization_research) at source commit `79764aa`, and wiring `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/settings.json` around them. | Module | Type | Why |
|---|---|---|

The pre-existing uncommitted `docs/` changes (in-progress generated output) were left untouched — they're not part of this bootstrap.

author: bdelanghe
body:
## Problem (prx-hz1)

Every headless agent (`prx triage|intake|submit|author agent`, GH-2380's headless-first default) was dispatched with `--permission-mode plan`. Plan mode produces a plan and then **blocks on ExitPlanMode approval** — which a headless run has no operator to give. So it launched a real `claude --permission-mode plan` child, blocked the main thread on `kevent`, emitted nothing, never timed out, and leaked the child on parent kill. The whole "headless-first" path never actually terminated.

## Fix (core layer — no CLI logic added)

- **`machine/runtime_profiles.ts`** — the shared headless SDK builder (`buildSessionProfileSdkRuntimeProfile`, feeding triage/intake/submit/author) now sets `permissionMode: "acceptEdits"` instead of `"plan"`. The run proceeds autonomously and terminates; the allow/deny lists (unchanged) + the policy gate remain the authority boundary, mirroring the implement headless posture. The plan-**generator** profile (`prx plan session`, `--print` one-shot artifact) intentionally keeps plan mode and is left untouched (follow-up filed).
- **`pr-state/executor.ts`** — the SDK path no longer treats `timeoutMs: undefined` as "no watchdog" (spike §3.2's footgun); it falls back to `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_AGENT_WATCHDOG_MS` (15m). "A headless run never hangs forever" is now a core invariant. Explicit `timeoutMs` still wins.

## Verification

- typecheck clean; **700 pass / 0 fail** across profile/session/executor/cli suites
- **LIVE**: headless triage against the rebuilt binary exits **0 in ~2m16s with no leaked claude child** (was: infinite hang)
- intake headless profile confirmed `acceptEdits` via dry-run (no live mutation)

## PR checklist

1. [x] **Independent PR** — only the prx-hz1 headless permission-mode + watchdog fix
2. [x] **Changed codepaths verified** — live headless triage run + 700 unit tests
3. [x] **Root cause identified** — `permissionMode: "plan"` on headless SDK profiles (no approver) + no SDK watchdog default
4. [x] **No duplication** — single shared builder fixed; 6 test assertions flipped in lockstep
5. [x] **No unrelated changes** — N/A
